title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
intro_en: Swept far from her Kansas home by a cyclone, a young girl named Dorothy lands in the magical Land of Oz. To find her way back, she follows a road of yellow brick toward the Emerald City, making three unlikely friends along the way — a Scarecrow who wants a brain, a Tin Woodman who longs for a heart, and a Lion in search of courage.
intro_zh: 一场龙卷风把堪萨斯的小女孩多萝西卷到了神奇的奥兹国。为了回家,她沿着黄砖路走向翡翠城,一路上结识了三位奇特的朋友——想要脑子的稻草人、渴望一颗心的铁皮人,以及寻找勇气的狮子。
copyright_note: Public domain (first published 1900). Source: Project Gutenberg eBook #55. 公有领域(1900 年首版);正文取自 Project Gutenberg #55,面向学习者的分句/翻译加工。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy lived in the midst of the great Kansas prairies, with Uncle Henry, who was a farmer, and Aunt Em, who was the farmer’s wife.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西和亨利叔叔、艾姆婶婶住在一起。亨利叔叔是农民，艾姆婶婶是农民的妻子。他们住在大大的堪萨斯草原中间。

paragraphs.en: Their house was small, for the lumber to build it had to be carried by wagon many miles.
paragraphs.cn: 他们的房子很小，因为盖房子的木头要用马车运很远的路。

paragraphs.en: There were four walls, a floor and a roof, which made one room; and this room contained a rusty looking cookstove, a cupboard for the dishes, a table, three or four chairs, and the beds.
paragraphs.cn: 房子有四面墙、一个地板和一个屋顶，只有一个房间。这个房间里有一个旧旧的炉子、一个放碗碟的柜子、一张桌子、三四把椅子和几张床。

paragraphs.en: Uncle Henry and Aunt Em had a big bed in one corner, and Dorothy a little bed in another corner.
paragraphs.cn: 亨利叔叔和艾姆婶婶有一个大床在屋子的一角，多萝西有一个小床在另一个角。

paragraphs.en: There was no garret at all, and no cellar—except a small hole dug in the ground, called a cyclone cellar, where the family could go in case one of those great whirlwinds arose, mighty enough to crush any building in its path.
paragraphs.cn: 家里没有阁楼，也没有地窖。只有一个小小的洞，挖在地上，大家叫它‘龙卷风地窖’。要是来了大大的龙卷风，能把房子都刮倒，他们就躲到里面去。

paragraphs.en: It was reached by a trap door in the middle of the floor, from which a ladder led down into the small, dark hole.
paragraphs.cn: 从地板中间的一个暗门进去，有一架梯子通到那个又小又黑的洞里。

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy stood in the doorway and looked around, she could see nothing but the great gray prairie on every side.
paragraphs.cn: 当多萝西站在门边向四周看时，她只能看到一片大大的灰色草原，什么都没有。

paragraphs.en: Not a tree nor a house broke the broad sweep of flat country that reached to the edge of the sky in all directions.
paragraphs.cn: 没有一棵树，也没有一座房子，只有平坦的土地一直延伸到天边。

paragraphs.en: The sun had baked the plowed land into a gray mass, with little cracks running through it.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳把耕过的地晒得硬邦邦的，变成一片灰蒙蒙的，上面还有一些小裂缝。

paragraphs.en: Even the grass was not green, for the sun had burned the tops of the long blades until they were the same gray color to be seen everywhere.
paragraphs.cn: 连草都不是绿色的，太阳把长长的草尖都晒黄了，到处都是一样的灰色。

paragraphs.en: Once the house had been painted, but the sun blistered the paint and the rains washed it away, and now the house was as dull and gray as everything else.
paragraphs.cn: 房子以前漆过油漆，但是太阳把油漆晒得起了泡，雨水又把油漆冲掉了。现在房子也变得和周围的一切一样，又暗又灰。

paragraphs.en: When Aunt Em came there to live she was a young, pretty wife.
paragraphs.cn: 艾姆婶婶刚来这里住的时候，她是一个年轻又漂亮的妻子。

paragraphs.en: The sun and wind had changed her, too.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳和风也改变了她。

paragraphs.en: They had taken the sparkle from her eyes and left them a sober gray; they had taken the red from her cheeks and lips, and they were gray also.
paragraphs.cn: 她的眼睛不再闪亮，变得灰蒙蒙的；她的脸颊和嘴唇也没有了红色，也变成了灰色。

paragraphs.en: She was thin and gaunt, and never smiled now.
paragraphs.cn: 她又瘦又憔悴，现在从不笑了。

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy, who was an orphan, first came to her, Aunt Em had been so startled by the child’s laughter that she would scream and press her hand upon her heart whenever Dorothy’s merry voice reached her ears; and she still looked at the little girl with wonder that she could find anything to laugh at.
paragraphs.cn: 当多萝西（她是一个孤儿）刚来到她身边时，艾姆婶婶听到孩子笑声时吓了一跳，每次多萝西开心笑出声，她都会尖叫，捂住自己的心口。她还是会好奇地看着这个小女孩，想不通她有什么好笑的。

paragraphs.en: Uncle Henry never laughed.
paragraphs.cn: 亨利叔叔从不笑。

paragraphs.en: He worked hard from morning till night and did not know what joy was.
paragraphs.cn: 他从早到晚努力干活，不知道什么叫快乐。

paragraphs.en: He was gray also, from his long beard to his rough boots, and he looked stern and solemn, and rarely spoke.
paragraphs.cn: 他也是灰色的，从长长的胡子到粗糙的靴子。他看起来很严肃，不苟言笑，也很少说话。

paragraphs.en: It was Toto that made Dorothy laugh, and saved her from growing as gray as her other surroundings.
paragraphs.cn: 是托托让多萝西开心地笑了，也让她没有变得像周围环境一样灰暗。

paragraphs.en: Toto was not gray; he was a little black dog, with long silky hair and small black eyes that twinkled merrily on either side of his funny, wee nose.
paragraphs.cn: 托托不是灰色的；它是一只小黑狗，有着长长的丝滑毛发，还有两只小小的黑眼睛，在它滑稽的小鼻子的两边，闪着开心的光。

paragraphs.en: Toto played all day long, and Dorothy played with him, and loved him dearly.
paragraphs.cn: 托托整天都在玩耍，多萝西和它一起玩，而且非常爱它。

paragraphs.en: Today, however, they were not playing.
paragraphs.cn: 但是今天，他们没有玩耍。

paragraphs.en: Uncle Henry sat upon the doorstep and looked anxiously at the sky, which was even grayer than usual.
paragraphs.cn: 亨利叔叔坐在门槛上，焦急地看着天空，天空比平时更灰暗了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy stood in the door with Toto in her arms, and looked at the sky too.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西抱着托托站在门口，也看着天空。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Em was washing the dishes.
paragraphs.cn: 艾姆婶婶正在洗碗。

paragraphs.en: From the far north they heard a low wail of the wind, and Uncle Henry and Dorothy could see where the long grass bowed in waves before the coming storm.
paragraphs.cn: 他们从很远的北方听到风呜咽的声音，亨利叔叔和多萝西能看到长长的草被风吹得像波浪一样弯下腰，暴风雨要来了。

paragraphs.en: There now came a sharp whistling in the air from the south, and as they turned their eyes that way they saw ripples in the grass coming from that direction also.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，南方传来一阵尖锐的呼啸声，他们朝那个方向看去，看到草地上也出现了波浪，从那边涌过来。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly Uncle Henry stood up.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，亨利叔叔站了起来。

paragraphs.en: “There’s a cyclone coming, Em,” he called to his wife.
paragraphs.cn: “龙卷风要来了，艾姆！”他对妻子喊道。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll go look after the stock.”
paragraphs.cn: “我去看看牲口。”

paragraphs.en: Then he ran toward the sheds where the cows and horses were kept.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他跑向牛棚，那里养着奶牛和马。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Em dropped her work and came to the door.
paragraphs.cn: 艾姆婶婶放下手里的活儿，走到门口。

paragraphs.en: One glance told her of the danger close at hand.
paragraphs.cn: 她看了一眼，就知道危险就在眼前。

paragraphs.en: “Quick, Dorothy!” she screamed. “Run for the cellar!”
paragraphs.cn: “快，多萝西！”她大叫。“快跑去地窖！”

paragraphs.en: Toto jumped out of Dorothy’s arms and hid under the bed, and the girl started to get him.
paragraphs.cn: 托托从多萝西的怀里跳出来，躲到床底下，小女孩便去抓它。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Em, badly frightened, threw open the trap door in the floor and climbed down the ladder into the small, dark hole.
paragraphs.cn: 艾姆婶婶吓坏了，她打开地板上的活板门，顺着梯子爬进那个又小又黑的洞里。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy caught Toto at last and started to follow her aunt.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西终于抓住了托托，然后跟着婶婶走。

paragraphs.en: When she was halfway across the room there came a great shriek from the wind, and the house shook so hard that she lost her footing and sat down suddenly upon the floor.
paragraphs.cn: 当她走到房间一半的时候，风发出了一声巨大的尖叫，房子摇晃得太厉害，她站不稳，一下子就坐在了地上。

paragraphs.en: Then a strange thing happened.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，一件奇怪的事情发生了。

paragraphs.en: The house whirled around two or three times and rose slowly through the air.
paragraphs.cn: 房子转了两三圈，然后慢慢地升到空中。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy felt as if she were going up in a balloon.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西感觉自己好像坐着气球飞起来了。

paragraphs.en: The north and south winds met where the house stood, and made it the exact center of the cyclone.
paragraphs.cn: 北风和南风在房子所在的地方相遇，让房子正好在龙卷风的中心。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of a cyclone the air is generally still, but the great pressure of the wind on every side of the house raised it up higher and higher, until it was at the very top of the cyclone; and there it remained and was carried miles and miles away as easily as you could carry a feather.
paragraphs.cn: 龙卷风的中心通常是平静的，但风从四面八方给房子巨大的压力，把房子抬得越来越高，直到它到了龙卷风的最顶端；房子就留在那里，被带走了很远很远，就像你拿起一片羽毛一样轻松。

paragraphs.en: It was very dark, and the wind howled horribly around her, but Dorothy found she was riding quite easily.
paragraphs.cn: 外面很黑，风在她身边可怕地呼啸着，但多萝西发现自己坐得很稳。

paragraphs.en: After the first few whirls around, and one other time when the house tipped badly, she felt as if she were being rocked gently, like a baby in a cradle.
paragraphs.cn: 房子最开始转了几圈，后来有一次还剧烈倾斜了一下，但过了这些之后，她感觉自己被轻轻地摇晃着，就像摇篮里的宝宝一样。

paragraphs.en: Toto did not like it.
paragraphs.cn: 托托不喜欢这样。

paragraphs.en: He ran about the room, now here, now there, barking loudly; but Dorothy sat quite still on the floor and waited to see what would happen.
paragraphs.cn: 他在房间里跑来跑去，一会儿跑这儿，一会儿跑那儿，大声地叫着；但多萝西安静地坐在地板上，等着看会发生什么。

paragraphs.en: Once Toto got too near the open trap door, and fell in; and at first the little girl thought she had lost him.
paragraphs.cn: 有一次，托托离打开的活板门太近，掉了进去；小女孩一开始以为把它弄丢了。

paragraphs.en: But soon she saw one of his ears sticking up through the hole, for the strong pressure of the air was keeping him up so that he could not fall.
paragraphs.cn: 但很快她就看到他的一只耳朵从洞里伸出来，因为空气强大的压力托住了他，所以他没有掉下去。

paragraphs.en: She crept to the hole, caught Toto by the ear, and dragged him into the room again, afterward closing the trap door so that no more accidents could happen.
paragraphs.cn: 她悄悄走到洞口，抓住托托的耳朵，把他拖回房间，然后关上活板门，这样就不会再发生意外了。

paragraphs.en: Hour after hour passed away, and slowly Dorothy got over her fright; but she felt quite lonely, and the wind shrieked so loudly all about her that she nearly became deaf.
paragraphs.cn: 一个小时又一个小时过去了，多萝西慢慢地不再那么害怕了；但她感觉很孤单，风在她身边大声呼啸，她差点被震聋了。

paragraphs.en: At first she had wondered if she would be dashed to pieces when the house fell again; but as the hours passed and nothing terrible happened, she stopped worrying and resolved to wait calmly and see what the future would bring.
paragraphs.cn: 一开始她担心房子再掉下去的时候，自己会不会摔得粉碎；但随着时间过去，什么可怕的事情都没发生，她就不再担心了，决定平静地等待，看看未来会怎样。

paragraphs.en: At last she crawled over the swaying floor to her bed, and lay down upon it; and Toto followed and lay down beside her.
paragraphs.cn: 最后她爬过摇晃的地板到她的床上，躺了上去；托托也跟着过来，躺在她身边。

paragraphs.en: In spite of the swaying of the house and the wailing of the wind, Dorothy soon closed her eyes and fell fast asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管房子还在摇晃，风还在呼啸，多萝西很快就闭上眼睛，睡着了。

paragraphs.en: She was awakened by a shock, so sudden and severe that if Dorothy had not been lying on the soft bed she might have been hurt.
paragraphs.cn: 她被一阵冲击惊醒了，那冲击又突然又猛烈，如果多萝西没有躺在柔软的床上，她可能就受伤了。

paragraphs.en: As it was, the jar made her catch her breath and wonder what had happened; and Toto put his cold little nose into her face and whined dismally.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管如此，这一震还是让她倒吸一口气，想知道发生了什么；托托把冰冷的小鼻子伸到她脸上，可怜地呜咽着。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy sat up and noticed that the house was not moving; nor was it dark, for the bright sunshine came in at the window, flooding the little room.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西坐起来，发现房子不动了；也不再黑暗了，因为明亮的阳光从窗户照进来，洒满了整个小房间。

paragraphs.en: She sprang from her bed and with Toto at her heels ran and opened the door.
paragraphs.cn: 她从床上跳起来，托托跟在她身后，她跑过去打开了门。

paragraphs.en: The little girl gave a cry of amazement and looked about her, her eyes growing bigger and bigger at the wonderful sights she saw.
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩惊奇地叫了一声，环顾四周，她看到的奇妙景象让她眼睛越睁越大。

paragraphs.en: The cyclone had set the house down very gently—for a cyclone—in the midst of a country of marvelous beauty.
paragraphs.cn: 龙卷风把房子轻轻地放了下来，在一个很美的地方。

paragraphs.en: There were lovely patches of greensward all about, with stately trees bearing rich and luscious fruits.
paragraphs.cn: 周围有绿绿的草地，还有高大的树，上面结满了好吃的水果。

paragraphs.en: Banks of gorgeous flowers were on every hand, and birds with rare and brilliant plumage sang and fluttered in the trees and bushes.
paragraphs.cn: 四处都是漂亮的花，还有穿着漂亮羽毛的鸟儿在树丛里唱歌、飞舞。

paragraphs.en: A little way off was a small brook, rushing and sparkling along between green banks, and murmuring in a voice very grateful to a little girl who had lived so long on the dry, gray prairies.
paragraphs.cn: 不远处有条小溪，水哗啦啦地流着，在绿色的岸边闪闪发光。对于一个一直住在干旱草原上的小女孩来说，这声音听起来很舒服。

paragraphs.en: While she stood looking eagerly at the strange and beautiful sights, she noticed coming toward her a group of the queerest people she had ever seen.
paragraphs.cn: 她好奇地看着这些又奇怪又美丽的地方时，看到一群她从没见过的人朝她走来。

paragraphs.en: They were not as big as the grown folk she had always been used to; but neither were they very small.
paragraphs.cn: 他们不像她平时见的大人那么高，但也不是很矮。

paragraphs.en: In fact, they seemed about as tall as Dorothy, who was a well-grown child for her age, although they were, so far as looks go, many years older.
paragraphs.cn: 他们看起来跟多萝西差不多高，多萝西在同龄孩子里算长得挺好的。不过，他们看起来比多萝西大很多岁。

paragraphs.en: Three were men and one a woman, and all were oddly dressed.
paragraphs.cn: 他们有三男一女，穿的衣服都很特别。

paragraphs.en: They wore round hats that rose to a small point a foot above their heads, with little bells around the brims that tinkled sweetly as they moved.
paragraphs.cn: 他们戴着圆帽子，帽子顶上尖尖的，比头高一尺。帽子边上还有小铃铛，他们一动就发出好听的叮当声。

paragraphs.en: The hats of the men were blue; the little woman’s hat was white, and she wore a white gown that hung in pleats from her shoulders.
paragraphs.cn: 男士们的帽子是蓝色的；小妇人的帽子是白色的，她穿着一件白色的连衣裙，从肩膀垂下来有许多褶子。

paragraphs.en: Over it were sprinkled little stars that glistened in the sun like diamonds.
paragraphs.cn: 连衣裙上洒满了小星星，在阳光下像钻石一样闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: The men were dressed in blue, of the same shade as their hats, and wore well-polished boots with a deep roll of blue at the tops.
paragraphs.cn: 男士们穿着蓝色的衣服，和帽子是同样的颜色，还穿着擦得亮亮的靴子，靴子顶部有一圈深蓝色。

paragraphs.en: The men, Dorothy thought, were about as old as Uncle Henry, for two of them had beards.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西觉得，男士们看起来跟亨利叔叔差不多大，因为他们中有两个人留着胡子。

paragraphs.en: But the little woman was doubtless much older.
paragraphs.cn: 但那个小妇人肯定大多了。

paragraphs.en: Her face was covered with wrinkles, her hair was nearly white, and she walked rather stiffly.
paragraphs.cn: 她的脸上都是皱纹，头发几乎全白了，走路也有些僵硬。

paragraphs.en: When these people drew near the house where Dorothy was standing in the doorway, they paused and whispered among themselves, as if afraid to come farther.
paragraphs.cn: 当这些人走到多萝西站在门口的房子附近时，他们停了下来，互相小声说话，好像不敢再往前走了。

paragraphs.en: But the little old woman walked up to Dorothy, made a low bow and said, in a sweet voice:
paragraphs.cn: 但那个小老妇人走到多萝西面前，深深地鞠了一躬，然后用甜甜的声音说：

paragraphs.en: “You are welcome, most noble Sorceress, to the land of the Munchkins.
paragraphs.cn: “最尊贵的魔法师，欢迎你来到芒奇金人的土地。”

paragraphs.en: We are so grateful to you for having killed the Wicked Witch of the East, and for setting our people free from bondage.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们非常感谢你杀了那个东方坏女巫，把我们的人民从苦难中解救出来。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy listened to this speech with wonder.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西听着这些话，感到很惊讶。

paragraphs.en: What could the little woman possibly mean by calling her a sorceress, and saying she had killed the Wicked Witch of the East?
paragraphs.cn: 这个小妇人叫她魔法师，还说她杀了那个东方坏女巫，到底是什么意思呢？

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was an innocent, harmless little girl, who had been carried by a cyclone many miles from home; and she had never killed anything in all her life.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西只是一个天真无害的小女孩，她被龙卷风从家里卷到了很远的地方。她这辈子从来没杀过任何东西。

paragraphs.en: But the little woman evidently expected her to answer; so Dorothy said, with hesitation, “You are very kind, but there must be some mistake.
paragraphs.cn: 但那个小妇人显然在等她回答，所以多萝西有些迟疑地说：“你人很好，但这一定弄错了。

paragraphs.en: I have not killed anything.”
paragraphs.cn: 我没有杀过任何东西。”

paragraphs.en: “Your house did, anyway,” replied the little old woman, with a laugh, “and that is the same thing.
paragraphs.cn: “反正你的房子做到了！”小老妇人笑着回答，“那是一样的。”

paragraphs.en: See!” she continued, pointing to the corner of the house. “There are her two feet, still sticking out from under a block of wood.”
paragraphs.cn: “看！”她接着说，指着房子的角落，“她的两只脚还在那块木头下面露出来呢。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy looked, and gave a little cry of fright.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西看了一眼，吓得小声叫了起来。

paragraphs.en: There, indeed, just under the corner of the great beam the house rested on, two feet were sticking out, shod in silver shoes with pointed toes.
paragraphs.cn: 果然，就在房子下面那根大梁的角落里，有两只脚伸了出来，脚上穿着银色的尖头鞋。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, dear!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！

paragraphs.en: Oh, dear!” cried Dorothy, clasping her hands together in dismay.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀！”多萝西沮丧地把手合在一起，叫道。

paragraphs.en: “The house must have fallen on her.
paragraphs.cn: “房子一定砸到她了。

paragraphs.en: Whatever shall we do?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们该怎么办呀？”

paragraphs.en: “There is nothing to be done,” said the little woman calmly.
paragraphs.cn: “没办法了，”小个子女人平静地说。

paragraphs.en: “But who was she?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “可是她是谁呀？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “She was the Wicked Witch of the East, as I said,” answered the little woman.
paragraphs.cn: “她就是东方坏女巫，我刚才说了，”小个子女人回答。

paragraphs.en: “She has held all the Munchkins in bondage for many years, making them slave for her night and day.
paragraphs.cn: “她把所有的芒奇金人都抓起来好多年了，让他们白天晚上都给她干活。

paragraphs.en: Now they are all set free, and are grateful to you for the favor.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在他们都自由了，很感谢你帮的忙。”

paragraphs.en: “Who are the Munchkins?” inquired Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “芒奇金人是谁呀？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “They are the people who live in this land of the East where the Wicked Witch ruled.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们是住在东方的人，坏女巫以前管着这里。”

paragraphs.en: “Are you a Munchkin?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “你是个芒奇金人吗？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “No, but I am their friend, although I live in the land of the North.
paragraphs.cn: “不是，我是他们的朋友，虽然我住在北方。

paragraphs.en: When they saw the Witch of the East was dead the Munchkins sent a swift messenger to me, and I came at once.
paragraphs.cn: 他们看到东方女巫死了，芒奇金人就马上派人告诉我，我一下子就来了。

paragraphs.en: I am the Witch of the North.”
paragraphs.cn: 我就是北方好女巫。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, gracious!” cried Dorothy. “Are you a real witch?”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，天哪！”多萝西喊道，“你真的是女巫吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, indeed,” answered the little woman.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，”小个子女人回答。

paragraphs.en: “But I am a good witch, and the people love me.
paragraphs.cn: “不过我是个好女巫，大家都很喜欢我。

paragraphs.en: I am not as powerful as the Wicked Witch was who ruled here, or I should have set the people free myself.”
paragraphs.cn: 我没有以前管这里的坏女巫那么厉害，不然我早就自己把大家放出来了。”

paragraphs.en: “But I thought all witches were wicked,” said the girl, who was half frightened at facing a real witch.
paragraphs.cn: “可是我以为所有女巫都是坏的呢，”小女孩说，她看到真的女巫，有点害怕。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no, that is a great mistake.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不，你错了。

paragraphs.en: There were only four witches in all the Land of Oz, and two of them, those who live in the North and the South, are good witches.
paragraphs.cn: 整个奥兹国只有四个女巫，其中两个是好女巫，她们住在北方和南方。

paragraphs.en: I know this is true, for I am one of them myself, and cannot be mistaken.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道这是真的，因为我就是其中一个，我不会弄错的。

paragraphs.en: Those who dwelt in the East and the West were, indeed, wicked witches; but now that you have killed one of them, there is but one Wicked Witch in all the Land of Oz—the one who lives in the West.”
paragraphs.cn: 住在东方和西方的女巫确实是坏女巫；不过你已经杀了一个，整个奥兹国就只剩下一个坏女巫了——就是住在西方的那一个。”

paragraphs.en: “But,” said Dorothy, after a moment’s thought, “Aunt Em has told me that the witches were all dead—years and years ago.”
paragraphs.cn: “可是，”多萝西想了想说，“艾姆婶婶告诉我，女巫们早就死了——很久很久以前就死了。”

paragraphs.en: “Who is Aunt Em?” inquired the little old woman.
paragraphs.cn: “艾姆婶婶是谁呀？”小老太太问。

paragraphs.en: “She is my aunt who lives in Kansas, where I came from.”
paragraphs.cn: “她是我婶婶，住在堪萨斯，我就是从那里来的。”

paragraphs.en: The Witch of the North seemed to think for a time, with her head bowed and her eyes upon the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 北方好女巫低着头，眼睛看着地上，好像在想了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Then she looked up and said, “I do not know where Kansas is, for I have never heard that country mentioned before.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她抬起头说，“我不知道堪萨斯在哪里，因为我从来没听过这个地方。

paragraphs.en: But tell me, is it a civilized country?”
paragraphs.cn: 不过告诉我，那是个文明的地方吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes,” replied Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是的，”多萝西回答。

paragraphs.en: “Then that accounts for it.
paragraphs.cn: “那就对了。

paragraphs.en: In the civilized countries I believe there are no witches left, nor wizards, nor sorceresses, nor magicians.
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得在那些很棒的国家，已经没有女巫、男巫和魔法师了。

paragraphs.en: But, you see, the Land of Oz has never been civilized, for we are cut off from all the rest of the world.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，你看，这个奥兹国从来都不文明，因为我们跟外面的世界都分开了。

paragraphs.en: Therefore we still have witches and wizards amongst us.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以我们这里还有女巫和男巫。”

paragraphs.en: “Who are the wizards?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “谁是男巫啊？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “Oz himself is the Great Wizard,” answered the Witch, sinking her voice to a whisper.
paragraphs.cn: “奥兹大王自己就是最厉害的男巫，”女巫悄悄地说。

paragraphs.en: “He is more powerful than all the rest of us together.
paragraphs.cn: “他比我们所有人都厉害得多。

paragraphs.en: He lives in the City of Emeralds.”
paragraphs.cn: 他住在翡翠城里。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was going to ask another question, but just then the Munchkins, who had been standing silently by, gave a loud shout and pointed to the corner of the house where the Wicked Witch had been lying.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西刚想再问，可这时，一直没说话的芒奇金人突然大叫一声，指着屋角，那里就是坏女巫躺着的地方。

paragraphs.en: “What is it?” asked the little old woman, and looked, and began to laugh.
paragraphs.cn: “怎么啦？”小老太太问，她看了一眼，就哈哈笑起来。

paragraphs.en: The feet of the dead Witch had disappeared entirely, and nothing was left but the silver shoes.
paragraphs.cn: 死去的女巫的脚完全不见了，只剩下那双闪闪的银鞋子。

paragraphs.en: “She was so old,” explained the Witch of the North, “that she dried up quickly in the sun.
paragraphs.cn: “她太老啦，”北方好女巫说，“在太阳下一晒，就很快变干了。

paragraphs.en: That is the end of her.
paragraphs.cn: 她就这样不见了。

paragraphs.en: But the silver shoes are yours, and you shall have them to wear.”
paragraphs.cn: 但这双银鞋是你的，你可以穿上它。”

paragraphs.en: She reached down and picked up the shoes, and after shaking the dust out of them handed them to Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: 她弯腰捡起鞋子，抖掉上面的灰尘，递给多萝西。

paragraphs.en: “The Witch of the East was proud of those silver shoes,” said one of the Munchkins, “and there is some charm connected with them; but what it is we never knew.”
paragraphs.cn: “东方女巫很喜欢那双银鞋子，”一个芒奇金人说，“它们好像有魔法，可是我们从来都不知道那是什么魔法。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy carried the shoes into the house and placed them on the table.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西把鞋子拿进屋里，放在桌子上。

paragraphs.en: Then she came out again to the Munchkins and said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后她又出来对芒奇金人说：

paragraphs.en: “I am anxious to get back to my aunt and uncle, for I am sure they will worry about me.
paragraphs.cn: “我好想快点回到我的叔叔和婶婶身边，他们肯定很担心我。

paragraphs.en: Can you help me find my way?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们能帮我找到回家的路吗？”

paragraphs.en: The Munchkins and the Witch first looked at one another, and then at Dorothy, and then shook their heads.
paragraphs.cn: 芒奇金人和女巫先是互相看，又看看多萝西，最后都摇了摇头。

paragraphs.en: “At the East, not far from here,” said one, “there is a great desert, and none could live to cross it.”
paragraphs.cn: “在东方，离这里不远的地方，”一个人说，“有一片大沙漠，没有人能活着走过去。”

paragraphs.en: “It is the same at the South,” said another, “for I have been there and seen it.
paragraphs.cn: “南方也是这样，”另一个人说，“因为我去过那里，亲眼看到了。

paragraphs.en: The South is the country of the Quadlings.”
paragraphs.cn: 南方是奎德林人的国家。”

paragraphs.en: “I am told,” said the third man, “that it is the same at the West.
paragraphs.cn: “我听说，”第三个人说，“西方也是这样。

paragraphs.en: And that country, where the Winkies live, is ruled by the Wicked Witch of the West, who would make you her slave if you passed her way.”
paragraphs.cn: 那个国家，是温基人住的地方，由西方坏女巫来管，如果你从那里经过，她会让你变成她的仆人。”

paragraphs.en: “The North is my home,” said the old lady, “and at its edge is the same great desert that surrounds this Land of Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “北方是我的家，”老太太说，“北方边上也是一片大沙漠，它把这个奥兹国团团围住。

paragraphs.en: I’m afraid, my dear, you will have to live with us.”
paragraphs.cn: 亲爱的，看来你得跟我们一起住啦。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy began to sob at this, for she felt lonely among all these strange people.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西听了这话，就哭了起来，因为在这些陌生人中间，她感到孤零零的。

paragraphs.en: Her tears seemed to grieve the kind-hearted Munchkins, for they immediately took out their handkerchiefs and began to weep also.
paragraphs.cn: 她的眼泪好像让善良的芒奇金人也很难过，他们赶紧拿出自己的手帕，也跟着哭起来。

paragraphs.en: As for the little old woman, she took off her cap and balanced the point on the end of her nose, while she counted “One, two, three” in a solemn voice.
paragraphs.cn: 那个小老太太呢，她摘下帽子，把帽尖稳稳地放在鼻尖上，然后用很认真的声音数着“一、二、三”。

paragraphs.en: At once the cap changed to a slate, on which was written in big, white chalk marks:
paragraphs.cn: 帽子立刻变成一块石板，上面写着大大的白粉笔字：

paragraphs.en: “LET DOROTHY GO TO THE CITY OF EMERALDS”
paragraphs.cn: “让多萝西去翡翠城”

paragraphs.en: The little old woman took the slate from her nose, and having read the words on it, asked, “Is your name Dorothy, my dear?”
paragraphs.cn: 小老太太从鼻子上拿下石板，读了上面的字，问：“亲爱的，你叫多萝西吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” answered the child, looking up and drying her tears.
paragraphs.cn: “是的。”孩子抬起头，擦干眼泪回答。

paragraphs.en: “Then you must go to the City of Emeralds.
paragraphs.cn: “那你一定要去翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps Oz will help you.”
paragraphs.cn: 也许奥兹大王会帮你。”

paragraphs.en: “Where is this city?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “这个城市在哪里？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “It is exactly in the center of the country, and is ruled by Oz, the Great Wizard I told you of.”
paragraphs.cn: “它就在国家的正中间，由我跟你说过的大魔法师奥兹大王统治。”

paragraphs.en: “Is he a good man?” inquired the girl anxiously.
paragraphs.cn: “他是个好人吗？”女孩有点担心地问。

paragraphs.en: “He is a good Wizard.
paragraphs.cn: “他是个好魔法师。

paragraphs.en: Whether he is a man or not I cannot tell, for I have never seen him.”
paragraphs.cn: 他是不是人，我可不知道，因为我从没见过他。”

paragraphs.en: “How can I get there?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我怎么才能去那里呢？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “You must walk.
paragraphs.cn: “你必须走路去。

paragraphs.en: It is a long journey, through a country that is sometimes pleasant and sometimes dark and terrible.
paragraphs.cn: 那是一段很长的路，要经过有时很美、有时又很黑很可怕的地方。

paragraphs.en: However, I will use all the magic arts I know of to keep you from harm.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过，我会用我所有的魔法，让你不受伤害。”

paragraphs.en: “Won’t you go with me?” pleaded the girl, who had begun to look upon the little old woman as her only friend.
paragraphs.cn: “你不能和我一起去吗？”女孩恳求道，她已经把小老太太当成自己唯一的朋友了。

paragraphs.en: “No, I cannot do that,” she replied, “but I will give you my kiss, and no one will dare injure a person who has been kissed by the Witch of the North.”
paragraphs.cn: “不行，我不能那样做，”她回答，“但我会给你一个我的吻，被北方好女巫亲过的人，没人敢伤害她。”

paragraphs.en: She came close to Dorothy and kissed her gently on the forehead.
paragraphs.cn: 她走近多萝西，轻轻地亲了亲她的额头。

paragraphs.en: Where her lips touched the girl they left a round, shining mark, as Dorothy found out soon after.
paragraphs.cn: 她的嘴唇碰到女孩的地方，留下了一个圆圆的闪亮印记，多萝西很快就发现了。

paragraphs.en: “The road to the City of Emeralds is paved with yellow brick,” said the Witch, “so you cannot miss it.
paragraphs.cn: “去翡翠城的路是用黄砖铺成的，”女巫说，“所以你不会迷路。

paragraphs.en: When you get to Oz do not be afraid of him, but tell your story and ask him to help you.
paragraphs.cn: 等你到了奥兹大王那里，不要害怕他，要告诉他你的故事，请他帮助你。

paragraphs.en: Good-bye, my dear.”
paragraphs.cn: 再见，亲爱的。”

paragraphs.en: The three Munchkins bowed low to her and wished her a pleasant journey, after which they walked away through the trees.
paragraphs.cn: 三个芒奇金人向她深深地鞠了一躬，祝她旅途愉快，然后穿过树林走开了。

paragraphs.en: The Witch gave Dorothy a friendly little nod, whirled around on her left heel three times, and straightway disappeared, much to the surprise of little Toto, who barked after her loudly enough when she had gone, because he had been afraid even to growl while she stood by.
paragraphs.cn: 女巫朝多萝西友善地点了点头，然后左脚跟转了三圈，立刻就消失了，这让小托托很惊讶，她在女巫走后大声地叫了起来，因为女巫在旁边的时候，它连哼一声都不敢。

paragraphs.en: But Dorothy, knowing her to be a witch, had expected her to disappear in just that way, and was not surprised in the least.
paragraphs.cn: 但是多萝西知道她是个女巫，所以她早就料到女巫会那样消失，一点也不惊讶。

chapters.title_zh: 多萝西如何拯救稻草人

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy was left alone she began to feel hungry.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西一个人待着的时候，她开始感到饿了。

paragraphs.en: So she went to the cupboard and cut herself some bread, which she spread with butter.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她走到碗柜前，切了些面包，又涂上黄油。

paragraphs.en: She gave some to Toto, and taking a pail from the shelf she carried it down to the little brook and filled it with clear, sparkling water.
paragraphs.cn: 她分了些给托托，然后从架子上拿了一个水桶，提到小溪边，装满了清澈闪亮的水。

paragraphs.en: Toto ran over to the trees and began to bark at the birds sitting there.
paragraphs.cn: 托托跑到树林那边，开始对着停在那里的鸟儿叫。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy went to get him, and saw such delicious fruit hanging from the branches that she gathered some of it, finding it just what she wanted to help out her breakfast.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西去叫它回来，看到了树枝上挂着好多好吃的水果，于是她摘了一些，发现这正是她早餐想吃的。

paragraphs.en: Then she went back to the house, and having helped herself and Toto to a good drink of the cool, clear water, she set about making ready for the journey to the City of Emeralds.
paragraphs.cn: 她回到屋里，给自己和托托倒了一大杯清凉的水。喝完水，她就开始准备去翡翠城了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy had only one other dress, but that happened to be clean and was hanging on a peg beside her bed.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西只有一条裙子，不过它很干净，正挂在床边的钩子上。

paragraphs.en: It was gingham, with checks of white and blue; and although the blue was somewhat faded with many washings, it was still a pretty frock.
paragraphs.cn: 这条裙子是方格布做的，有白色和蓝色格子。虽然蓝色洗得有点旧了，但它还是很好看。

paragraphs.en: The girl washed herself carefully, dressed herself in the clean gingham, and tied her pink sunbonnet on her head.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩仔细洗了洗，穿上干净的方格裙，再戴上她的粉色遮阳帽。

paragraphs.en: She took a little basket and filled it with bread from the cupboard, laying a white cloth over the top.
paragraphs.cn: 她拿了一个小篮子，从柜子里拿出面包放进去，然后盖上一块白布。

paragraphs.en: Then she looked down at her feet and noticed how old and worn her shoes were.
paragraphs.cn: 她低头看了看自己的脚，发现鞋子又旧又破了。

paragraphs.en: “They surely will never do for a long journey, Toto,” she said.
paragraphs.cn: “这些鞋子肯定不能穿去长途旅行，托托，”她说道。

paragraphs.en: And Toto looked up into her face with his little black eyes and wagged his tail to show he knew what she meant.
paragraphs.cn: 托托用它的小黑眼睛看着她，摇了摇尾巴，表示它懂她的意思。

paragraphs.en: At that moment Dorothy saw lying on the table the silver shoes that had belonged to the Witch of the East.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，多萝西看到桌上放着一双银鞋，那是东方女巫的。

paragraphs.en: “I wonder if they will fit me,” she said to Toto.
paragraphs.cn: “不知道它们合不合我的脚？”她对托托说。

paragraphs.en: “They would be just the thing to take a long walk in, for they could not wear out.”
paragraphs.cn: “穿着它们走远路最好不过了，因为它们不会穿坏。”

paragraphs.en: She took off her old leather shoes and tried on the silver ones, which fitted her as well as if they had been made for her.
paragraphs.cn: 她脱掉旧皮鞋，穿上银鞋。银鞋穿在她脚上，就像是专门为她做的一样合脚。

paragraphs.en: Finally she picked up her basket.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，她拿起她的篮子。

paragraphs.en: “Come along, Toto,” she said.
paragraphs.cn: “来吧，托托，”她说道。

paragraphs.en: “We will go to the Emerald City and ask the Great Oz how to get back to Kansas again.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们去翡翠城，问问伟大的奥兹大王怎么才能回到堪萨斯。”

paragraphs.en: She closed the door, locked it, and put the key carefully in the pocket of her dress.
paragraphs.cn: 她关上门，锁好，然后小心地把钥匙放进裙子的口袋里。

paragraphs.en: And so, with Toto trotting along soberly behind her, she started on her journey.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，托托在她身后稳稳地小跑着，她开始了旅程。

paragraphs.en: There were several roads nearby, but it did not take her long to find the one paved with yellow bricks.
paragraphs.cn: 附近有几条路，但她很快就找到了那条用黄砖铺成的路。

paragraphs.en: Within a short time she was walking briskly toward the Emerald City, her silver shoes tinkling merrily on the hard, yellow road-bed.
paragraphs.cn: 没过多久，她就轻快地走向翡翠城，她的银鞋在坚硬的黄砖路上发出清脆的响声。

paragraphs.en: The sun shone bright and the birds sang sweetly, and Dorothy did not feel nearly so bad as you might think a little girl would who had been suddenly whisked away from her own country and set down in the midst of a strange land.
paragraphs.cn: 阳光明媚，小鸟唱着甜美的歌。多萝西并没有你想象的那么难过，虽然她突然被带离自己的家乡，来到了一个陌生的地方。

paragraphs.en: She was surprised, as she walked along, to see how pretty the country was about her.
paragraphs.cn: 她边走边看，惊讶地发现周围的景色真漂亮。

paragraphs.en: There were neat fences at the sides of the road, painted a dainty blue color, and beyond them were fields of grain and vegetables in abundance.
paragraphs.cn: 路边有整齐的蓝色小栅栏，栅栏后面是满满的庄稼和蔬菜地。

paragraphs.en: Evidently the Munchkins were good farmers and able to raise large crops.
paragraphs.cn: 看来芒奇金人都是好农民，能种出很多庄稼。

paragraphs.en: Once in a while she would pass a house, and the people came out to look at her and bow low as she went by; for everyone knew she had been the means of destroying the Wicked Witch and setting them free from bondage.
paragraphs.cn: 她偶尔会经过一栋房子，人们会出来看她，在她经过时深深鞠躬；因为每个人都知道，她帮他们打败了坏女巫，让他们摆脱了束缚。

paragraphs.en: The houses of the Munchkins were odd-looking dwellings, for each was round, with a big dome for a roof.
paragraphs.cn: 芒奇金人的房子很奇怪，每栋都是圆圆的，屋顶像个大圆顶。

paragraphs.en: All were painted blue, for in this country of the East blue was the favorite color.
paragraphs.cn: 所有的房子都涂成了蓝色，因为在这个东方国家，蓝色是大家最喜欢的颜色。

paragraphs.en: Toward evening, when Dorothy was tired with her long walk and began to wonder where she should pass the night, she came to a house rather larger than the rest.
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚时分，多萝西走了很久，有点累了，她开始想今晚在哪里过夜。这时，她走到一栋比其他房子大一些的屋子前。

paragraphs.en: On the green lawn before it many men and women were dancing.
paragraphs.cn: 屋前的绿色草坪上，许多男人和女人正在跳舞。

paragraphs.en: Five little fiddlers played as loudly as possible, and the people were laughing and singing, while a big table near by was loaded with delicious fruits and nuts, pies and cakes, and many other good things to eat.
paragraphs.cn: 五个小提琴手拉着琴，声音很大。人们又笑又唱，旁边的大桌子上摆满了好吃的水果、坚果、馅饼、蛋糕和许多其他美味。

paragraphs.en: The people greeted Dorothy kindly, and invited her to supper and to pass the night with them; for this was the home of one of the richest Munchkins in the land, and his friends were gathered with him to celebrate their freedom from the bondage of the Wicked Witch.
paragraphs.cn: 人们亲切地问候多萝西，请她一起吃晚饭，并在他们家过夜。因为这是这片土地上最富有的芒奇金人的家，他的朋友们都聚在这里，庆祝他们摆脱了坏女巫的束缚。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy ate a hearty supper and was waited upon by the rich Munchkin himself, whose name was Boq.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 吃了一顿好吃的晚饭，很有钱的 芒奇金人 博克亲自来招待她。

paragraphs.en: Then she sat upon a settee and watched the people dance.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她坐在一张沙发上，看大家跳舞。

paragraphs.en: When Boq saw her silver shoes he said, “You must be a great sorceress.”
paragraphs.cn: 博克看到她的银鞋子，就说：“你一定是个很厉害的女巫师！”

paragraphs.en: “Why?” asked the girl.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩问：“为什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Because you wear silver shoes and have killed the Wicked Witch.
paragraphs.cn: “因为你穿着银色的鞋子，还把 坏女巫 杀死了。

paragraphs.en: Besides, you have white in your frock, and only witches and sorceresses wear white.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，你的裙子上有白色，只有女巫和女巫师才穿白色。”

paragraphs.en: “My dress is blue and white checked,” said Dorothy, smoothing out the wrinkles in it.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 抚平裙子上的褶子说：“我的裙子是蓝色和白色格子的。”

paragraphs.en: “It is kind of you to wear that,” said Boq.
paragraphs.cn: 博克说：“你穿这件衣服真好。”

paragraphs.en: “Blue is the color of the Munchkins, and white is the witch color.
paragraphs.cn: “蓝色是 芒奇金人 的颜色，白色是女巫的颜色。

paragraphs.en: So we know you are a friendly witch.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以我们知道你是个友善的女巫。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy did not know what to say to this, for all the people seemed to think her a witch, and she knew very well she was only an ordinary little girl who had come by the chance of a cyclone into a strange land.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 不知道该说什么，因为所有人都觉得她是个女巫。她明明知道自己只是个普通小女孩，只是因为一阵龙卷风才来到了这个陌生的地方。

paragraphs.en: When she had tired watching the dancing, Boq led her into the house, where he gave her a room with a pretty bed in it.
paragraphs.cn: 她看跳舞看累了，博克就带她进了屋子，给了她一间有漂亮床的房间。

paragraphs.en: The sheets were made of blue cloth, and Dorothy slept soundly in them till morning, with Toto curled up on the blue rug beside her.
paragraphs.cn: 床单是蓝色的布做的，多萝西 在上面睡得很香，一直到早上。托托 卷缩在她身边的蓝色地毯上。

paragraphs.en: She ate a hearty breakfast, and watched a wee Munchkin baby, who played with Toto and pulled his tail and crowed and laughed in a way that greatly amused Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: 她吃了一顿丰盛的早餐，看着一个小小 芒奇金人 婴儿玩 托托，拉它的尾巴，咯咯地笑，这让 多萝西 觉得很有趣。

paragraphs.en: Toto was a fine curiosity to all the people, for they had never seen a dog before.
paragraphs.cn: 托托 让所有人都很好奇，因为他们以前从没见过小狗。

paragraphs.en: “How far is it to the Emerald City?” the girl asked.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩问：“到 翡翠城 还有多远？”

paragraphs.en: “I do not know,” answered Boq gravely, “for I have never been there.
paragraphs.cn: 博克认真地回答：“我不知道，因为我从来没去过那里。

paragraphs.en: It is better for people to keep away from Oz, unless they have business with him.
paragraphs.cn: 最好大家离 奥兹大王 远一点，除非有事情找他。

paragraphs.en: But it is a long way to the Emerald City, and it will take you many days.
paragraphs.cn: 但是到 翡翠城 的路很远，你要走很多天。

paragraphs.en: The country here is rich and pleasant, but you must pass through rough and dangerous places before you reach the end of your journey.”
paragraphs.cn: 这里很漂亮，东西也多，但是你必须经过一些又难走又危险的地方，才能到达旅程的终点。”

paragraphs.en: This worried Dorothy a little, but she knew that only the Great Oz could help her get to Kansas again, so she bravely resolved not to turn back.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 有点担心，但她知道只有大 奥兹大王 才能帮她回到 堪萨斯，所以她勇敢地决定不回头。

paragraphs.en: She bade her friends good-bye, and again started along the road of yellow brick.
paragraphs.cn: 她跟朋友们说了再见，又沿着黄砖路出发了。

paragraphs.en: When she had gone several miles she thought she would stop to rest, and so climbed to the top of the fence beside the road and sat down.
paragraphs.cn: 她走了好几英里后，想停下来休息一下，就爬到路边的篱笆顶上坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: There was a great cornfield beyond the fence, and not far away she saw a Scarecrow, placed high on a pole to keep the birds from the ripe corn.
paragraphs.cn: 篱笆后面有一大片玉米地，不远处她看到一个 稻草人，高高地立在杆子上，用来吓跑吃玉米的鸟。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy leaned her chin upon her hand and gazed thoughtfully at the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 用手托着下巴，认真地看着 稻草人。

paragraphs.en: Its head was a small sack stuffed with straw, with eyes, nose, and mouth painted on it to represent a face.
paragraphs.cn: 它的头是一个塞满稻草的小袋子，上面画着眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴，像一张脸。

paragraphs.en: An old, pointed blue hat, that had belonged to some Munchkin, was perched on his head, and the rest of the figure was a blue suit of clothes, worn and faded, which had also been stuffed with straw.
paragraphs.cn: 它的头上戴着一顶旧旧的蓝色尖帽子，这帽子以前是某个 芒奇金人 的。它的身体是一套蓝色衣服，又旧又褪色，里面也塞满了稻草。

paragraphs.en: On the feet were some old boots with blue tops, such as every man wore in this country, and the figure was raised above the stalks of corn by means of the pole stuck up its back.
paragraphs.cn: 它的脚上穿着旧靴子，上面是蓝色的，就像这个国家所有男人穿的那样。它的背上插着一根杆子，让它高高地立在玉米秆上面。

paragraphs.en: While Dorothy was looking earnestly into the queer, painted face of the Scarecrow, she was surprised to see one of the eyes slowly wink at her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 正在仔细地看着 稻草人 那张奇怪的、画出来的脸，突然惊讶地看到其中一只眼睛慢慢地冲她眨了一下。

paragraphs.en: She thought she must have been mistaken at first, for none of the scarecrows in Kansas ever wink; but presently the figure nodded its head to her in a friendly way.
paragraphs.cn: 她一开始以为自己看错了，因为 堪萨斯 里的稻草人从来不会眨眼。但很快，那个稻草人友好地向她点了点头。

paragraphs.en: Then she climbed down from the fence and walked up to it, while Toto ran around the pole and barked.
paragraphs.cn: 她从篱笆上爬下来，走到那儿。托托呢，它围着杆子跑来跑去，叫个不停。

paragraphs.en: “Good day,” said the Scarecrow, in a rather husky voice.
paragraphs.cn: “你好啊！”稻草人声音有点粗粗地说。

paragraphs.en: “Did you speak?” asked the girl, in wonder.
paragraphs.cn: “你、你会说话？”小女孩好奇地问。

paragraphs.en: “Certainly,” answered the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “当然啦！”稻草人回答说。

paragraphs.en: “How do you do?”
paragraphs.cn: “你好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m pretty well, thank you,” replied Dorothy politely.
paragraphs.cn: “我挺好的，谢谢你。”多萝西很有礼貌地回答。

paragraphs.en: “How do you do?”
paragraphs.cn: “你好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not feeling well,” said the Scarecrow, with a smile, “for it is very tedious being perched up here night and day to scare away crows.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不太好。”稻草人笑着说，“每天晚上白天都站在这儿，赶乌鸦，太无聊啦。”

paragraphs.en: “Can’t you get down?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “你不能下来吗？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “No, for this pole is stuck up my back.
paragraphs.cn: “不行啊，这根杆子插在我背上呢。

paragraphs.en: If you will please take away the pole I shall be greatly obliged to you.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你能把杆子拿开，我会非常感谢你的。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy reached up both arms and lifted the figure off the pole, for, being stuffed with straw, it was quite light.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西伸出两只胳膊，把那个东西从杆子上拿了下来。因为它里面都是稻草，所以很轻。

paragraphs.en: “Thank you very much,” said the Scarecrow, when he had been set down on the ground.
paragraphs.cn: “太谢谢你啦！”当稻草人被放到地上时，它说。

paragraphs.en: “I feel like a new man.”
paragraphs.cn: “我感觉自己像个新的人！”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was puzzled at this, for it sounded queer to hear a stuffed man speak, and to see him bow and walk along beside her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西觉得很奇怪，因为一个用稻草做的假人说话，还会鞠躬，然后跟她一起走路，听起来真是不可思议。

paragraphs.en: “Who are you?” asked the Scarecrow when he had stretched himself and yawned. “And where are you going?”
paragraphs.cn: “你是谁呀？”稻草人伸了个懒腰，打了个哈欠，然后问，“你要去哪儿啊？”

paragraphs.en: “My name is Dorothy,” said the girl, “and I am going to the Emerald City, to ask the Great Oz to send me back to Kansas.”
paragraphs.cn: “我叫多萝西。”小女孩说，“我要去翡翠城，请伟大的奥兹大王把我送回堪萨斯去。”

paragraphs.en: “Where is the Emerald City?” he inquired. “And who is Oz?”
paragraphs.cn: “翡翠城在哪里？”它问，“奥兹大王又是谁呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, don’t you know?” she returned, in surprise.
paragraphs.cn: “咦，你不知道吗？”她很惊讶地问。

paragraphs.en: “No, indeed.
paragraphs.cn: “不，真的不知道。

paragraphs.en: I don’t know anything.
paragraphs.cn: 我什么都不知道。

paragraphs.en: You see, I am stuffed, so I have no brains at all,” he answered sadly.
paragraphs.cn: 你看，我里面都是稻草，所以根本没有脑子。”它伤心地回答。

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” said Dorothy, “I’m awfully sorry for you.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，”多萝西说，“我真替你难过。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you think,” he asked, “if I go to the Emerald City with you, that Oz would give me some brains?”
paragraphs.cn: “你觉得，”它问，“如果我跟你一起去翡翠城，奥兹大王会给我一些脑子吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I cannot tell,” she returned, “but you may come with me, if you like.
paragraphs.cn: “我不能确定。”她回答，“但是如果你想，你可以跟我一起来。

paragraphs.en: If Oz will not give you any brains you will be no worse off than you are now.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果奥兹大王不给你脑子，你也不会比现在更糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: “That is true,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “那倒是真的。”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “You see,” he continued confidentially, “I don’t mind my legs and arms and body being stuffed, because I cannot get hurt.
paragraphs.cn: “你看啊，”它悄悄地接着说，“我腿啊、胳膊啊、身体啊，里面都是稻草，我一点都不介意，因为我不会受伤。

paragraphs.en: If anyone treads on my toes or sticks a pin into me, it doesn’t matter, for I can’t feel it.
paragraphs.cn: 要是谁踩到我的脚趾头，或者用针扎我，都没关系，因为我感觉不到疼。

paragraphs.en: But I do not want people to call me a fool, and if my head stays stuffed with straw instead of with brains, as yours is, how am I ever to know anything?”
paragraphs.cn: 可是我不想让别人叫我笨蛋，如果我的脑袋一直只有稻草，没有像你一样的脑子，那我怎么能知道很多事情呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I understand how you feel,” said the little girl, who was truly sorry for him.
paragraphs.cn: “我懂你的感受，”小女孩说，她真的很替他难过。

paragraphs.en: “If you will come with me I’ll ask Oz to do all he can for you.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果你跟我来，我就会请奥兹大王尽力帮你。”

paragraphs.en: “Thank you,” he answered gratefully.
paragraphs.cn: “谢谢你，”他开心地回答说。

paragraphs.en: They walked back to the road.
paragraphs.cn: 他们走回了路上。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy helped him over the fence, and they started along the path of yellow brick for the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西扶他过了篱笆，他们沿着黄砖路，往翡翠城的方向走去。

paragraphs.en: Toto did not like this addition to the party at first.
paragraphs.cn: 一开始，托托不喜欢这个新加入的伙伴。

paragraphs.en: He smelled around the stuffed man as if he suspected there might be a nest of rats in the straw, and he often growled in an unfriendly way at the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: 它闻了闻那个填充人，好像觉得稻草里有老鼠。它还常常不高兴地对稻草人低吼。

paragraphs.en: “Don’t mind Toto,” said Dorothy to her new friend.
paragraphs.cn: “别理托托，”多萝西对她的新朋友说。

paragraphs.en: “He never bites.”
paragraphs.cn: “他从来不咬人。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I’m not afraid,” replied the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，我不怕，”稻草人回答说。

paragraphs.en: “He can’t hurt the straw.
paragraphs.cn: “他伤不了稻草的。

paragraphs.en: Do let me carry that basket for you.
paragraphs.cn: 让我帮你提那个篮子吧。

paragraphs.en: I shall not mind it, for I can’t get tired.
paragraphs.cn: 我不会觉得累，因为我不会累的。

paragraphs.en: I’ll tell you a secret,” he continued, as he walked along.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉你一个秘密，”他边走边说。

paragraphs.en: “There is only one thing in the world I am afraid of.”
paragraphs.cn: “世界上我只怕一样东西。”

paragraphs.en: “What is that?” asked Dorothy; “the Munchkin farmer who made you?”
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么？”多萝西问，“是做你的那个芒奇金人农夫吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” answered the Scarecrow; “it’s a lighted match.”
paragraphs.cn: “不是，”稻草人回答说，“是一根点燃的火柴。”

paragraphs.en: After a few hours the road began to be rough, and the walking grew so difficult that the Scarecrow often stumbled over the yellow bricks, which were here very uneven.
paragraphs.cn: 几个小时后，路变得不平了。走路很难，稻草人老是被绊倒，因为这里的黄砖很不平。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes, indeed, they were broken or missing altogether, leaving holes that Toto jumped across and Dorothy walked around.
paragraphs.cn: 有时，黄砖甚至碎了或者完全不见了，留下了坑洞，托托跳了过去，多萝西绕了过去。

paragraphs.en: As for the Scarecrow, having no brains, he walked straight ahead, and so stepped into the holes and fell at full length on the hard bricks.
paragraphs.cn: 至于那个稻草人，他没有脑子，只顾往前走，所以就踩进了坑里，重重地摔在硬砖上。

paragraphs.en: It never hurt him, however, and Dorothy would pick him up and set him upon his feet again, while he joined her in laughing merrily at his own mishap.
paragraphs.cn: 他从来不会受伤。多萝西会扶他起来站好，他也会跟多萝西一起，开心地笑自己摔倒了。

paragraphs.en: The farms were not nearly so well cared for here as they were farther back.
paragraphs.cn: 这里的农场没有后面那些地方照看得那么好。

paragraphs.en: There were fewer houses and fewer fruit trees, and the farther they went the more dismal and lonesome the country became.
paragraphs.cn: 房子和果树都变少了，他们走得越远，乡村就变得越荒凉和寂寞。

paragraphs.en: At noon they sat down by the roadside, near a little brook, and Dorothy opened her basket and got out some bread.
paragraphs.cn: 中午时分，他们在一个小溪边，坐在路边。多萝西打开篮子，拿出了一些面包。

paragraphs.en: She offered a piece to the Scarecrow, but he refused.
paragraphs.cn: 她递了一块给那个稻草人，但他不要。

paragraphs.en: “I am never hungry,” he said, “and it is a lucky thing I am not, for my mouth is only painted, and if I should cut a hole in it so I could eat, the straw I am stuffed with would come out, and that would spoil the shape of my head.”
paragraphs.cn: “我从来不饿，”他说，“我不饿真好，因为我的嘴巴只是画上去的。如果我剪个洞吃东西，里面的稻草就会掉出来，那样我的头就会变形了。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy saw at once that this was true, so she only nodded and went on eating her bread.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西一下子就明白他说的是真的，所以她只是点点头，继续吃她的面包。

paragraphs.en: “Tell me something about yourself and the country you came from,” said the Scarecrow, when she had finished her dinner.
paragraphs.cn: 她吃完饭后，那个稻草人说：“跟我说说你自己，还有你来的那个地方吧。”

paragraphs.en: So she told him all about Kansas, and how gray everything was there, and how the cyclone had carried her to this queer Land of Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她告诉他关于堪萨斯的一切，那里的一切都是灰蒙蒙的，还有龙卷风怎么把她带到了这个奇怪的奥兹国。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow listened carefully, and said, “I cannot understand why you should wish to leave this beautiful country and go back to the dry, gray place you call Kansas.”
paragraphs.cn: 那个稻草人认真地听着，然后说：“我不明白你为什么要离开这个美丽的地方，回到你说的那个又干又灰的堪萨斯去。”

paragraphs.en: “That is because you have no brains” answered the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “那是因为你没有脑子呀！”小女孩回答说。

paragraphs.en: “No matter how dreary and gray our homes are, we people of flesh and blood would rather live there than in any other country, be it ever so beautiful.
paragraphs.cn: “不管我们的家多么灰暗、多么无趣，我们这些有血有肉的人，宁愿住在家里，也不愿去其他再美的地方。

paragraphs.en: There is no place like home.”
paragraphs.cn: 没有比家更好的地方了。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow sighed.
paragraphs.cn: 那个稻草人叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: “Of course I cannot understand it,” he said.
paragraphs.cn: “我当然不明白，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “If your heads were stuffed with straw, like mine, you would probably all live in the beautiful places, and then Kansas would have no people at all.
paragraphs.cn: “如果你们的脑袋里也像我一样塞满了稻草，你们可能都会住在那些美丽的地方，那样的话，堪萨斯就一个人都没有了。

paragraphs.en: It is fortunate for Kansas that you have brains.”
paragraphs.cn: 堪萨斯很幸运你们有脑子。”

paragraphs.en: “Won’t you tell me a story, while we are resting?” asked the child.
paragraphs.cn: “我们休息的时候，你给我讲个故事好不好？”孩子问道。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow looked at her reproachfully, and answered:
paragraphs.cn: 那个稻草人责备地看了她一眼，然后回答说：

paragraphs.en: “My life has been so short that I really know nothing whatever.
paragraphs.cn: “我的生命太短了，什么都不知道。

paragraphs.en: I was only made day before yesterday.
paragraphs.cn: 我前天才被做出来。

paragraphs.en: What happened in the world before that time is all unknown to me.
paragraphs.cn: 在这之前世界上发生了什么，我一点也不知道。

paragraphs.en: Luckily, when the farmer made my head, one of the first things he did was to paint my ears, so that I heard what was going on.
paragraphs.cn: 幸好，农民叔叔做我脑袋的时候，最先做的一件事就是给我画耳朵，所以我听到了发生的一切。

paragraphs.en: There was another Munchkin with him, and the first thing I heard was the farmer saying, ‘How do you like those ears?’
paragraphs.cn: 当时还有一个芒奇金人在他身边，我听到的第一句话就是农民叔叔问：‘你觉得这耳朵怎么样？’

paragraphs.en: “‘They aren’t straight,’” answered the other.
paragraphs.cn: “‘它们不直呀，’”另一个回答说。

paragraphs.en: “‘Never mind,’” said the farmer.
paragraphs.cn: “‘没关系，’”农民叔叔说。

paragraphs.en: “‘They are ears just the same,’” which was true enough.
paragraphs.cn: “‘它们一样是耳朵，’”这话倒也挺对。

paragraphs.en: “‘Now I’ll make the eyes,’” said the farmer.
paragraphs.cn: “‘现在我来做眼睛，’”农民叔叔说。

paragraphs.en: So he painted my right eye, and as soon as it was finished I found myself looking at him and at everything around me with a great deal of curiosity, for this was my first glimpse of the world.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他画了我的右眼，眼睛一画好，我就好奇地看着他和周围的一切，因为这是我第一次看到这个世界。

paragraphs.en: “‘That’s a rather pretty eye,’” remarked the Munchkin who was watching the farmer.
paragraphs.cn: “‘这眼睛挺好看的，’”那个看着农民叔叔的芒奇金人说。

paragraphs.en: “‘Blue paint is just the color for eyes.’
paragraphs.cn: “‘蓝色颜料最适合做眼睛了。’

paragraphs.en: “‘I think I’ll make the other a little bigger,’” said the farmer.
paragraphs.cn: “‘我想把另一只眼睛画大一点，’”农民叔叔说。

paragraphs.en: And when the second eye was done I could see much better than before.
paragraphs.cn: 第二只眼睛画好后，我看得比以前清楚多了。

paragraphs.en: Then he made my nose and my mouth.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他做了我的鼻子和嘴巴。

paragraphs.en: But I did not speak, because at that time I didn’t know what a mouth was for.
paragraphs.cn: 但我没说话，因为那时候我不知道嘴巴是用来干什么的。

paragraphs.en: I had the fun of watching them make my body and my arms and legs; and when they fastened on my head, at last, I felt very proud, for I thought I was just as good a man as anyone.
paragraphs.cn: 我看着他们做我的身体、胳膊和腿，觉得很有趣；最后他们把我的头安上去的时候，我非常骄傲，因为我觉得我跟其他人一样棒。

paragraphs.en: “‘This fellow will scare the crows fast enough,’ said the farmer.
paragraphs.cn: “‘这家伙能很快把乌鸦吓跑，’”农民叔叔说。

paragraphs.en: ‘He looks just like a man.’
paragraphs.cn: ‘他看起来真像个人。’

paragraphs.en: “‘Why, he is a man,’ said the other, and I quite agreed with him.
paragraphs.cn: “‘哎呀，他就是一个人呀！’”另一个人说，我非常同意他的话。

paragraphs.en: The farmer carried me under his arm to the cornfield, and set me up on a tall stick, where you found me.
paragraphs.cn: 农民叔叔把我夹在胳膊下面，带到玉米地里，把我立在一根高高的杆子上，你就是在那里找到我的。

paragraphs.en: He and his friend soon after walked away and left me alone.
paragraphs.cn: 他和他的朋友很快就走了，把我一个人留在那儿。

paragraphs.en: “I did not like to be deserted this way.
paragraphs.cn: “我不喜欢这样被丢下。

paragraphs.en: So I tried to walk after them.
paragraphs.cn: 所以我试着去追他们。

paragraphs.en: But my feet would not touch the ground, and I was forced to stay on that pole.
paragraphs.cn: 但是我的脚碰不到地，我只好待在那根杆子上。

paragraphs.en: It was a lonely life to lead, for I had nothing to think of, having been made such a little while before.
paragraphs.cn: 我过得很孤单，因为我刚做好没多久，什么都不知道。

paragraphs.en: Many crows and other birds flew into the cornfield, but as soon as they saw me they flew away again, thinking I was a Munchkin; and this pleased me and made me feel that I was quite an important person.
paragraphs.cn: 好多乌鸦和其他鸟飞到玉米地里，可是一看到我，它们就又飞走了，以为我是一个芒奇金人；这让我很高兴，觉得自己是个很重要的人。

paragraphs.en: By and by an old crow flew near me, and after looking at me carefully he perched upon my shoulder and said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，一只老乌鸦飞到我身边，仔细看了看我，然后落在我的肩膀上说：

paragraphs.en: “‘I wonder if that farmer thought to fool me in this clumsy manner.
paragraphs.cn: “‘我猜那个农夫是不是想用这种笨方法骗我。

paragraphs.en: Any crow of sense could see that you are only stuffed with straw.’
paragraphs.cn: 任何一只聪明的乌鸦都能看出来，你只是个草人罢了。’

paragraphs.en: Then he hopped down at my feet and ate all the corn he wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他跳到我脚边，想吃多少玉米就吃多少。

paragraphs.en: The other birds, seeing he was not harmed by me, came to eat the corn too, so in a short time there was a great flock of them about me.
paragraphs.cn: 别的鸟看到他没有被我伤害，也过来吃玉米了，没一会儿，我身边就围着一大群鸟。

paragraphs.en: “I felt sad at this, for it showed I was not such a good Scarecrow after all; but the old crow comforted me, saying, ‘If you only had brains in your head you would be as good a man as any of them, and a better man than some of them.
paragraphs.cn: 我为此感到难过，因为这说明我根本不是一个好稻草人；但是那只老乌鸦安慰我说，‘如果你脑袋里有脑子，你就会和他们任何人一样棒，甚至比他们中的一些人还要棒。

paragraphs.en: Brains are the only things worth having in this world, no matter whether one is a crow or a man.’
paragraphs.cn: 在这个世界上，脑子是唯一值得拥有的东西，不管你是一只乌鸦还是一个人。’

paragraphs.en: “After the crows had gone I thought this over, and decided I would try hard to get some brains.
paragraphs.cn: 乌鸦们走了以后，我把这件事想了又想，决定要努力去得到一些脑子。

paragraphs.en: By good luck you came along and pulled me off the stake, and from what you say I am sure the Great Oz will give me brains as soon as we get to the Emerald City.”
paragraphs.cn: 很幸运你来了，把我从木桩上拉了下来，听你说的，我相信等我们到了翡翠城，伟大的奥兹大王就会给我脑子。”

paragraphs.en: “I hope so,” said Dorothy earnestly, “since you seem anxious to have them.”
paragraphs.cn: “我希望是这样。”多萝西认真地说，“因为你看起来很想得到它们。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes; I am anxious,” returned the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是的！我特别想。”稻草人回答说。

paragraphs.en: “It is such an uncomfortable feeling to know one is a fool.”
paragraphs.cn: “知道自己是个傻瓜，这种感觉太难受了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said the girl, “let us go.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，”小女孩说，“我们走吧。”

paragraphs.en: And she handed the basket to the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: 她把篮子递给了稻草人。

paragraphs.en: There were no fences at all by the roadside now, and the land was rough and untilled.
paragraphs.cn: 现在路边已经完全没有栅栏了，土地也很荒凉，没有人耕种。

paragraphs.en: Toward evening they came to a great forest, where the trees grew so big and close together that their branches met over the road of yellow brick.
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚时分，他们来到了一片大森林，那里的树又高又密，树枝都碰到了一起，盖住了黄砖路。

paragraphs.en: It was almost dark under the trees, for the branches shut out the daylight; but the travelers did not stop, and went on into the forest.
paragraphs.cn: 树底下几乎是黑的，因为树枝挡住了阳光；但是旅行者们没有停下，继续往前走进了森林。

paragraphs.en: “If this road goes in, it must come out,” said the Scarecrow, “and as the Emerald City is at the other end of the road, we must go wherever it leads us.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果这条路能进去，那它就一定能出去，”稻草人说，“而且翡翠城就在路的另一头，所以我们必须顺着这条路走下去。”

paragraphs.en: “Anyone would know that,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “谁都知道这个。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “Certainly; that is why I know it,” returned the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “当然了；所以我才知道啊。”稻草人回答说。

paragraphs.en: “If it required brains to figure it out, I never should have said it.”
paragraphs.cn: “要是想明白这个需要脑子，那我肯定就说不出来了。”

paragraphs.en: After an hour or so the light faded away, and they found themselves stumbling along in the darkness.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一个小时左右，光线就消失了，他们只好在黑暗中摸索着往前走。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy could not see at all, but Toto could, for some dogs see very well in the dark; and the Scarecrow declared he could see as well as by day.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西什么也看不见，但是托托能看见，因为有些狗狗在黑暗中看得很清楚；而稻草人也说他白天晚上都看得见。

paragraphs.en: So she took hold of his arm and managed to get along fairly well.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她抓住了他的胳膊，勉强还能走得挺好。

paragraphs.en: “If you see any house, or any place where we can pass the night,” she said, “you must tell me; for it is very uncomfortable walking in the dark.”
paragraphs.cn: 她说：“如果你看到房子，或者可以睡觉的地方，你要告诉我；因为天黑了走路很不舒服。”

paragraphs.en: Soon after the Scarecrow stopped.
paragraphs.cn: 没过多久，稻草人停了下来。

paragraphs.en: “I see a little cottage at the right of us,” he said, “built of logs and branches.
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“我看到右边有个小房子，是用木头和树枝搭的。

paragraphs.en: Shall we go there?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们去那里好不好？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, indeed,” answered the child.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子回答说：“好啊，当然好啦！”

paragraphs.en: “I am all tired out.”
paragraphs.cn: “我太累了。”

paragraphs.en: So the Scarecrow led her through the trees until they reached the cottage, and Dorothy entered and found a bed of dried leaves in one corner.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，稻草人带着她穿过树林，直到他们走到那个小房子。多萝西走了进去，在一个角落里找到了一张用干树叶铺的床。

paragraphs.en: She lay down at once, and with Toto beside her soon fell into a sound sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 她马上躺了下来，托托在她身边，她很快就睡着了。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow, who was never tired, stood up in another corner and waited patiently until morning came.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人从来不觉得累，它站在另一个角落里，一直耐心地等着，直到天亮。

chapters.title_en: The Rescue of the Tin Woodman

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy awoke the sun was shining through the trees and Toto had long been out chasing birds around him and squirrels.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西醒来的时候，太阳光透过树林照了进来，托托早就出去追小鸟和松鼠了。

paragraphs.en: She sat up and looked around her.
paragraphs.cn: 她坐了起来，看看周围。

paragraphs.en: There was the Scarecrow, still standing patiently in his corner, waiting for her.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人还在那里，仍然耐心又安静地站在角落里等着她。

paragraphs.en: “We must go and search for water,” she said to him.
paragraphs.cn: 她对他说：“我们得去找水。”

paragraphs.en: “Why do you want water?” he asked.
paragraphs.cn: 他问：“你为什么要水呀？”

paragraphs.en: “To wash my face clean after the dust of the road, and to drink, so the dry bread will not stick in my throat.”
paragraphs.cn: “为了洗掉脸上的灰尘，让脸变干净。还要喝水，这样干面包就不会卡在我的喉咙里了。”

paragraphs.en: “It must be inconvenient to be made of flesh,” said the Scarecrow thoughtfully, “for you must sleep, and eat and drink.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人想了想说：“用肉做的身体真不方便啊，因为你得睡觉，还得吃东西喝水。

paragraphs.en: However, you have brains, and it is worth a lot of bother to be able to think properly.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过，你有脑袋，能好好思考，就算麻烦一点也值得。”

paragraphs.en: They left the cottage and walked through the trees until they found a little spring of clear water, where Dorothy drank and bathed and ate her breakfast.
paragraphs.cn: 他们离开了小房子，穿过树林，走到找到一个清澈的小泉水的地方，多萝西在那里喝水、洗澡，还吃了早饭。

paragraphs.en: She saw there was not much bread left in the basket, and the girl was thankful the Scarecrow did not have to eat anything, for there was scarcely enough for herself and Toto for the day.
paragraphs.cn: 她看到篮子里剩下的面包不多了，女孩很庆幸稻草人不用吃东西，因为面包就只够她自己和托托吃一天的了。

paragraphs.en: When she had finished her meal, and was about to go back to the road of yellow brick, she was startled to hear a deep groan near by.
paragraphs.cn: 她吃完饭后，正要走回那条黄砖路，突然听到旁边传来一声很响的呻吟声，吓了一跳。

paragraphs.en: “What was that?” she asked timidly.
paragraphs.cn: 她小声地问：“那是什么声音？”

paragraphs.en: “I cannot imagine,” replied the Scarecrow; “but we can go and see.”
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人回答说：“我不知道，但是我们可以去看看。”

paragraphs.en: Just then another groan reached their ears, and the sound seemed to come from behind them.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，又一声呻吟传到他们耳朵里，声音好像是从他们后面传来的。

paragraphs.en: They turned and walked through the forest a few steps, when Dorothy discovered something shining in a ray of sunshine that fell between the trees.
paragraphs.cn: 他们转过身，在森林里走了几步，突然多萝西发现有一道阳光透过树林照下来，那里有什么东西亮亮的。

paragraphs.en: She ran to the place and then stopped short, with a little cry of surprise.
paragraphs.cn: 她跑到那个地方，然后突然停住了，惊讶地叫了一声。

paragraphs.en: One of the big trees had been partly chopped through, and standing beside it, with an uplifted axe in his hands, was a man made entirely of tin.
paragraphs.cn: 有一棵大树被砍了一半，旁边站着一个人，手里拿着一把举起来的斧头，那个人完全是用铁皮做的。

paragraphs.en: His head and arms and legs were jointed upon his body, but he stood perfectly motionless, as if he could not stir at all.
paragraphs.cn: 他的头、胳膊和腿都连接在身体上，但是他一动不动，好像完全不能动一样。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy looked at him in amazement, and so did the Scarecrow, while Toto barked sharply and made a snap at the tin legs, which hurt his teeth.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西很惊讶地看着他，稻草人也一样。托托大声叫了几下，还去咬铁皮腿，结果把它的牙都弄疼了。

paragraphs.en: “Did you groan?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西问：“是你发出呻吟声的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” answered the tin man, “I did.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，”铁皮人回答说，“是我。”

paragraphs.en: I’ve been groaning for more than a year, and no one has ever heard me before or come to help me.”
paragraphs.cn: 我已经哼哼一年多了，以前从来没人听到我，也没人来帮我。

paragraphs.en: “What can I do for you?” she inquired softly, for she was moved by the sad voice in which the man spoke.
paragraphs.cn: “我能为你做些什么呢？”她轻轻地问，因为那个男人的声音听起来太伤心了，她很心疼。

paragraphs.en: “Get an oil-can and oil my joints,” he answered.
paragraphs.cn: “拿个油壶，给我的关节上点油。”他回答。

paragraphs.en: “They are rusted so badly that I cannot move them at all; if I am well oiled I shall soon be all right again.
paragraphs.cn: “它们生锈得太厉害了，我一点也动不了。如果能好好上油，我很快就会好起来的。

paragraphs.en: You will find an oil-can on a shelf in my cottage.”
paragraphs.cn: 你会在我的小房子里，一个架子上找到油壶的。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy at once ran back to the cottage and found the oil-can, and then she returned and asked anxiously, “Where are your joints?”
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西立刻跑回小房子，找到了油壶。然后她回来，焦急地问：“你的关节在哪里呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Oil my neck, first,” replied the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “先给我的脖子上油。”铁皮人回答说。

paragraphs.en: So she oiled it, and as it was quite badly rusted the Scarecrow took hold of the tin head and moved it gently from side to side until it worked freely, and then the man could turn it himself.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她给它上了油。因为生锈得很厉害，稻草人抓住那个铁头，轻轻地左右动了动，直到它能自由活动了，那个人就能自己转动了。

paragraphs.en: “Now oil the joints in my arms,” he said.
paragraphs.cn: “现在，给我的胳膊关节上油。”他说。

paragraphs.en: And Dorothy oiled them and the Scarecrow bent them carefully until they were quite free from rust and as good as new.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西给它们上了油，稻草人小心地弯动它们，直到它们完全没有锈了，和新的一样好。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman gave a sigh of satisfaction and lowered his axe, which he leaned against the tree.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人满意地叹了口气，放下了斧头，把它靠在树上。

paragraphs.en: “This is a great comfort,” he said.
paragraphs.cn: “这真舒服啊！”他说。

paragraphs.en: “I have been holding that axe in the air ever since I rusted, and I’m glad to be able to put it down at last.
paragraphs.cn: “自从我生锈以后，就一直把斧头举在空中。现在终于能放下了，我真高兴。

paragraphs.en: Now, if you will oil the joints of my legs, I shall be all right once more.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，如果你能给我的腿关节上油，我就又会好起来了。”

paragraphs.en: So they oiled his legs until he could move them freely; and he thanked them again and again for his release, for he seemed a very polite creature, and very grateful.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们给他的腿上了油，直到他可以自由地动了。他一遍又一遍地感谢他们，因为他看起来非常有礼貌，也很感激。

paragraphs.en: “I might have stood there always if you had not come along,” he said; “so you have certainly saved my life.
paragraphs.cn: “如果你们没有来，我可能就一直站在那里了。”他说，“所以你们真是救了我的命啊！

paragraphs.en: How did you happen to be here?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们怎么会在这里呢？”

paragraphs.en: “We are on our way to the Emerald City to see the Great Oz,” she answered, “and we stopped at your cottage to pass the night.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们正在去 翡翠城 的路上，想去见伟大的 奥兹大王。”她回答说，“我们停在你的小房子里过夜。”

paragraphs.en: “Why do you wish to see Oz?” he asked.
paragraphs.cn: “你们为什么想见 奥兹大王 呢？”他问。

paragraphs.en: “I want him to send me back to Kansas, and the Scarecrow wants him to put a few brains into his head,” she replied.
paragraphs.cn: “我想让他送我回 堪萨斯，而 稻草人 想让他给自己一些脑子。”她回答说。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman appeared to think deeply for a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人好像认真地想了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Do you suppose Oz could give me a heart?”
paragraphs.cn: “你们觉得 奥兹大王 能给我一颗心吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I guess so,” Dorothy answered.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我想可以吧。”多萝西回答说。

paragraphs.en: “It would be as easy as to give the Scarecrow brains.”
paragraphs.cn: “这和给 稻草人 脑子一样容易。”

paragraphs.en: “True,” the Tin Woodman returned.
paragraphs.cn: “确实是这样！”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “So, if you will allow me to join your party, I will also go to the Emerald City and ask Oz to help me.”
paragraphs.cn: “那么，如果你们愿意让我加入，我也想和你们一起去 翡翠城，请 奥兹大王 帮我。”

paragraphs.en: “Come along,” said the Scarecrow heartily, and Dorothy added that she would be pleased to have his company.
paragraphs.cn: “一起来吧！”稻草人高兴地说，多萝西也补充说，她很高兴有他作伴。

paragraphs.en: So the Tin Woodman shouldered his axe and they all passed through the forest until they came to the road that was paved with yellow brick.
paragraphs.cn: 于是铁皮人扛起他的斧头，他们都穿过森林，直到来到那条铺着黄色砖块的路上。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman had asked Dorothy to put the oil-can in her basket.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人已经请多萝西把油壶放进她的篮子里了。

paragraphs.en: “For,” he said, “if I should get caught in the rain, and rust again, I would need the oil-can badly.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“要是淋了雨，我又生锈了，就特别需要油壶。”

paragraphs.en: It was a bit of good luck to have their new comrade join the party, for soon after they had begun their journey again they came to a place where the trees and branches grew so thick over the road that the travelers could not pass.
paragraphs.cn: 有新朋友加入真幸运，因为他们没走多久，就到了一个地方。那里的树木枝叶很密，把路都遮住了，大家过不去。

paragraphs.en: But the Tin Woodman set to work with his axe and chopped so well that soon he cleared a passage for the entire party.
paragraphs.cn: 但是铁皮人拿起斧子，使劲砍起来，很快就为大家开出一条路。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was thinking so earnestly as they walked along that she did not notice when the Scarecrow stumbled into a hole and rolled over to the side of the road.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西走路时想得太认真了，没看到稻草人不小心掉进洞里，滚到路边。

paragraphs.en: Indeed he was obliged to call to her to help him up again.
paragraphs.cn: 他只好叫她来帮忙，把他扶起来。

paragraphs.en: “Why didn’t you walk around the hole?” asked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么不绕开那个洞走呢？”铁皮人问。

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know enough,” replied the Scarecrow cheerfully.
paragraphs.cn: “我懂得不够多，”稻草人开心地说。

paragraphs.en: “My head is stuffed with straw, you know, and that is why I am going to Oz to ask him for some brains.”
paragraphs.cn: “我的脑袋里都是稻草，你知道的。所以我才要去奥兹大王那里，请他给我一些脑子。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I see,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，我懂了，”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “But, after all, brains are not the best things in the world.”
paragraphs.cn: “但是，脑子也不是世界上最好的东西。”

paragraphs.en: “Have you any?” inquired the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你有脑子吗？”稻草人问。

paragraphs.en: “No, my head is quite empty,” answered the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “没有，我的脑袋是空的，”铁皮人回答说。

paragraphs.en: “But once I had brains, and a heart also; so, having tried them both, I should much rather have a heart.”
paragraphs.cn: “但我以前有脑子，也有心。我都试过了，我更想要一颗心。”

paragraphs.en: “And why is that?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “为什么呢？”稻草人问。

paragraphs.en: “I will tell you my story, and then you will know.”
paragraphs.cn: “我告诉你我的故事，你就知道了。”

paragraphs.en: So, while they were walking through the forest, the Tin Woodman told the following story:
paragraphs.cn: 于是，他们走过森林的时候，铁皮人讲了下面的故事：

paragraphs.en: “I was born the son of a woodman who chopped down trees in the forest and sold the wood for a living.
paragraphs.cn: “我是一个砍树人的儿子，爸爸在森林里砍树，卖木头赚钱养家。

paragraphs.en: When I grew up, I too became a wood-chopper, and after my father died I took care of my old mother as long as she lived.
paragraphs.cn: 我长大后，也成了砍树人。爸爸去世后，我一直照顾妈妈，直到她去世。

paragraphs.en: Then I made up my mind that instead of living alone I would marry, so that I might not become lonely.
paragraphs.cn: 后来我想，我不能一个人生活，要结婚，这样才不会孤单。

paragraphs.en: “There was one of the Munchkin girls who was so beautiful that I soon grew to love her with all my heart.
paragraphs.cn: “在芒奇金人的女孩中，有一个长得特别美，我很快就爱上了她。

paragraphs.en: She, on her part, promised to marry me as soon as I could earn enough money to build a better house for her; so I set to work harder than ever.
paragraphs.cn: 她答应我，只要我赚够钱给她盖一栋好房子，就嫁给我。所以我比以前更努力地工作。

paragraphs.en: But the girl lived with an old woman who did not want her to marry anyone, for she was so lazy she wished the girl to remain with her and do the cooking and the housework.
paragraphs.cn: 但是那个女孩跟一个老太太住在一起，老太太很懒，不想让她嫁人。她希望女孩一直留在身边，做饭和做家务。

paragraphs.en: So the old woman went to the Wicked Witch of the East, and promised her two sheep and a cow if she would prevent the marriage.
paragraphs.cn: 于是老太太找到东方坏女巫，说只要她能阻止这门婚事，就给她两只羊和一头牛。

paragraphs.en: Thereupon the Wicked Witch enchanted my axe, and when I was chopping away at my best one day, for I was anxious to get the new house and my wife as soon as possible, the axe slipped all at once and cut off my left leg.
paragraphs.cn: 于是坏女巫给我的斧子施了魔法。有一天我使劲砍树，因为我急着想快点盖好新房，娶到妻子。结果斧子突然滑了一下，把我的左腿砍掉了。

paragraphs.en: “This at first seemed a great misfortune, for I knew a one-legged man could not do very well as a wood-chopper.
paragraphs.cn: “这刚开始看来是个大麻烦，因为我知道独腿的人当砍树工，肯定做不好。

paragraphs.en: So I went to a tinsmith and had him make me a new leg out of tin.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我去找一个打铁的，让他给我做了一条锡腿。

paragraphs.en: The leg worked very well, once I was used to it.
paragraphs.cn: 我习惯了以后，这条腿用起来很好。

paragraphs.en: But my action angered the Wicked Witch of the East, for she had promised the old woman I should not marry the pretty Munchkin girl.
paragraphs.cn: 但是我的做法惹恼了东方坏女巫，因为她答应过老太太，不让我娶那个美丽的芒奇金人女孩。

paragraphs.en: When I began chopping again, my axe slipped and cut off my right leg.
paragraphs.cn: 我又开始砍树时，斧子滑了一下，把我的右腿也砍掉了。

paragraphs.en: Again I went to the tinsmith, and again he made me a leg out of tin.
paragraphs.cn: 我又去找那个打铁的，他又给我做了一条锡腿。

paragraphs.en: After this the enchanted axe cut off my arms, one after the other; but, nothing daunted, I had them replaced with tin ones.
paragraphs.cn: 后来，那把斧子把我的胳膊一个个砍掉了。但我没害怕，就让铁匠给我安上锡胳膊。

paragraphs.en: The Wicked Witch then made the axe slip and cut off my head, and at first I thought that was the end of me.
paragraphs.cn: 后来，坏女巫 又让斧子滑了一下，把我的头砍掉了。我那时以为自己要完蛋了。

paragraphs.en: But the tinsmith happened to come along, and he made me a new head out of tin.
paragraphs.cn: 但这时铁匠正好来了，他用锡给我做了个新脑袋。

paragraphs.en: “I thought I had beaten the Wicked Witch then, and I worked harder than ever; but I little knew how cruel my enemy could be.
paragraphs.cn: “我那时以为打败了 坏女巫，就更努力地干活了。但我不知道敌人有多坏。

paragraphs.en: She thought of a new way to kill my love for the beautiful Munchkin maiden, and made my axe slip again, so that it cut right through my body, splitting me into two halves.
paragraphs.cn: 她又想了个办法，要让我不再爱美丽的 芒奇金人 姑娘。她又让我的斧子滑了一下，正好把我从中间劈成了两半。

paragraphs.en: Once more the tinsmith came to my help and made me a body of tin, fastening my tin arms and legs and head to it, by means of joints, so that I could move around as well as ever.
paragraphs.cn: 铁匠又来帮我了，他给我做了个锡身体。他把我的锡胳膊、锡腿和锡头都安在上面，用接头连好，这样我又能像以前一样动了。

paragraphs.en: But, alas!
paragraphs.cn: 唉！

paragraphs.en: I had now no heart, so that I lost all my love for the Munchkin girl, and did not care whether I married her or not.
paragraphs.cn: 我现在没了心，所以也不爱 芒奇金人 姑娘了。我也不在乎娶不娶她。

paragraphs.en: I suppose she is still living with the old woman, waiting for me to come after her.
paragraphs.cn: 我想她还在和老太太住，等着我去找她吧。

paragraphs.en: “My body shone so brightly in the sun that I felt very proud of it and it did not matter now if my axe slipped, for it could not cut me.
paragraphs.cn: “我的身体在太阳下亮亮的，我很骄傲。现在斧子滑了也没事，因为它砍不动我了。

paragraphs.en: There was only one danger—that my joints would rust; but I kept an oil-can in my cottage and took care to oil myself whenever I needed it.
paragraphs.cn: 只有一个地方不好——我的关节会生锈。但我屋里有个油壶，我总是小心地给自己上油。

paragraphs.en: However, there came a day when I forgot to do this, and, being caught in a rainstorm, before I thought of the danger my joints had rusted, and I was left to stand in the woods until you came to help me.
paragraphs.cn: 可是有一天，我忘了给自己上油。我被大雨淋湿了，还没想起来，关节就生锈了。我只能一直站在森林里，直到你们来帮我。

paragraphs.en: It was a terrible thing to undergo, but during the year I stood there I had time to think that the greatest loss I had known was the loss of my heart.
paragraphs.cn: 这很难受，但我站在那一年里，有时间想，我失去的最重要的东西是我的心。

paragraphs.en: While I was in love I was the happiest man on earth; but no one can love who has not a heart, and so I am resolved to ask Oz to give me one.
paragraphs.cn: 我恋爱时，是世界上最开心的人。但没有心就不能爱，所以我决定请 奥兹大王 给我一颗心。

paragraphs.en: If he does, I will go back to the Munchkin maiden and marry her.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果他给了，我就会去找 芒奇金人 姑娘，娶她。”

paragraphs.en: Both Dorothy and the Scarecrow had been greatly interested in the story of the Tin Woodman, and now they knew why he was so anxious to get a new heart.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 和 稻草人 都很喜欢 铁皮人 的故事，现在他们知道他为什么那么想要一颗新的心了。

paragraphs.en: “All the same,” said the Scarecrow, “I shall ask for brains instead of a heart; for a fool would not know what to do with a heart if he had one.”
paragraphs.cn: “不过呢，” 稻草人 说，“我还是要脑子，不要心。因为傻瓜就算有心，也不知道怎么用。”

paragraphs.en: “I shall take the heart,” returned the Tin Woodman; “for brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world.”
paragraphs.cn: “我还是要心，” 铁皮人 说，“因为有脑子不一定快乐，而快乐是世界上最好的事。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy did not say anything, for she was puzzled to know which of her two friends was right, and she decided if she could only get back to Kansas and Aunt Em, it did not matter so much whether the Woodman had no brains and the Scarecrow no heart, or each got what he wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 没说话，因为她不知道两个朋友谁说得对。她决定，只要能回到 堪萨斯 和 艾姆婶婶 那里，那 铁皮人 没脑子和 稻草人 没心，或者每个人都得到想要的东西，就没那么重要了。

paragraphs.en: What worried her most was that the bread was nearly gone, and another meal for herself and Toto would empty the basket.
paragraphs.cn: 最让她担心的是面包快没了，她和 托托 再吃一顿，篮子就空了。

paragraphs.en: To be sure, neither the Woodman nor the Scarecrow ever ate anything, but she was not made of tin nor straw, and could not live unless she was fed.
paragraphs.cn: 没错，铁皮人 和 稻草人 从来不吃东西，但她不是锡做的也不是稻草做的，她不吃东西就活不了。

paragraphs.en: All this time Dorothy and her companions had been walking through the thick woods.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间，多萝西 和她的朋友们一直在很密的森林里走。

paragraphs.en: The road was still paved with yellow brick, but these were much covered by dried branches and dead leaves from the trees, and the walking was not at all good.
paragraphs.cn: 路还是黄砖铺的，但被树上的枯树枝和落叶盖住了好多，走起来一点也不好。

paragraphs.en: There were few birds in this part of the forest, for birds love the open country where there is plenty of sunshine.
paragraphs.cn: 这片森林里鸟很少，因为鸟喜欢有很多阳光的空旷地方。

paragraphs.en: But now and then there came a deep growl from some wild animal hidden among the trees.
paragraphs.cn: 但时不时地，树林里会传来一些野兽低沉的叫声。

paragraphs.en: These sounds made the little girl’s heart beat fast, for she did not know what made them; but Toto knew, and he walked close to Dorothy’s side, and did not even bark in return.
paragraphs.cn: 这些声音让小女孩的心跳得很快，因为她不知道是什么声音。但 托托 知道，他紧紧地跟在 多萝西 身边，甚至都没有叫。

paragraphs.en: “How long will it be,” the child asked of the Tin Woodman, “before we are out of the forest?”
paragraphs.cn: “我们要多久才能走出森林呢？”孩子问 铁皮人。

paragraphs.en: “I cannot tell,” was the answer, “for I have never been to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，”他回答，“因为我从来没去过 翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: But my father went there once, when I was a boy, and he said it was a long journey through a dangerous country, although nearer to the city where Oz dwells the country is beautiful.
paragraphs.cn: 但我爸爸在我小的时候去过一次，他说那是一段很远的路，要穿过危险的地方。不过，靠近 奥兹大王 住的那个城市，景色就很美。

paragraphs.en: But I am not afraid so long as I have my oil-can, and nothing can hurt the Scarecrow, while you bear upon your forehead the mark of the Good Witch’s kiss, and that will protect you from harm.”
paragraphs.cn: 但只要我有我的油壶，我就不怕。没有人能伤害 稻草人。你的额头上还有 好女巫 亲吻的印记，那会保护你不受伤。”

paragraphs.en: “But Toto!” said the girl anxiously. “What will protect him?”
paragraphs.cn: “可是 托托！”小女孩着急地说，“什么能保护他呢？”

paragraphs.en: “We must protect him ourselves if he is in danger,” replied the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “如果他有危险，我们就要自己保护他，”铁皮人 回答说。

paragraphs.en: Just as he spoke there came from the forest a terrible roar, and the next moment a great Lion bounded into the road.
paragraphs.cn: 他刚说完，森林里就传来一声可怕的吼叫，接着，一只大大的 狮子 跳到了路上。

paragraphs.en: With one blow of his paw he sent the Scarecrow spinning over and over to the edge of the road, and then he struck at the Tin Woodman with his sharp claws.
paragraphs.cn: 他一爪子就把 稻草人 打得滚到了路边，然后用锋利的爪子抓向 铁皮人。

paragraphs.en: But, to the Lion’s surprise, he could make no impression on the tin, although the Woodman fell over in the road and lay still.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，让 狮子 吃惊的是，他抓不动锡皮，尽管 铁皮人 倒在路上一动不动了。

paragraphs.en: Little Toto, now that he had an enemy to face, ran barking toward the Lion, and the great beast had opened his mouth to bite the dog, when Dorothy, fearing Toto would be killed, and heedless of danger, rushed forward and slapped the Lion upon his nose as hard as she could, while she cried out:
paragraphs.cn: 小 托托 现在有敌人要面对了，他叫着跑向 狮子。那只大野兽张开嘴，正要咬狗，这时 多萝西 冲了上去。她怕 托托 会被咬死，也不管危险，使劲拍打 狮子 的鼻子，大声喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Don’t you dare to bite Toto!
paragraphs.cn: “你不许咬 托托！”

paragraphs.en: You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a big beast like you, to bite a poor little dog!”
paragraphs.cn: “你这么大的野兽，咬一只可怜的小狗，真应该感到羞耻！”

paragraphs.en: “I didn’t bite him,” said the Lion, as he rubbed his nose with his paw where Dorothy had hit it.
paragraphs.cn: “我没咬他，”狮子 说着，用爪子揉了揉 多萝西 打过的地方。

paragraphs.en: “No, but you tried to,” she retorted.
paragraphs.cn: “不，你试着咬了，”她反驳道。

paragraphs.en: “You are nothing but a big coward.”
paragraphs.cn: “你就是个大大的胆小鬼。”

paragraphs.en: “I know it,” said the Lion, hanging his head in shame.
paragraphs.cn: “我知道，”狮子 羞愧地低下了头。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve always known it.
paragraphs.cn: “我一直都知道。”

paragraphs.en: But how can I help it?”
paragraphs.cn: “可我能怎么办呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know, I’m sure.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，真的。”

paragraphs.en: To think of your striking a stuffed man, like the poor Scarecrow!”
paragraphs.cn: “你想想，你居然去打一个填充的人，就像可怜的 稻草人！”

paragraphs.en: “Is he stuffed?” asked the Lion in surprise, as he watched her pick up the Scarecrow and set him upon his feet, while she patted him into shape again.
paragraphs.cn: “他是填充的吗？”狮子 惊讶地问，他看着她扶起 稻草人，让他站好，还拍了拍，让他恢复原样。

paragraphs.en: “Of course he’s stuffed,” replied Dorothy, who was still angry.
paragraphs.cn: “他当然是填充的呀，”多萝西 回答说，她还有点生气。

paragraphs.en: “That’s why he went over so easily,” remarked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “所以他才那么容易就倒了，”狮子 说。

paragraphs.en: “It astonished me to see him whirl around so.
paragraphs.cn: “看到他那样转来转去，真让我吃惊。”

paragraphs.en: Is the other one stuffed also?”
paragraphs.cn: “另一个人也是填充的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” said Dorothy, “he’s made of tin.”
paragraphs.cn: “不是，”多萝西 说，“他是锡做的。”

paragraphs.en: And she helped the Woodman up again.
paragraphs.cn: 她又把 铁皮人 扶了起来。

paragraphs.en: “That’s why he nearly blunted my claws,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “所以他才差点弄钝了我的爪子，”狮子 说。

paragraphs.en: “When they scratched against the tin it made a cold shiver run down my back.
paragraphs.cn: “我的爪子碰到锡皮的时候，我感觉后背一阵发凉。”

paragraphs.en: What is that little animal you are so tender of?”
paragraphs.cn: “你那么爱护的小动物是什么呀？”

paragraphs.en: “He is my dog, Toto,” answered Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “他是我的狗，托托，”多萝西 回答道。

paragraphs.en: “Is he made of tin, or stuffed?” asked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “他是锡做的，还是填充的呀？”狮子 问道。

paragraphs.en: “Neither.
paragraphs.cn: “都不是。”

paragraphs.en: He’s a—a—a meat dog,” said the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “他是一只……一只……一只肉狗，”小女孩说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh!
He’s a curious animal and seems remarkably small, now that I look at him.
paragraphs.cn: 他是个好奇的小动物，我看着他，觉得他好小好小。

paragraphs.en: No one would think of biting such a little thing, except a coward like me,” continued the Lion sadly.
paragraphs.cn: 没人会想咬这么小的东西，除了我这样的胆小鬼，”狮子伤心地说。

paragraphs.en: “What makes you a coward?” asked Dorothy, looking at the great beast in wonder, for he was as big as a small horse.
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么是个胆小鬼呢？”多萝西好奇地问，看着这只大动物，它像一匹小马那么大。

paragraphs.en: “It’s a mystery,” replied the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “这是个秘密，”狮子回答。

paragraphs.en: “I suppose I was born that way.
paragraphs.cn: “我想我生来就是这样。”
