paragraphs.en: All the other animals in the forest naturally expect me to be brave, for the Lion is everywhere thought to be the King of Beasts.
paragraphs.cn: 森林里所有别的动物都觉得我应该很勇敢，因为大家总觉得狮子是动物之王。

paragraphs.en: I learned that if I roared very loudly every living thing was frightened and got out of my way.
paragraphs.cn: 我发现，只要我大声吼叫，所有的动物都会害怕，然后躲开我。

paragraphs.en: Whenever I’ve met a man I’ve been awfully scared; but I just roared at him, and he has always run away as fast as he could go.
paragraphs.cn: 每次我遇到人，我都特别害怕；但我只是冲他们吼叫，他们就总是跑得飞快。

paragraphs.en: If the elephants and the tigers and the bears had ever tried to fight me, I should have run myself—I’m such a coward; but just as soon as they hear me roar they all try to get away from me, and of course I let them go.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果大象、老虎和熊想和我打架，我肯定会自己先跑掉——我就是个胆小鬼；可是只要它们听到我吼叫，它们就都想跑开，我当然就让它们走了。”

paragraphs.en: “But that isn’t right.
paragraphs.cn: “可是这样不对啊。

paragraphs.en: The King of Beasts shouldn’t be a coward,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: 动物之王不应该是胆小鬼，”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “I know it,” returned the Lion, wiping a tear from his eye with the tip of his tail.
paragraphs.cn: “我知道，”狮子回答，用尾巴尖擦了擦眼泪。

paragraphs.en: “It is my great sorrow, and makes my life very unhappy.
paragraphs.cn: “这是我最大的烦恼，让我的生活很不开心。

paragraphs.en: But whenever there is danger, my heart begins to beat fast.”
paragraphs.cn: 可是每当有危险，我的心就跳得好快。”

paragraphs.en: “Perhaps you have heart disease,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “也许你得了心脏病，”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “It may be,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “可能吧，”狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “If you have,” continued the Tin Woodman, “you ought to be glad, for it proves you have a heart.
paragraphs.cn: “如果你有，”铁皮人接着说，“你应该高兴，因为这说明你有心脏啊。

paragraphs.en: For my part, I have no heart; so I cannot have heart disease.”
paragraphs.cn: 我呢，我没有心脏；所以我不会得心脏病。”

paragraphs.en: “Perhaps,” said the Lion thoughtfully, “if I had no heart I should not be a coward.”
paragraphs.cn: “也许，”狮子想了想说，“如果我没有心脏，我就不会是胆小鬼了。”

paragraphs.en: “Have you brains?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你有脑子吗？”稻草人问。

paragraphs.en: “I suppose so.
paragraphs.cn: “我想有吧。

paragraphs.en: I’ve never looked to see,” replied the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: 我从来没看过，”狮子回答。

paragraphs.en: “I am going to the Great Oz to ask him to give me some,” remarked the Scarecrow, “for my head is stuffed with straw.”
paragraphs.cn: “我要去见伟大的奥兹大王，请他给我一些，”稻草人说，“因为我的脑袋里塞满了稻草。”

paragraphs.en: “And I am going to ask him to give me a heart,” said the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “我呢，要去请他给我一颗心，”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “And I am going to ask him to send Toto and me back to Kansas,” added Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我呢，要去请他把托托和我送回堪萨斯，”多萝西补充道。

paragraphs.en: “Do you think Oz could give me courage?” asked the Cowardly Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “你觉得奥兹大王能给我勇气吗？”胆小的狮子问。

paragraphs.en: “Just as easily as he could give me brains,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “就像他能给我脑子一样容易，”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “Or give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “或者给我一颗心，”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “Or send me back to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “或者把我送回堪萨斯，”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “Then, if you don’t mind, I’ll go with you,” said the Lion, “for my life is simply unbearable without a bit of courage.”
paragraphs.cn: “那，如果你不介意，我就和你一起去吧，” 狮子说，“我的生活没有一点勇气，真是太难受了。”

paragraphs.en: “You will be very welcome,” answered Dorothy, “for you will help to keep away the other wild beasts.
paragraphs.cn: “你会很受欢迎的，” 多萝西回答，“因为你会帮我们赶走其他的野兽。

paragraphs.en: It seems to me they must be more cowardly than you are if they allow you to scare them so easily.”
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得呀，如果他们让你这么容易就吓跑了，那他们肯定比你还胆小呢。”

paragraphs.en: “They really are,” said the Lion, “but that doesn’t make me any braver, and as long as I know myself to be a coward I shall be unhappy.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们确实是这样，” 狮子说，“但这并不能让我变得更勇敢。只要觉得自己是个胆小鬼，我就不高兴。”

paragraphs.en: So once more the little company set off upon the journey, the Lion walking with stately strides at Dorothy’s side.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，这小队又一次出发了，狮子迈着大步，走在多萝西旁边。

paragraphs.en: Toto did not approve of this new comrade at first, for he could not forget how nearly he had been crushed between the Lion’s great jaws.
paragraphs.cn: 托托一开始不太喜欢这个新朋友，因为他忘不了自己差点被狮子的大嘴巴夹住。

paragraphs.en: But after a time he became more at ease, and presently Toto and the Cowardly Lion had grown to be good friends.
paragraphs.cn: 但过了一会儿，他放松了许多，很快，托托和胆小的狮子就成了好朋友。

paragraphs.en: During the rest of that day there was no other adventure to mar the peace of their journey.
paragraphs.cn: 那天剩下的时间里，他们的旅程很平静，没有再遇到其他事情。

paragraphs.en: Once, indeed, the Tin Woodman stepped upon a beetle that was crawling along the road, and killed the poor little thing.
paragraphs.cn: 有一次，铁皮人不小心踩到了一只在路上爬的小甲虫，把这个可怜的小东西踩死了。

paragraphs.en: This made the Tin Woodman very unhappy, for he was always careful not to hurt any living creature; and as he walked along he wept several tears of sorrow and regret.
paragraphs.cn: 这让铁皮人很不开心，因为他总是很小心，不伤害任何小动物；他一边走一边流下了伤心的眼泪。

paragraphs.en: These tears ran slowly down his face and over the hinges of his jaw, and there they rusted.
paragraphs.cn: 这些眼泪慢慢地流过他的脸，流到他下巴的关节上，然后，关节就生锈了。

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy presently asked him a question the Tin Woodman could not open his mouth, for his jaws were tightly rusted together.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西很快问他一个问题时，铁皮人却张不开嘴了，因为他的下巴关节都锈住了。

paragraphs.en: He became greatly frightened at this and made many motions to Dorothy to relieve him, but she could not understand.
paragraphs.cn: 他吓坏了，不停地对多萝西比划，想让她帮他，但多萝西不明白。

paragraphs.en: The Lion was also puzzled to know what was wrong.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子也不知道是怎么回事，感到很困惑。

paragraphs.en: But the Scarecrow seized the oil-can from Dorothy’s basket and oiled the Woodman’s jaws, so that after a few moments he could talk as well as before.
paragraphs.cn: 但稻草人从多萝西的篮子里拿过油壶，给铁皮人的下巴关节上油，过了一会儿，他就能像以前一样说话了。

paragraphs.en: “This will serve me a lesson,” said he, “to look where I step.
paragraphs.cn: “这给我上了一课，” 他说，“走路要看脚下。

paragraphs.en: For if I should kill another bug or beetle I should surely cry again, and crying rusts my jaws so that I cannot speak.”
paragraphs.cn: 因为如果我又踩死别的虫子或甲虫，我肯定还会哭，一哭下巴就会生锈，那样我就说不了话了。”

paragraphs.en: Thereafter he walked very carefully, with his eyes on the road, and when he saw a tiny ant toiling by he would step over it, so as not to harm it.
paragraphs.cn: 从那以后，他走路非常小心，眼睛一直看着路。当他看到一只小蚂蚁在旁边忙碌时，他就会跨过去，不伤害它。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman knew very well he had no heart, and therefore he took great care never to be cruel or unkind to anything.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人很清楚自己没有心，所以他非常小心，从不对任何东西坏坏的。

paragraphs.en: “You people with hearts,” he said, “have something to guide you, and need never do wrong; but I have no heart, and so I must be very careful.
paragraphs.cn: “你们这些有心的人啊，” 他说，“有东西指引你们，永远不会做错事；但我没有心，所以我必须非常小心。

paragraphs.en: When Oz gives me a heart of course I needn’t mind so much.”
paragraphs.cn: 等奥兹大王给了我一颗心，我就不用那么小心了。”

chapters.title_en: The Journey to the Great Oz

paragraphs.en: They were obliged to camp out that night under a large tree in the forest, for there were no houses near.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，他们只能在森林里的一棵大树下露营，因为附近没有房子。

paragraphs.en: The tree made a good, thick covering to protect them from the dew, and the Tin Woodman chopped a great pile of wood with his axe and Dorothy built a splendid fire that warmed her and made her feel less lonely.
paragraphs.cn: 大树提供了厚厚的遮蔽，保护他们不被露水打湿，铁皮人用他的斧头砍了一大堆木头，多萝西生了一个很棒的火堆，火堆让她暖和起来，也让她感觉不那么孤单了。

paragraphs.en: She and Toto ate the last of their bread, and now she did not know what they would do for breakfast.
paragraphs.cn: 她和托托吃完了最后一点面包，现在她不知道他们早上要吃什么了。

paragraphs.en: “If you wish,” said the Lion, “I will go into the forest and kill a deer for you.
paragraphs.cn: “如果你想的话，” 狮子说，“我可以进森林里给你打一只鹿。

paragraphs.en: You can roast it by the fire, since your tastes are so peculiar that you prefer cooked food, and then you will have a very good breakfast.”
paragraphs.cn: 你可以在火边烤着吃，因为你的口味很特别，喜欢吃煮熟的食物，那样你就有很棒的早餐了。”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t!
Please don’t,” begged the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: 求求你，别那样！” 铁皮人央求道。

paragraphs.en: “I should certainly weep if you killed a poor deer, and then my jaws would rust again.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果你杀了那可怜的鹿，我一定会哭的，然后我的下巴又会生锈了。”

paragraphs.en: But the Lion went away into the forest and found his own supper, and no one ever knew what it was, for he didn’t mention it.
paragraphs.cn: 但是狮子自己进了森林，找到了他的晚饭，没人知道他吃了什么，因为他没说。

paragraphs.en: And the Scarecrow found a tree full of nuts and filled Dorothy’s basket with them, so that she would not be hungry for a long time.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 找到一棵长满坚果的树，把坚果装满 多萝西 的篮子，这样她就不会饿肚子很久了。

paragraphs.en: She thought this was very kind and thoughtful of the Scarecrow, but she laughed heartily at the awkward way in which the poor creature picked up the nuts.
paragraphs.cn: 她觉得 稻草人 真是太好心了，但她看到这个小家伙笨手笨脚地捡坚果时，忍不住哈哈大笑起来。

paragraphs.en: His padded hands were so clumsy and the nuts were so small that he dropped almost as many as he put in the basket.
paragraphs.cn: 他的肉乎乎的手太笨拙了，坚果又那么小，他掉到地上的坚果和放进篮子的差不多一样多。

paragraphs.en: But the Scarecrow did not mind how long it took him to fill the basket, for it enabled him to keep away from the fire, as he feared a spark might get into his straw and burn him up.
paragraphs.cn: 但是 稻草人 不在乎要多久才能把篮子装满，因为这样他就可以离火远一点，他怕火星会掉进他的草里把他烧着了。

paragraphs.en: So he kept a good distance away from the flames, and only came near to cover Dorothy with dry leaves when she lay down to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他离火焰远远的，只有 多萝西 躺下睡觉时，他才走近一点，用干树叶盖住她。

paragraphs.en: These kept her very snug and warm, and she slept soundly until morning.
paragraphs.cn: 这些树叶让她很舒服很暖和，她一直睡到天亮。

paragraphs.en: When it was daylight, the girl bathed her face in a little rippling brook, and soon after they all started toward the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 天亮了，小女孩在小溪里洗了脸，很快，他们就一起朝着 翡翠城 走去。

paragraphs.en: This was to be an eventful day for the travelers.
paragraphs.cn: 对这些旅行者来说，这一天会有很多特别的事发生。

paragraphs.en: They had hardly been walking an hour when they saw before them a great ditch that crossed the road and divided the forest as far as they could see on either side.
paragraphs.cn: 他们刚走了不到一个小时，就看到前面有一条大沟，这条沟穿过马路，把森林分成了两半，一眼望不到头。

paragraphs.en: It was a very wide ditch, and when they crept up to the edge and looked into it they could see it was also very deep, and there were many big, jagged rocks at the bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 这条沟很宽，当他们爬到沟边往下看时，发现它也很深，底部还有很多大块的尖石头。

paragraphs.en: The sides were so steep that none of them could climb down, and for a moment it seemed that their journey must end.
paragraphs.cn: 沟的两边非常陡峭，他们谁也下不去，一时间，他们觉得自己的旅程要到此为止了。

paragraphs.en: “What shall we do?” asked Dorothy despairingly.
paragraphs.cn: “我们该怎么办？” 多萝西 伤心地问。

paragraphs.en: “I haven’t the faintest idea,” said the Tin Woodman, and the Lion shook his shaggy mane and looked thoughtful.
paragraphs.cn: “我一点办法都没有。” 铁皮人 说，狮子 甩了甩他那乱糟糟的鬃毛，看起来在想办法。

paragraphs.en: But the Scarecrow said, “We cannot fly, that is certain.
paragraphs.cn: 但是 稻草人 说：“我们不能飞，这是肯定的。

paragraphs.en: Neither can we climb down into this great ditch.
paragraphs.cn: 我们也不能爬进这条大沟。

paragraphs.en: Therefore, if we cannot jump over it, we must stop where we are.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以，如果我们跳不过去，我们就只能待在这里了。”

paragraphs.en: “I think I could jump over it,” said the Cowardly Lion, after measuring the distance carefully in his mind.
paragraphs.cn: “我想我能跳过去。” 胆小的狮子 说，他在心里仔细地估量了一下距离。

paragraphs.en: “Then we are all right,” answered the Scarecrow, “for you can carry us all over on your back, one at a time.”
paragraphs.cn: “那我们就没事了！” 稻草人 回答，“因为你可以一个一个地把我们都背过去。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll try it,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，我试试看。” 狮子 说。

paragraphs.en: “Who will go first?”
paragraphs.cn: “谁先来？”

paragraphs.en: “I will,” declared the Scarecrow, “for, if you found that you could not jump over the gulf, Dorothy would be killed, or the Tin Woodman badly dented on the rocks below.
paragraphs.cn: “我来！” 稻草人 说，“因为如果你跳不过去，多萝西 可能会死掉，或者 铁皮人 会在下面的石头上摔坏。”

paragraphs.en: But if I am on your back it will not matter so much, for the fall would not hurt me at all.”
paragraphs.cn: 但是如果我在你的背上，就没那么要紧了，因为摔下去一点都不会伤到我。”

paragraphs.en: “I am terribly afraid of falling, myself,” said the Cowardly Lion, “but I suppose there is nothing to do but try it.
paragraphs.cn: “我自己也很怕摔倒。” 胆小的狮子 说，“但我想除了试试看，也没别的办法了。

paragraphs.en: So get on my back and we will make the attempt.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以，到我背上来，我们去试试看。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow sat upon the Lion’s back, and the big beast walked to the edge of the gulf and crouched down.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 坐在 狮子 的背上，这只大野兽走到深沟边缘，然后蹲了下来。

paragraphs.en: “Why don’t you run and jump?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么不跑起来跳呢？” 稻草人 问。

paragraphs.en: “Because that isn’t the way we Lions do these things,” he replied.
paragraphs.cn: “因为我们狮子不是那样做的。” 他回答说。

paragraphs.en: Then giving a great spring, he shot through the air and landed safely on the other side.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他猛地一跳，飞过空中，安全地落在了另一边。

paragraphs.en: They were all greatly pleased to see how easily he did it, and after the Scarecrow had got down from his back the Lion sprang across the ditch again.
paragraphs.cn: 看到他跳得这么轻松，大家都很高兴。稻草人 从他背上下来后，狮子 又跳回了沟的这边。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy thought she would go next; so she took Toto in her arms and climbed on the Lion’s back, holding tightly to his mane with one hand.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 觉得她该下一个过去了；所以她抱起 托托，爬到 狮子 的背上，一只手紧紧抓住他的鬃毛。

paragraphs.en: The next moment it seemed as if she were flying through the air; and then, before she had time to think about it, she was safe on the other side.
paragraphs.cn: 下一刻，她好像在空中飞。还没来得及想，她就安全地到了对面。

paragraphs.en: The Lion went back a third time and got the Tin Woodman, and then they all sat down for a few moments to give the beast a chance to rest, for his great leaps had made his breath short, and he panted like a big dog that has been running too long.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子又回去了一次，把铁皮人也带来了。然后他们都坐下来休息了一会儿，让那只动物歇歇脚。因为它跳得太猛了，喘不过气，就像跑了很久的大狗一样呼哧呼哧地喘气。

paragraphs.en: They found the forest very thick on this side, and it looked dark and gloomy.
paragraphs.cn: 他们发现这边的森林很密，看起来又黑又暗。

paragraphs.en: After the Lion had rested they started along the road of yellow brick, silently wondering, each in his own mind, if ever they would come to the end of the woods and reach the bright sunshine again.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子休息好了，他们就沿着黄砖路往前走。大家心里都在默默地想，他们什么时候才能走出这片森林，再次看到明亮的阳光呢？

paragraphs.en: To add to their discomfort, they soon heard strange noises in the depths of the forest, and the Lion whispered to them that it was in this part of the country that the Kalidahs lived.
paragraphs.cn: 更让他们不舒服的是，他们很快就听到森林深处传来奇怪的声音。狮子小声告诉他们，卡力达就住在这个地方。

paragraphs.en: “What are the Kalidahs?” asked the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “卡力达是什么呀？”小女孩问。

paragraphs.en: “They are monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers,” replied the Lion, “and with claws so long and sharp that they could tear me in two as easily as I could kill Toto.
paragraphs.cn: “它们是可怕的怪兽，身子像熊，头像老虎，”狮子回答，“它们的爪子又长又尖，能把我撕成两半，就像我能杀死托托一样容易。

paragraphs.en: I’m terribly afraid of the Kalidahs.”
paragraphs.cn: 我特别害怕卡力达。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not surprised that you are,” returned Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “你害怕一点也不奇怪，”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “They must be dreadful beasts.”
paragraphs.cn: “它们一定是可怕的怪兽。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion was about to reply when suddenly they came to another gulf across the road.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子正要回答，突然他们又来到了一条横在路上的大沟。

paragraphs.en: But this one was so broad and deep that the Lion knew at once he could not leap across it.
paragraphs.cn: 可这条沟又宽又深，狮子一看就知道自己跳不过去。

paragraphs.en: So they sat down to consider what they should do, and after serious thought the Scarecrow said:
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们坐下来，想想该怎么办。仔细想了想，稻草人说：

paragraphs.en: “Here is a great tree, standing close to the ditch.
paragraphs.cn: “这儿有一棵大树，就长在沟边上。

paragraphs.en: If the Tin Woodman can chop it down, so that it will fall to the other side, we can walk across it easily.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果铁皮人能把它砍倒，让它倒到沟对面去，我们就能轻松地走过去了。”

paragraphs.en: “That is a first-rate idea,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “这是个好主意！”狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “One would almost suspect you had brains in your head, instead of straw.”
paragraphs.cn: “你脑袋里简直像是长了脑子，而不是稻草！”

paragraphs.en: The Woodman set to work at once, and so sharp was his axe that the tree was soon chopped nearly through.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人立刻开始干活。它的斧头很锋利，很快就把树砍得差不多了。

paragraphs.en: Then the Lion put his strong front legs against the tree and pushed with all his might, and slowly the big tree tipped and fell with a crash across the ditch, with its top branches on the other side.
paragraphs.cn: 然后狮子用它强壮的前腿顶住树，使劲一推。大树慢慢地倾斜，轰隆一声倒了下去，横在了沟上，树顶的枝条也到了对面。

paragraphs.en: They had just started to cross this queer bridge when a sharp growl made them all look up, and to their horror they saw running toward them two great beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers.
paragraphs.cn: 他们刚开始过这座奇怪的桥，就听到一声尖锐的吼叫，所有人都抬起头。让他们害怕的是，他们看到两只怪兽正朝他们跑来，它们的身体像熊，头像老虎。

paragraphs.en: “They are the Kalidahs!” said the Cowardly Lion, beginning to tremble.
paragraphs.cn: “它们是卡力达！”胆小的狮子说着，身体开始发抖。

paragraphs.en: “Quick!” cried the Scarecrow. “Let us cross over.”
paragraphs.cn: “快！”稻草人大喊，“我们快过去！”

paragraphs.en: So Dorothy went first, holding Toto in her arms, the Tin Woodman followed, and the Scarecrow came next.
paragraphs.cn: 于是多萝西抱着托托先过去了，铁皮人跟着，然后是稻草人。

paragraphs.en: The Lion, although he was certainly afraid, turned to face the Kalidahs, and then he gave so loud and terrible a roar that Dorothy screamed and the Scarecrow fell over backward, while even the fierce beasts stopped short and looked at him in surprise.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子虽然也很害怕，但他还是转过身，面对着卡力达，然后发出了震耳欲聋的可怕吼声。多萝西吓得尖叫起来，稻草人也向后摔倒了。就连那些凶猛的怪兽也停了下来，惊讶地看着他。

paragraphs.en: But, seeing they were bigger than the Lion, and remembering that there were two of them and only one of him, the Kalidahs again rushed forward, and the Lion crossed over the tree and turned to see what they would do next.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，那些怪兽看到它们比狮子还大，又想到它们有两只，而它只有一只，于是卡力达又冲了过来。狮子已经过了树桥，转过身想看看它们接下来会做什么。

paragraphs.en: Without stopping an instant the fierce beasts also began to cross the tree.
paragraphs.cn: 那些凶猛的怪兽一点也没停，也开始过那棵树了。

paragraphs.en: And the Lion said to Dorothy:
paragraphs.cn: 狮子对多萝西说：

paragraphs.en: “We are lost, for they will surely tear us to pieces with their sharp claws.
paragraphs.cn: “我们完蛋了，它们一定会用锋利的爪子把我们撕成碎片的。”

paragraphs.en: But stand close behind me, and I will fight them as long as I am alive.”
paragraphs.cn: “但是，你站到我后面来，只要我还活着，我就会和它们打！”

paragraphs.en: “Wait a minute!” called the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “等一下！”稻草人大喊。

paragraphs.en: He had been thinking what was best to be done, and now he asked the Woodman to chop away the end of the tree that rested on their side of the ditch.
paragraphs.cn: 他一直在想办法。他请 铁皮人 砍掉伸到沟里的那段树。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman began to use his axe at once, and, just as the two Kalidahs were nearly across, the tree fell with a crash into the gulf, carrying the ugly, snarling brutes with it, and both were dashed to pieces on the sharp rocks at the bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 立刻拿起斧头砍树。就在两只 卡力达 快要爬过来时，大树“轰”地一声倒进了深渊，把那些又丑又凶的 卡力达 也带了下去。它们撞到下面的尖石头上，摔得粉碎。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said the Cowardly Lion, drawing a long breath of relief, “I see we are going to live a little while longer, and I am glad of it, for it must be a very uncomfortable thing not to be alive.
paragraphs.cn: “呼，” 胆小的狮子 松了口气说，“看来我们还能多活一会儿。我真高兴，因为死了肯定很难受。”

paragraphs.en: Those creatures frightened me so badly that my heart is beating yet.”
paragraphs.cn: 那些东西把我吓坏了，我的心还在扑通扑通地跳呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Ah,” said the Tin Woodman sadly, “I wish I had a heart to beat.”
paragraphs.cn: “唉，” 铁皮人 伤心地说，“我真希望我有一颗会跳的心。”

paragraphs.en: This adventure made the travelers more anxious than ever to get out of the forest, and they walked so fast that Dorothy became tired, and had to ride on the Lion’s back.
paragraphs.cn: 这次惊险的事让大家更想快点走出森林。他们走得很快，多萝西 都累了，只好骑在 狮子 的背上。

paragraphs.en: To their great joy the trees became thinner the farther they advanced, and in the afternoon they suddenly came upon a broad river, flowing swiftly just before them.
paragraphs.cn: 让他们高兴的是，越往前走，树木越稀疏了。下午，他们突然看到一条宽宽的河，河水在他们面前哗哗地流淌。

paragraphs.en: On the other side of the water they could see the road of yellow brick running through a beautiful country, with green meadows dotted with bright flowers and all the road bordered with trees hanging full of delicious fruits.
paragraphs.cn: 在河的另一边，他们看到了黄砖路。黄砖路穿过一片美丽的土地，那里有绿油油的草地，开满了鲜花，路两边都长满了挂着甜美果子的树。

paragraphs.en: They were greatly pleased to see this delightful country before them.
paragraphs.cn: 看到眼前这片美丽的地方，他们非常开心。

paragraphs.en: “How shall we cross the river?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我们怎么过河呢？” 多萝西 问道。

paragraphs.en: “That is easily done,” replied the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “这很容易！” 稻草人 回答。

paragraphs.en: “The Tin Woodman must build us a raft, so we can float to the other side.”
paragraphs.cn: “铁皮人 必须给我们造一个木筏，这样我们就能漂到对面去了。”

paragraphs.en: So the Woodman took his axe and began to chop down small trees to make a raft, and while he was busy at this the Scarecrow found on the riverbank a tree full of fine fruit.
paragraphs.cn: 于是 铁皮人 拿起斧头，开始砍小树来做木筏。就在他忙着的时候，稻草人 在河岸边找到了一棵结满了美味果子的树。

paragraphs.en: This pleased Dorothy, who had eaten nothing but nuts all day, and she made a hearty meal of the ripe fruit.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 一整天只吃了坚果，这让她很高兴，她饱饱地吃了一顿成熟的果子。

paragraphs.en: But it takes time to make a raft, even when one is as industrious and untiring as the Tin Woodman, and when night came the work was not done.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，造木筏需要时间，即使像 铁皮人 那样勤劳、不知疲倦的人也一样。晚上到了，木筏还没造好。

paragraphs.en: So they found a cozy place under the trees where they slept well until the morning; and Dorothy dreamed of the Emerald City, and of the good Wizard Oz, who would soon send her back to her own home again.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们在树下找了个舒服的地方，一直睡到天亮。多萝西 梦到了 翡翠城，还有善良的巫师 奥兹大王，巫师很快就会送她回家。

paragraphs.en: Our little party of travelers awakened the next morning refreshed and full of hope, and Dorothy breakfasted like a princess off peaches and plums from the trees beside the river.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，小小的旅行队伍醒来，精神饱满，充满希望。多萝西 像公主一样，吃了河边树上的桃子和李子当早餐。

paragraphs.en: Behind them was the dark forest they had passed safely through, although they had suffered many discouragements; but before them was a lovely, sunny country that seemed to beckon them on to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 他们身后是他们安全穿过的黑森林，虽然经历了很多不开心的事情。但眼前却是一片可爱、阳光明媚的土地，仿佛在招手让他们去 翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: To be sure, the broad river now cut them off from this beautiful land.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，这条宽阔的河流把他们和这片美丽的土地隔开了。

paragraphs.en: But the raft was nearly done, and after the Tin Woodman had cut a few more logs and fastened them together with wooden pins, they were ready to start.
paragraphs.cn: 但木筏快要造好了。铁皮人 再砍几根木头，用木钉把它们固定在一起后，他们就可以出发了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy sat down in the middle of the raft and held Toto in her arms.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 坐在木筏中间，抱着 托托。

paragraphs.en: When the Cowardly Lion stepped upon the raft it tipped badly, for he was big and heavy; but the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman stood upon the other end to steady it, and they had long poles in their hands to push the raft through the water.
paragraphs.cn: 当 胆小的狮子 走上木筏时，木筏晃得很厉害，因为他又大又重。但 稻草人 和 铁皮人 站在另一头来稳住木筏，他们手里拿着长长的杆子，用来在水里推木筏。

paragraphs.en: They got along quite well at first, but when they reached the middle of the river the swift current swept the raft downstream, farther and farther away from the road of yellow brick.
paragraphs.cn: 一开始他们走得很顺利，但当他们到了河中间时，湍急的水流把木筏冲向下游，离黄砖路越来越远了。

paragraphs.en: And the water grew so deep that the long poles would not touch the bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 河水变得很深，长杆子都够不着底了。

paragraphs.en: “This is bad,” said the Tin Woodman, “for if we cannot get to the land we shall be carried into the country of the Wicked Witch of the West, and she will enchant us and make us her slaves.”
paragraphs.cn: “这可糟了，” 铁皮人 说，“要是我们到不了岸边，就会被冲到 西方坏女巫 的国家，她会施魔法把我们变成她的奴隶。”

paragraphs.en: “And then I should get no brains,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “那我可就得不到脑子了！” 稻草人 说。

paragraphs.en: “And I should get no courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “那我可就得不到勇气了！” 胆小的狮子 说。

paragraphs.en: “And I should get no heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “那我可就得不到心了！” 铁皮人 说。

paragraphs.en: “And I should never get back to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “那我永远都回不了 堪萨斯 了！” 多萝西 说。

paragraphs.en: “We must certainly get to the Emerald City if we can,” the Scarecrow continued, and he pushed so hard on his long pole that it stuck fast in the mud at the bottom of the river.
paragraphs.cn: “我们一定要想办法到 翡翠城 去，” 稻草人 接着说。他用力地推着长杆子，结果杆子牢牢地卡在了河底的泥巴里。

paragraphs.en: Then, before he could pull it out again—or let go—the raft was swept away, and the poor Scarecrow was left clinging to the pole in the middle of the river.
paragraphs.cn: 他还没来得及把杆子拔出来，木筏就被水冲走了。可怜的 稻草人 只好紧紧抱着杆子，孤零零地留在河中间。

paragraphs.en: “Good-bye!” he called after them, and they were very sorry to leave him.
paragraphs.cn: “再见！”他大声喊着。大家都很舍不得他。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, the Tin Woodman began to cry, but fortunately remembered that he might rust, and so dried his tears on Dorothy’s apron.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 真的开始哭了，但他想起自己可能会生锈，就赶紧用 多萝西 的围裙擦干了眼泪。

paragraphs.en: Of course this was a bad thing for the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，这对 稻草人 来说是很糟糕的事。

paragraphs.en: “I am now worse off than when I first met Dorothy,” he thought.
paragraphs.cn: “我现在比第一次遇到 多萝西 的时候更糟了。”他想。

paragraphs.en: “Then, I was stuck on a pole in a cornfield, where I could make-believe scare the crows, at any rate.
paragraphs.cn: “那时，我插在玉米地里的杆子上，至少还能假装吓唬乌鸦。

paragraphs.en: But surely there is no use for a Scarecrow stuck on a pole in the middle of a river.
paragraphs.cn: 但一个插在河中央杆子上的 稻草人，肯定没用了。

paragraphs.en: I am afraid I shall never have any brains, after all!”
paragraphs.cn: 我恐怕永远也得不到脑子了！”

paragraphs.en: Down the stream the raft floated, and the poor Scarecrow was left far behind.
paragraphs.cn: 木筏顺着水流漂走了，可怜的 稻草人 被远远地落下了。

paragraphs.en: Then the Lion said:
paragraphs.cn: 这时 狮子 说：

paragraphs.en: “Something must be done to save us.
paragraphs.cn: “我们得想办法救大家。”

paragraphs.en: I think I can swim to the shore and pull the raft after me, if you will only hold fast to the tip of my tail.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想我觉得我能游到岸边，把木筏拉过来，只要你们紧紧抓住我的尾巴尖。”

paragraphs.en: So he sprang into the water, and the Tin Woodman caught fast hold of his tail.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他跳进水里，铁皮人 赶紧抓住了他的尾巴。

paragraphs.en: Then the Lion began to swim with all his might toward the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 接着 狮子 用尽全身力气，向岸边游去。

paragraphs.en: It was hard work, although he was so big; but by and by they were drawn out of the current, and then Dorothy took the Tin Woodman’s long pole and helped push the raft to the land.
paragraphs.cn: 这可真费力啊，虽然他很大。但是很快，他们就被带出了急流。然后 多萝西 拿起 铁皮人 的长杆，帮忙把木筏推到了岸上。

paragraphs.en: They were all tired out when they reached the shore at last and stepped off upon the pretty green grass, and they also knew that the stream had carried them a long way past the road of yellow brick that led to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 他们终于到了岸边，踩在漂亮的绿草地上，都累坏了。他们也知道，水流把他们带离了通往 翡翠城 的黄色砖路很远了。

paragraphs.en: “What shall we do now?” asked the Tin Woodman, as the Lion lay down on the grass to let the sun dry him.
paragraphs.cn: “我们现在该怎么办呢？” 铁皮人 问。这时 狮子 正躺在草地上晒太阳，想让身体变干。

paragraphs.en: “We must get back to the road, in some way,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我们必须想办法回到路上。” 多萝西 说道。

paragraphs.en: “The best plan will be to walk along the riverbank until we come to the road again,” remarked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “最好的办法是沿着河岸走，直到我们回到那条路上。” 狮子 说。

paragraphs.en: So, when they were rested, Dorothy picked up her basket and they started along the grassy bank, to the road from which the river had carried them.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，他们休息好后，多萝西 拿起她的篮子，大家沿着长满草的河岸走，回到河水冲走他们的那条路上。

paragraphs.en: It was a lovely country, with plenty of flowers and fruit trees and sunshine to cheer them, and had they not felt so sorry for the poor Scarecrow, they could have been very happy.
paragraphs.cn: 那是个美丽的地方，有很多鲜花、果树和阳光，让大家很开心。如果不是为可怜的 稻草人 感到难过，他们本来会很开心的。

paragraphs.en: They walked along as fast as they could, Dorothy only stopping once to pick a beautiful flower; and after a time the Tin Woodman cried out: “Look!”
paragraphs.cn: 他们尽可能快地往前走，多萝西 只停下来一次去摘了一朵漂亮的花。过了一会儿，铁皮人 突然喊道：“看！”

paragraphs.en: Then they all looked at the river and saw the Scarecrow perched upon his pole in the middle of the water, looking very lonely and sad.
paragraphs.cn: 于是大家看向河里，看到 稻草人 孤零零地站在水中央的杆子上，看起来很孤独也很伤心。

paragraphs.en: “What can we do to save him?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我们能做些什么来救他呢？” 多萝西 问。

paragraphs.en: The Lion and the Woodman both shook their heads, for they did not know.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子 和 铁皮人 都摇了摇头，因为他们都不知道。

paragraphs.en: So they sat down upon the bank and gazed wistfully at the Scarecrow until a Stork flew by, who, upon seeing them, stopped to rest at the water’s edge.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们坐在河岸上，看着 稻草人，心里很着急。直到一只 鹳鸟 飞过，它看到他们后，就停下来在水边休息。

paragraphs.en: “Who are you and where are you going?” asked the Stork.
paragraphs.cn: “你们是谁？要去哪里啊？” 鹳鸟 问。

paragraphs.en: “I am Dorothy,” answered the girl, “and these are my friends, the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion; and we are going to the Emerald City.”
paragraphs.cn: “我是 多萝西，”女孩回答，“这些是我的朋友，铁皮人 和 胆小的狮子。我们要去 翡翠城。”

paragraphs.en: “This isn’t the road,” said the Stork, as she twisted her long neck and looked sharply at the queer party.
paragraphs.cn: “这不是那条路啊。” 鹳鸟 说，它扭着长长的脖子，好奇地看着这群奇怪的朋友们。

paragraphs.en: “I know it,” returned Dorothy, “but we have lost the Scarecrow, and are wondering how we shall get him again.”
paragraphs.cn: “我知道。” 多萝西 回答，“但是我们把 稻草人 弄丢了，不知道怎么把他找回来。”

paragraphs.en: “Where is he?” asked the Stork.
paragraphs.cn: “他在哪儿？” 鹳鸟问。

paragraphs.en: “Over there in the river,” answered the little girl.
paragraphs.cn: “在那边的河里呢，” 小女孩回答。

paragraphs.en: “If he wasn’t so big and heavy I would get him for you,” remarked the Stork.
paragraphs.cn: “要是他没那么大那么重，我就帮你把他拿回来，” 鹳鸟说。

paragraphs.en: “He isn’t heavy a bit,” said Dorothy eagerly, “for he is stuffed with straw; and if you will bring him back to us, we shall thank you ever and ever so much.”
paragraphs.cn: “他一点也不重啊！” 多萝西着急地说，“他肚子里全是稻草！你要是把他带回来，我们会非常非常感谢你的！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll try,” said the Stork, “but if I find he is too heavy to carry I shall have to drop him in the river again.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，我试试看，” 鹳鸟说，“不过要是他太重了，我拿不动，就只能再把他扔回河里啦。”

paragraphs.en: So the big bird flew into the air and over the water till she came to where the Scarecrow was perched upon his pole.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，大鸟飞上天空，飞过水面，一直飞到 稻草人停在他柱子上的地方。

paragraphs.en: Then the Stork with her great claws grabbed the Scarecrow by the arm and carried him up into the air and back to the bank, where Dorothy and the Lion and the Tin Woodman and Toto were sitting.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，鹳鸟用她的大爪子抓住了 稻草人的胳膊，把他带到空中，又带回河岸边，多萝西、狮子、铁皮人和 托托都在那儿坐着呢。

paragraphs.en: When the Scarecrow found himself among his friends again, he was so happy that he hugged them all, even the Lion and Toto; and as they walked along he sang “Tol-de-ri-de-oh!” at every step, he felt so gay.
paragraphs.cn: 当 稻草人又回到了朋友们身边，他可高兴啦！他抱了抱所有人，连 狮子和 托托也抱了。他们边走边唱着“Tol-de-ri-de-oh!”，每走一步都唱，他真是太开心了。

paragraphs.en: “I was afraid I should have to stay in the river forever,” he said, “but the kind Stork saved me, and if I ever get any brains I shall find the Stork again and do her some kindness in return.”
paragraphs.cn: “我刚才还以为我得永远待在河里了呢，”他说，“但是好心的 鹳鸟救了我。如果我以后变聪明了，我一定会再找到 鹳鸟，好好报答她！”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right,” said the Stork, who was flying along beside them.
paragraphs.cn: “没关系啦，” 鹳鸟在他们旁边飞着说。

paragraphs.en: “I always like to help anyone in trouble.
paragraphs.cn: “我总是喜欢帮助遇到麻烦的人。”

paragraphs.en: But I must go now, for my babies are waiting in the nest for me.
paragraphs.cn: “不过我得走了，我的宝宝们还在窝里等我呢。”

paragraphs.en: I hope you will find the Emerald City and that Oz will help you.”
paragraphs.cn: “我希望你能找到 翡翠城，也希望 奥兹大王会帮助你。”

paragraphs.en: “Thank you,” replied Dorothy, and then the kind Stork flew into the air and was soon out of sight.
paragraphs.cn: “谢谢你！” 多萝西回答。接着，好心的 鹳鸟飞上了天，很快就不见了。

paragraphs.en: They walked along listening to the singing of the brightly colored birds and looking at the lovely flowers which now became so thick that the ground was carpeted with them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们继续往前走，听着五颜六色的鸟儿唱歌，看着漂亮的花朵。花儿越来越多，把地面都铺满了，像地毯一样。

paragraphs.en: There were big yellow and white and blue and purple blossoms, besides great clusters of scarlet poppies, which were so brilliant in color they almost dazzled Dorothy’s eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 那里有大朵的黄色、白色、蓝色和紫色花朵，还有一大丛一大丛火红色的罂粟花。这些花儿颜色鲜艳极了，都快把 多萝西的眼睛闪花了。

paragraphs.en: “Aren’t they beautiful?” the girl asked, as she breathed in the spicy scent of the bright flowers.
paragraphs.cn: “它们是不是很美呀？”女孩闻着鲜花的香味问道。

paragraphs.en: “I suppose so,” answered the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我想是吧，” 稻草人回答。

paragraphs.en: “When I have brains, I shall probably like them better.”
paragraphs.cn: “等我有了大脑，我可能就会更喜欢它们了。”

paragraphs.en: “If I only had a heart, I should love them,” added the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “要是我有一颗心，我就会爱上它们了，” 铁皮人补充道。

paragraphs.en: “I always did like flowers,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “我一直都喜欢花，” 狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “They seem so helpless and frail.
paragraphs.cn: “它们看起来好柔弱，需要人保护。”

paragraphs.en: But there are none in the forest so bright as these.”
paragraphs.cn: “不过森林里没有这么鲜艳的花。”

paragraphs.en: They now came upon more and more of the big scarlet poppies, and fewer and fewer of the other flowers; and soon they found themselves in the midst of a great meadow of poppies.
paragraphs.cn: 他们现在看到了越来越多的火红色大罂粟花，其他的花却越来越少了。很快，他们就来到了一大片罂粟花海里。

paragraphs.en: Now it is well known that when there are many of these flowers together their odor is so powerful that anyone who breathes it falls asleep, and if the sleeper is not carried away from the scent of the flowers, he sleeps on and on forever.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都知道，如果这些花开得很多，它们的气味就会很浓，闻到的人都会睡着。要是睡着的人没有被带离花丛，他就会一直睡下去，永远醒不过来。

paragraphs.en: But Dorothy did not know this, nor could she get away from the bright red flowers that were everywhere about; so presently her eyes grew heavy and she felt she must sit down to rest and to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 但是 多萝西不知道这件事，她也无法离开那些到处都是的鲜红花朵。于是，她的眼睛越来越重，觉得她必须坐下来休息睡觉了。

paragraphs.en: But the Tin Woodman would not let her do this.
paragraphs.cn: 但是 铁皮人不让她这么做。

paragraphs.en: “We must hurry and get back to the road of yellow brick before dark,” he said; and the Scarecrow agreed with him.
paragraphs.cn: “我们得赶紧在天黑前回到黄砖路上去！”他说。稻草人也同意了他的话。

paragraphs.en: So they kept walking until Dorothy could stand no longer.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们继续走，直到 多萝西再也站不住了。

paragraphs.en: Her eyes closed in spite of herself and she forgot where she was and fell among the poppies, fast asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 她不由自主地闭上了眼睛，忘了自己在哪里，倒在了罂粟花丛中，睡着了。

paragraphs.en: “What shall we do?” asked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “我们该怎么办？” 铁皮人问。

paragraphs.en: “If we leave her here she will die,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “如果我们把她留在这儿，她会死的。” 狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “The smell of the flowers is killing us all.
paragraphs.cn: “这些花的味道快把我们都熏倒了。

paragraphs.en: I myself can scarcely keep my eyes open, and the dog is asleep already.”
paragraphs.cn: 我自己都睁不开眼睛了，小狗也睡着了。”

paragraphs.en: It was true; Toto had fallen down beside his little mistress.
paragraphs.cn: 真的，托托已经倒在他小主人身边了。

paragraphs.en: But the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, not being made of flesh, were not troubled by the scent of the flowers.
paragraphs.cn: 但稻草人和铁皮人不是肉做的，所以不怕花香。

paragraphs.en: “Run fast,” said the Scarecrow to the Lion, “and get out of this deadly flower bed as soon as you can.
paragraphs.cn: “快跑，” 稻草人对狮子说，“尽快离开这个危险的花丛。

paragraphs.en: We will bring the little girl with us, but if you should fall asleep you are too big to be carried.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们会带小女孩走，但如果你睡着了，你太大了，我们可抬不动你。”

paragraphs.en: So the Lion aroused himself and bounded forward as fast as he could go.
paragraphs.cn: 于是狮子振作起来，尽力往前跑。

paragraphs.en: In a moment he was out of sight.
paragraphs.cn: 一会儿工夫，他就看不见了。

paragraphs.en: “Let us make a chair with our hands and carry her,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我们用手做个椅子抬她吧，” 稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: So they picked up Toto and put the dog in Dorothy’s lap, and then they made a chair with their hands for the seat and their arms for the arms and carried the sleeping girl between them through the flowers.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们抱起托托，把小狗放在多萝西的腿上。然后他们用手当椅子面，用胳膊当扶手，抬着睡着的小女孩穿过花丛。

paragraphs.en: On and on they walked, and it seemed that the great carpet of deadly flowers that surrounded them would never end.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一直走啊走，周围那一大片危险的花海似乎永远走不完。

paragraphs.en: They followed the bend of the river, and at last came upon their friend the Lion, lying fast asleep among the poppies.
paragraphs.cn: 他们沿着河湾走，终于看到了他们的朋友狮子，他正躺在罂粟花里睡得很熟。

paragraphs.en: The flowers had been too strong for the huge beast and he had given up at last, and fallen only a short distance from the end of the poppy bed, where the sweet grass spread in beautiful green fields before them.
paragraphs.cn: 花的力量对这只大野兽来说太强大了，他终于放弃了。他倒下的地方离罂粟花丛的尽头不远，那里有美丽的绿色草地，长着甜甜的青草。

paragraphs.en: “We can do nothing for him,” said the Tin Woodman, sadly; “for he is much too heavy to lift.
paragraphs.cn: “我们帮不了他，” 铁皮人伤心地说，“他太重了，我们抬不动。

paragraphs.en: We must leave him here to sleep on forever, and perhaps he will dream that he has found courage at last.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们只能让他永远睡在这里了，也许他会梦到自己终于变得勇敢了。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m sorry,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我很抱歉，” 稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “The Lion was a very good comrade for one so cowardly.
paragraphs.cn: “狮子虽然有点胆小，但他是个很好的伙伴。

paragraphs.en: But let us go on.”
paragraphs.cn: 可是，我们得继续走了。”

paragraphs.en: They carried the sleeping girl to a pretty spot beside the river, far enough from the poppy field to prevent her breathing any more of the poison of the flowers, and here they laid her gently on the soft grass and waited for the fresh breeze to waken her.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把睡着的小女孩抬到河边一个漂亮的地方，那里离罂粟花田很远，小女孩就不会再吸到花的毒气了。他们轻轻地把她放在柔软的草地上，等着清新的风把她唤醒。

chapters.title_en: The Queen of the Field Mice

paragraphs.en: “We cannot be far from the road of yellow brick, now,” remarked the Scarecrow, as he stood beside the girl, “for we have come nearly as far as the river carried us away.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们现在离黄砖路应该不远了，” 稻草人站在女孩旁边说，“因为我们已经走了差不多河水把我们冲走那么远了。”

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman was about to reply when he heard a low growl, and turning his head (which worked beautifully on hinges) he saw a strange beast come bounding over the grass toward them.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人正要回答，突然听到一声低沉的吼叫。他转过头（他的头在铰链上转得很漂亮），看到一只奇怪的野兽从草地上向他们跑来。

paragraphs.en: It was, indeed, a great yellow Wildcat, and the Woodman thought it must be chasing something, for its ears were lying close to its head and its mouth was wide open, showing two rows of ugly teeth, while its red eyes glowed like balls of fire.
paragraphs.cn: 这确实是一只大大的黄色野猫，铁皮人觉得它一定在追什么东西，因为它的耳朵紧贴着头，嘴巴张得大大的，露出两排可怕的牙齿，红色的眼睛像火球一样发光。

paragraphs.en: As it came nearer the Tin Woodman saw that running before the beast was a little gray field mouse, and although he had no heart he knew it was wrong for the Wildcat to try to kill such a pretty, harmless creature.
paragraphs.cn: 离得近了，铁皮人看到跑在野兽前面的是一只灰色小田鼠。虽然他没有心脏，但他知道野猫去杀这么可爱、没害处的小动物是不对的。

paragraphs.en: So the Woodman raised his axe, and as the Wildcat ran by he gave it a quick blow that cut the beast’s head clean off from its body, and it rolled over at his feet in two pieces.
paragraphs.cn: 于是铁皮人举起斧头，当野猫跑过时，他快速一击，把野兽的头从身体上砍了下来，野猫分成两半，滚到他脚下。

paragraphs.en: The field mouse, now that it was freed from its enemy, stopped short; and coming slowly up to the Woodman it said, in a squeaky little voice:
paragraphs.cn: 小田鼠从敌人那里逃脱了，它立刻停了下来。它慢慢走到铁皮人身边，用吱吱的小声音说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, thank you!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，谢谢你！

paragraphs.en: Thank you ever so much for saving my life.”
paragraphs.cn: 太感谢你救了我的命了！”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t speak of it, I beg of you,” replied the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “别客气，小事一桩。” 铁皮人回答。

paragraphs.en: “I have no heart, you know, so I am careful to help all those who may need a friend, even if it happens to be only a mouse.”
paragraphs.cn: “我没有心，所以我会很小心地帮助那些需要朋友的人，就算它只是一只小老鼠。”

paragraphs.en: “Only a mouse!” cried the little animal, indignantly. “Why, I am a Queen—the Queen of all the Field Mice!”
paragraphs.cn: “只是一只老鼠！”小动物生气地喊道，“我可是一位女王——所有田鼠的女王！”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, indeed,” said the Woodman, making a bow.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，真的吗？”铁皮人说着，鞠了一躬。

paragraphs.en: “Therefore you have done a great deed, as well as a brave one, in saving my life,” added the Queen.
paragraphs.cn: “所以，你救了我的命，做了一件很棒也很勇敢的事，”女王补充道。

paragraphs.en: At that moment several mice were seen running up as fast as their little legs could carry them, and when they saw their Queen they exclaimed:
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，几只老鼠跑了过来，跑得飞快。当它们看到自己的女王时，大声喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, your Majesty, we thought you would be killed!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，陛下，我们以为您会被杀死呢！

paragraphs.en: How did you manage to escape the great Wildcat?”
paragraphs.cn: 您是怎么从那只大野猫手里逃出来的呀？”

paragraphs.en: They all bowed so low to the little Queen that they almost stood upon their heads.
paragraphs.cn: 它们都向小女王深深地鞠躬，几乎都要倒立了。

paragraphs.en: “This funny tin man,” she answered, “killed the Wildcat and saved my life.
paragraphs.cn: “这个有趣的铁皮人，”她回答，“杀了那只野猫，救了我的命。

paragraphs.en: So hereafter you must all serve him, and obey his slightest wish.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以从今以后，你们都得为他服务，听他所有的话。”

paragraphs.en: “We will!” cried all the mice, in a shrill chorus.
paragraphs.cn: “我们会的！”所有老鼠尖声合唱道。

paragraphs.en: And then they scampered in all directions, for Toto had awakened from his sleep, and seeing all these mice around him he gave one bark of delight and jumped right into the middle of the group.
paragraphs.cn: 然后它们四处跑开，因为托托醒了。他看到身边有这么多老鼠，就高兴地叫了一声，跳进了老鼠群里。

paragraphs.en: Toto had always loved to chase mice when he lived in Kansas, and he saw no harm in it.
paragraphs.cn: 托托在堪萨斯生活的时候，就一直喜欢追老鼠，他觉得这没什么不对。

paragraphs.en: But the Tin Woodman caught the dog in his arms and held him tight, while he called to the mice, “Come back!
paragraphs.cn: 但是铁皮人把狗抱在怀里，紧紧地抱着，同时他对老鼠们喊道：“回来！

paragraphs.en: Come back!
paragraphs.cn: 回来！

paragraphs.en: Toto shall not hurt you.”
paragraphs.cn: 托托不会伤害你们的。”

paragraphs.en: At this the Queen of the Mice stuck her head out from underneath a clump of grass and asked, in a timid voice, “Are you sure he will not bite us?”
paragraphs.cn: 这时，老鼠女王从一丛草下面探出头来，怯生生地问：“你确定他不会咬我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I will not let him,” said the Woodman; “so do not be afraid.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不会让他咬的，”铁皮人说，“所以别害怕。”

paragraphs.en: One by one the mice came creeping back, and Toto did not bark again, although he tried to get out of the Woodman’s arms, and would have bitten him had he not known very well he was made of tin.
paragraphs.cn: 老鼠们一只接一只地爬了回来。托托没有再叫，虽然他努力想从铁皮人的怀里挣脱出去，如果他不知道铁皮人是铁皮做的，他肯定会咬他一口。

paragraphs.en: Finally one of the biggest mice spoke.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，其中一只最大的老鼠开口了。

paragraphs.en: “Is there anything we can do,” it asked, “to repay you for saving the life of our Queen?”
paragraphs.cn: 它问：“我们能做些什么，来报答您救了我们女王的命呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing that I know of,” answered the Woodman; but the Scarecrow, who had been trying to think, but could not because his head was stuffed with straw, said, quickly, “Oh, yes; you can save our friend, the Cowardly Lion, who is asleep in the poppy bed.”
paragraphs.cn: “据我所知，没有什么。”铁皮人回答道。但是稻草人，他一直在努力思考，却想不出来，因为他的脑袋里塞满了稻草，他很快地说：“哦，有了！你们可以救我们的朋友胆小的狮子，他睡在罂粟花丛里呢。”

paragraphs.en: “A Lion!” cried the little Queen. “Why, he would eat us all up.”
paragraphs.cn: “一只狮子！”小女王叫道，“他会把我们都吃掉的。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no,” declared the Scarecrow; “this Lion is a coward.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不，”稻草人说，“这只狮子是个胆小鬼。”

paragraphs.en: “Really?” asked the Mouse.
paragraphs.cn: “真的吗？”老鼠问道。

paragraphs.en: “He says so himself,” answered the Scarecrow, “and he would never hurt anyone who is our friend.
paragraphs.cn: “他自己就是这么说的，”稻草人回答，“他绝不会伤害我们的朋友。

paragraphs.en: If you will help us to save him I promise that he shall treat you all with kindness.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你帮我们救他，我保证他会对你们很好的。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well,” said the Queen, “we trust you.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，”女王说，“我们相信你。

paragraphs.en: But what shall we do?”
paragraphs.cn: 但是我们该怎么做呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Are there many of these mice which call you Queen and are willing to obey you?”
paragraphs.cn: “有没有很多老鼠都叫你女王，并且愿意听你的话？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes; there are thousands,” she replied.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是的，有好多好多只呢！”她回答说。

paragraphs.en: “Then send for them all to come here as soon as possible, and let each one bring a long piece of string.”
paragraphs.cn: “那就请它们都快点来这里吧，每只都要带一根长长的绳子哦。”

paragraphs.en: The Queen turned to the mice that attended her and told them to go at once and get all her people.
paragraphs.cn: 女王转头对身边的老鼠说，让它们赶紧去把所有老鼠都叫来。

paragraphs.en: As soon as they heard her orders they ran away in every direction as fast as possible.
paragraphs.cn: 它们一听到女王的命令，就飞快地朝各个方向跑开了。

paragraphs.en: “Now,” said the Scarecrow to the Tin Woodman, “you must go to those trees by the riverside and make a truck that will carry the Lion.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在，”稻草人对铁皮人说，“你得去河边的那些树那儿，做一个能运走狮子的小推车。”

paragraphs.en: So the Woodman went at once to the trees and began to work; and he soon made a truck out of the limbs of trees, from which he chopped away all the leaves and branches.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，铁皮人立刻跑到树林里开始干活了。他很快就用树枝做了一辆小推车，把上面的叶子和分叉都砍掉了。

paragraphs.en: He fastened it together with wooden pegs and made the four wheels out of short pieces of a big tree trunk.
paragraphs.cn: 他用木钉把它们固定在一起，又用一截大树干做了四个轮子。

paragraphs.en: So fast and so well did he work that by the time the mice began to arrive the truck was all ready for them.
paragraphs.cn: 他做得又快又好，等老鼠们开始来的时候，小推车就已经完全准备好了。

paragraphs.en: They came from all directions, and there were thousands of them: big mice and little mice and middle-sized mice; and each one brought a piece of string in his mouth.
paragraphs.cn: 它们从四面八方赶来，有好多好多只：大老鼠、小老鼠和中等大小的老鼠。每只嘴里都叼着一根绳子。

paragraphs.en: It was about this time that Dorothy woke from her long sleep and opened her eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这个时候，多萝西从睡梦中醒了过来，睁开了眼睛。

paragraphs.en: She was greatly astonished to find herself lying upon the grass, with thousands of mice standing around and looking at her timidly.
paragraphs.cn: 她很吃惊地发现自己躺在草地上，周围站着好多好多只老鼠，它们都怯怯地看着她。

paragraphs.en: But the Scarecrow told her about everything, and turning to the dignified little Mouse, he said:
paragraphs.cn: 但是稻草人把所有的事情都告诉了她。然后，他转向那只很有礼貌的小老鼠，说：

paragraphs.en: “Permit me to introduce to you her Majesty, the Queen.”
paragraphs.cn: “请允许我为您介绍，这位就是女王陛下。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy nodded gravely and the Queen made a curtsy, after which she became quite friendly with the little girl.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西郑重地点了点头，女王也行了个屈膝礼。之后，她就和这个小女孩变得很友好了。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow and the Woodman now began to fasten the mice to the truck, using the strings they had brought.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人和铁皮人开始把老鼠绑到小推车上，用的就是老鼠们带来的绳子。

paragraphs.en: One end of a string was tied around the neck of each mouse and the other end to the truck.
paragraphs.cn: 绳子的一头系在每只老鼠的脖子上，另一头系在小推车上。

paragraphs.en: Of course the truck was a thousand times bigger than any of the mice who were to draw it; but when all the mice had been harnessed, they were able to pull it quite easily.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，小推车比那些要拉它的老鼠大了一千倍！但是当所有老鼠都系好以后，它们就能很轻松地拉动小推车了。

paragraphs.en: Even the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman could sit on it, and were drawn swiftly by their queer little horses to the place where the Lion lay asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 连稻草人和铁皮人都能坐在上面，被它们那些特别的小马车夫飞快地拉到了狮子睡觉的地方。

paragraphs.en: After a great deal of hard work, for the Lion was heavy, they managed to get him up on the truck.
paragraphs.cn: 费了好大的劲儿，因为狮子很重，他们终于把他弄到了小推车上。

paragraphs.en: Then the Queen hurriedly gave her people the order to start, for she feared if the mice stayed among the poppies too long they also would fall asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 然后女王赶紧命令她的人们出发，因为她担心老鼠们在罂粟花里待太久，也会睡着。

paragraphs.en: At first the little creatures, many though they were, could hardly stir the heavily loaded truck; but the Woodman and the Scarecrow both pushed from behind, and they got along better.
paragraphs.cn: 一开始，这些小家伙们，虽然有很多只，却很难拉动这辆很重的小推车。但是铁皮人和稻草人都在后面推，他们就走得更好了。

paragraphs.en: Soon they rolled the Lion out of the poppy bed to the green fields, where he could breathe the sweet, fresh air again, instead of the poisonous scent of the flowers.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他们就把狮子从罂粟花丛里推出了，到了绿色的草地上。在那里，他又能呼吸到甜甜的新鲜空气了，而不是那些花有毒的味道。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy came to meet them and thanked the little mice warmly for saving her companion from death.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西来迎接他们，并热烈地感谢小老鼠们救了她的伙伴，让他免于死亡。

paragraphs.en: She had grown so fond of the big Lion she was glad he had been rescued.
paragraphs.cn: 她已经非常喜欢这个大大的狮子了，所以很高兴他被救了出来。

paragraphs.en: Then the mice were unharnessed from the truck and scampered away through the grass to their homes.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，老鼠们从小推车上解开，一溜烟地穿过草地跑回了家。

paragraphs.en: The Queen of the Mice was the last to leave.
paragraphs.cn: 老鼠女王是最后一个走的。

paragraphs.en: “If ever you need us again,” she said, “come out into the field and call, and we shall hear you and come to your assistance.
paragraphs.cn: “如果你们以后还需要我们，”她说，“就到田野里来叫我们，我们会听到的，然后来帮你们的忙。

paragraphs.en: Good-bye!”
paragraphs.cn: 再见！”

paragraphs.en: “Good-bye!” they all answered, and away the Queen ran, while Dorothy held Toto tightly lest he should run after her and frighten her.
paragraphs.cn: “再见！”他们都回答道。女王跑走了，而多萝西紧紧地拉着托托，生怕他追上去吓到女王。

paragraphs.en: After this they sat down beside the Lion until he should awaken; and the Scarecrow brought Dorothy some fruit from a tree near by, which she ate for her dinner.
paragraphs.cn: 这之后，他们就坐在狮子的旁边，等着他醒过来。稻草人从附近的树上给多萝西摘了一些水果，多萝西就把它当晚餐吃了。

paragraphs.en: It was some time before the Cowardly Lion awakened, for he had lain among the poppies a long while, breathing in their deadly fragrance; but when he did open his eyes and roll off the truck he was very glad to find himself still alive.
paragraphs.cn: 胆小的狮子睡了一会儿才醒来。他躺在罂粟花里很久，吸了它们危险的香味。当他睁开眼睛，从车上滚下来时，他很高兴自己还活着。

paragraphs.en: “I ran as fast as I could,” he said, sitting down and yawning, “but the flowers were too strong for me.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐下来打着哈欠说：“我跑得很快，但这些花太厉害了。”

paragraphs.en: How did you get me out?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们怎么把我弄出来的？”

paragraphs.en: Then they told him of the field mice, and how they had generously saved him from death; and the Cowardly Lion laughed, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他们告诉他田鼠们的事，说田鼠们是怎样好心地救了他。胆小的狮子笑了，说：

paragraphs.en: “I have always thought myself very big and terrible; yet such little things as flowers came near to killing me, and such small animals as mice have saved my life.
paragraphs.cn: “我一直觉得自己又高又壮，很厉害。可是，像花这样小的东西差点要了我的命，而像老鼠这样小的动物却救了我的命。”

paragraphs.en: How strange it all is!
paragraphs.cn: 这多奇怪啊！

paragraphs.en: But, comrades, what shall we do now?”
paragraphs.cn: “但是，伙伴们，我们现在该怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: “We must journey on until we find the road of yellow brick again,” said Dorothy, “and then we can keep on to the Emerald City.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们必须一直往前走，直到再次找到黄砖路，”多萝西说，“然后我们就能去到翡翠城了。”

paragraphs.en: So, the Lion being fully refreshed, and feeling quite himself again, they all started upon the journey, greatly enjoying the walk through the soft, fresh grass; and it was not long before they reached the road of yellow brick and turned again toward the Emerald City where the Great Oz dwelt.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，狮子精神完全恢复了，感觉又像以前一样了。他们都开始旅行，很喜欢走在柔软新鲜的草地上。没多久，他们就走到了黄砖路，再次走向伟大的奥兹大王住的翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: The road was smooth and well paved, now, and the country about was beautiful, so that the travelers rejoiced in leaving the forest far behind, and with it the many dangers they had met in its gloomy shades.
paragraphs.cn: 现在路面又平又好走，周围的景色也很美。旅行者们很高兴把森林远远地抛在身后，也把他们在黑暗森林里遇到的许多危险抛开了。

paragraphs.en: Once more they could see fences built beside the road; but these were painted green, and when they came to a small house, in which a farmer evidently lived, that also was painted green.
paragraphs.cn: 他们再次看到路边有篱笆了，这些篱笆都被漆成了绿色。当他们走到一间小房子前，里面好像住着一个农夫，那房子也被漆成了绿色。

paragraphs.en: They passed by several of these houses during the afternoon, and sometimes people came to the doors and looked at them as if they would like to ask questions; but no one came near them nor spoke to them because of the great Lion, of which they were very much afraid.
paragraphs.cn: 整个下午，他们经过了好几间这样的房子。有时有人走到门口，看着他们，好像想问问题。但没人走近他们，也没人跟他们说话，因为他们很害怕那个大大的狮子。

paragraphs.en: The people were all dressed in clothing of a lovely emerald-green color and wore peaked hats like those of the Munchkins.
paragraphs.cn: 那些人都穿着漂亮的翠绿色衣服，戴着像芒奇金人一样的尖帽子。

paragraphs.en: “This must be the Land of Oz,” said Dorothy, “and we are surely getting near the Emerald City.”
paragraphs.cn: “这一定是奥兹国，”多萝西说，“我们肯定快要到翡翠城了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” answered the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，”稻草人回答。

paragraphs.en: “Everything is green here, while in the country of the Munchkins blue was the favorite color.
paragraphs.cn: “这里的一切都是绿色的，而在芒奇金人的国度里，蓝色才是大家最喜欢的颜色。”

paragraphs.en: But the people do not seem to be as friendly as the Munchkins, and I’m afraid we shall be unable to find a place to pass the night.”
paragraphs.cn: “但这里的人们好像不像芒奇金人那么友好，我怕我们找不到过夜的地方。”

paragraphs.en: “I should like something to eat besides fruit,” said the girl, “and I’m sure Toto is nearly starved.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩说：“我除了水果，还想吃点别的。我肯定托托也快饿坏了。”

paragraphs.en: Let us stop at the next house and talk to the people.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们去下一家停下来，跟他们说说话吧。”

paragraphs.en: So, when they came to a good-sized farmhouse, Dorothy walked boldly up to the door and knocked.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，当他们走到一间挺大的农家房子前，多萝西大胆地走到门口敲了敲门。

paragraphs.en: A woman opened it just far enough to look out, and said, “What do you want, child, and why is that great Lion with you?”
paragraphs.cn: 一个女人把门开了一点点，探出头来，说：“孩子，你们想干什么？那个大大的狮子为什么跟着你们？”

paragraphs.en: “We wish to pass the night with you, if you will allow us,” answered Dorothy; “and the Lion is my friend and comrade, and would not hurt you for the world.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果我们能和你们一起过夜，我们会很高兴的，”多萝西回答，“狮子是我的朋友和伙伴，他绝对不会伤害你。”

paragraphs.en: “Is he tame?” asked the woman, opening the door a little wider.
paragraphs.cn: “他很温顺吗？”女人把门又开大了一点，问道。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes,” said the girl, “and he is a great coward, too.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是的，”女孩说，“他还是个大大的胆小鬼呢。”

paragraphs.en: He will be more afraid of you than you are of him.”
paragraphs.cn: 他会比你更害怕你。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said the woman, after thinking it over and taking another peep at the Lion, “if that is the case you may come in, and I will give you some supper and a place to sleep.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，”女人想了想，又偷偷看了看狮子，说，“如果真是这样，你们可以进来，我会给你们一些晚饭和睡觉的地方。”

paragraphs.en: So they all entered the house, where there were, besides the woman, two children and a man.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们都进了屋子。屋子里除了那个女人，还有两个孩子和一个男人。

paragraphs.en: The man had hurt his leg, and was lying on the couch in a corner.
paragraphs.cn: 那个男人腿受伤了，正躺在角落的沙发上。

paragraphs.en: They seemed greatly surprised to see so strange a company, and while the woman was busy laying the table the man asked:
paragraphs.cn: 他们看到这么一群陌生人，显得非常惊讶。女人忙着摆桌子的时候，男人问道：

paragraphs.en: “Where are you all going?”
paragraphs.cn: “你们要去哪里？”

paragraphs.en: “To the Emerald City,” said Dorothy, “to see the Great Oz.”
paragraphs.cn: “去 翡翠城，” 多萝西 说，“去见伟大的 奥兹大王。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, indeed!” exclaimed the man. “Are you sure that Oz will see you?”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，真的吗！” 那人惊呼道。“你确定 奥兹大王 会见你吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why not?” she replied.
paragraphs.cn: “为什么不呢？” 她回答。

paragraphs.en: “Why, it is said that he never lets anyone come into his presence.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，大家都说他从不见任何人。

paragraphs.en: I have been to the Emerald City many times, and it is a beautiful and wonderful place; but I have never been permitted to see the Great Oz, nor do I know of any living person who has seen him.”
paragraphs.cn: 我去了 翡翠城 好多次，那地方又美又好玩；可是我从来没能见到伟大的 奥兹大王，我也不知道有谁见过他。”

paragraphs.en: “Does he never go out?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “他从不出去吗？” 稻草人 问道。

paragraphs.en: “Never.
paragraphs.cn: “从不。

paragraphs.en: He sits day after day in the great Throne Room of his Palace, and even those who wait upon him do not see him face to face.”
paragraphs.cn: 他日复一日地坐在他宫殿的大宝座厅里，就连服侍他的人也见不到他的真面目。”

paragraphs.en: “What is he like?” asked the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “他长什么样呀？” 女孩问。

paragraphs.en: “That is hard to tell,” said the man thoughtfully.
paragraphs.cn: “这可不好说，” 那人想了想说。

paragraphs.en: “You see, Oz is a Great Wizard, and can take on any form he wishes.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，奥兹大王 是个大魔法师，他想变成什么样都行。

paragraphs.en: So that some say he looks like a bird; and some say he looks like an elephant; and some say he looks like a cat.
paragraphs.cn: 所以有人说他像小鸟；有人说他像大象；还有人说他像小猫。

paragraphs.en: To others he appears as a beautiful fairy, or a brownie, or in any other form that pleases him.
paragraphs.cn: 对另一些人来说，他会变成漂亮的仙女，或者小矮人，或者任何他喜欢的样子。

paragraphs.en: But who the real Oz is, when he is in his own form, no living person can tell.”
paragraphs.cn: 可是真正的 奥兹大王，他自己本来的样子是什么，没人能说出来。”

paragraphs.en: “That is very strange,” said Dorothy, “but we must try, in some way, to see him, or we shall have made our journey for nothing.”
paragraphs.cn: “这真奇怪，”多萝西 说，“但我们一定要想办法见到他，不然我们这次旅行就白费了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why do you wish to see the terrible Oz?” asked the man.
paragraphs.cn: “你们为什么要见可怕的 奥兹大王 呢？” 那人问。

paragraphs.en: “I want him to give me some brains,” said the Scarecrow eagerly.
paragraphs.cn: “我想要他给我一些脑子，” 稻草人 急切地说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Oz could do that easily enough,” declared the man.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，奥兹大王 很容易就能做到，” 那人说。

paragraphs.en: “He has more brains than he needs.”
paragraphs.cn: “他有好多用不完的脑子呢。”

paragraphs.en: “And I want him to give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “我想要他给我一颗心，” 铁皮人 说。

paragraphs.en: “That will not trouble him,” continued the man, “for Oz has a large collection of hearts, of all sizes and shapes.”
paragraphs.cn: “那不会麻烦他，” 那人接着说，“因为 奥兹大王 有一大堆心，各种大小形状的都有。”

paragraphs.en: “And I want him to give me courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “我想要他给我勇气，” 胆小的狮子 说。

paragraphs.en: “Oz keeps a great pot of courage in his Throne Room,” said the man, “which he has covered with a golden plate, to keep it from running over.
paragraphs.cn: “奥兹大王 在他的宝座厅里放着一大罐勇气，” 那人说，“他用一个金盘子盖着，防止它溢出来。

paragraphs.en: He will be glad to give you some.”
paragraphs.cn: 他会很乐意给你一些的。”

paragraphs.en: “And I want him to send me back to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我想要他把我送回 堪萨斯，” 多萝西 说。

paragraphs.en: “Where is Kansas?” asked the man, with surprise.
paragraphs.cn: “堪萨斯 在哪里？” 那人惊讶地问。

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know,” replied Dorothy sorrowfully, “but it is my home, and I’m sure it’s somewhere.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，” 多萝西 伤心地回答，“但那是我家，我相信它一定在某个地方。”

paragraphs.en: “Very likely.
paragraphs.cn: “很可能吧。

paragraphs.en: Well, Oz can do anything; so I suppose he will find Kansas for you.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，奥兹大王 什么都能做到；所以我猜他会帮你找到 堪萨斯 的。

paragraphs.en: But first you must get to see him, and that will be a hard task; for the Great Wizard does not like to see anyone, and he usually has his own way.
paragraphs.cn: 但首先你得去见到他，那可不容易；因为这位大魔法师不喜欢见任何人，而且他总是随心所欲。

paragraphs.en: But what do YOU want?” he continued, speaking to Toto.
paragraphs.cn: “那你想要什么呢？”他接着问托托。

paragraphs.en: Toto only wagged his tail; for, strange to say, he could not speak.
paragraphs.cn: 托托只是摇了摇尾巴，说来也奇怪，他不会说话。

paragraphs.en: The woman now called to them that supper was ready, so they gathered around the table and Dorothy ate some delicious porridge and a dish of scrambled eggs and a plate of nice white bread, and enjoyed her meal.
paragraphs.cn: 女人叫他们去吃晚饭，说晚饭做好了。他们围坐在桌子旁，多萝西吃了美味的粥、一盘炒鸡蛋和一片白面包，吃得很开心。

paragraphs.en: The Lion ate some of the porridge, but did not care for it, saying it was made from oats and oats were food for horses, not for lions.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子吃了点粥，但不喜欢，他说这是燕麦做的，燕麦是给马吃的，不是给狮子吃的。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman ate nothing at all.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人和铁皮人什么都没吃。

paragraphs.en: Toto ate a little of everything, and was glad to get a good supper again.
paragraphs.cn: 托托每样都吃了一点，很高兴又能吃到好吃的晚饭了。

paragraphs.en: The woman now gave Dorothy a bed to sleep in, and Toto lay down beside her, while the Lion guarded the door of her room so she might not be disturbed.
paragraphs.cn: 女人给多萝西一张床睡觉，托托睡在她旁边，狮子守在她的房门口，这样她就不会被打扰了。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman stood up in a corner and kept quiet all night, although of course they could not sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人和铁皮人站在一个角落里，整晚都安安静静的，虽然他们当然睡不着。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, as soon as the sun was up, they started on their way, and soon saw a beautiful green glow in the sky just before them.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，太阳一出来，他们就上路了。很快，他们就看到前面天空有一道美丽的绿光。

paragraphs.en: “That must be the Emerald City,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “那一定是翡翠城。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: As they walked on, the green glow became brighter and brighter, and it seemed that at last they were nearing the end of their travels.
paragraphs.cn: 他们继续往前走，绿光变得越来越亮，好像他们终于快走到旅行的终点了。

paragraphs.en: Yet it was afternoon before they came to the great wall that surrounded the City.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，直到下午，他们才走到包围着这座城市的大墙。

paragraphs.en: It was high and thick and of a bright green color.
paragraphs.cn: 这墙又高又厚，是亮绿色的。

paragraphs.en: In front of them, and at the end of the road of yellow brick, was a big gate, all studded with emeralds that glittered so in the sun that even the painted eyes of the Scarecrow were dazzled by their brilliancy.
paragraphs.cn: 在他们前面，也是黄砖路的尽头，有一扇大门，门上镶满了绿宝石，这些绿宝石在阳光下闪闪发光，甚至连稻草人画出来的眼睛都被闪得睁不开。

paragraphs.en: There was a bell beside the gate, and Dorothy pushed the button and heard a silvery tinkle sound within.
paragraphs.cn: 门旁边有一个铃铛，多萝西按了按钮，听到里面传来银铃般清脆的声音。

paragraphs.en: Then the big gate swung slowly open, and they all passed through and found themselves in a high arched room, the walls of which glistened with countless emeralds.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，大门慢慢地打开了，他们都走了进去，发现自己在一个高高的拱形房间里，房间的墙壁上闪耀着无数的绿宝石。

paragraphs.en: Before them stood a little man about the same size as the Munchkins.
paragraphs.cn: 他们面前站着一个小个子男人，和芒奇金人差不多高。

paragraphs.en: He was clothed all in green, from his head to his feet, and even his skin was of a greenish tint.
paragraphs.cn: 他从头到脚都穿着绿色的衣服，甚至他的皮肤都带点绿色。

paragraphs.en: At his side was a large green box.
paragraphs.cn: 他旁边有一个大大的绿色盒子。

paragraphs.en: When he saw Dorothy and her companions the man asked, “What do you wish in the Emerald City?”
paragraphs.cn: 当他看到多萝西和她的伙伴们时，那个男人问：“你们想在翡翠城做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “We came here to see the Great Oz,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我们来这里是想见伟大的奥兹大王。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: The man was so surprised at this answer that he sat down to think it over.
paragraphs.cn: 那个男人对这个回答感到很惊讶，他坐下来想了想。

paragraphs.en: “It has been many years since anyone asked me to see Oz,” he said, shaking his head in perplexity.
paragraphs.cn: “很多年了，没有人要求见奥兹大王了。”他困惑地摇了摇头说。

paragraphs.en: “He is powerful and terrible, and if you come on an idle or foolish errand to bother the wise reflections of the Great Wizard, he might be angry and destroy you all in an instant.”
paragraphs.cn: “他很强大，也很可怕。如果你们是无聊或者傻傻地来打扰伟大的巫师思考，他可能会生气，一瞬间把你们都消灭掉。”

paragraphs.en: “But it is not a foolish errand, nor an idle one,” replied the Scarecrow; “it is important.
paragraphs.cn: “这不是傻傻地来，也不是无聊地来。”稻草人回答说，“这件事很重要。

paragraphs.en: And we have been told that Oz is a good Wizard.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且我们听说奥兹大王是一位好巫师。”

paragraphs.en: “So he is,” said the green man, “and he rules the Emerald City wisely and well.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，他就是。”绿人说，“他管理翡翠城很聪明，也很好。”

paragraphs.en: But to those who are not honest, or who approach him from curiosity, he is most terrible, and few have ever dared ask to see his face.
paragraphs.cn: “但对于不诚实的人，或者只是好奇来找他的人，他就非常可怕，很少有人敢要求见他的真面目。”

paragraphs.en: I am the Guardian of the Gates, and since you demand to see the Great Oz I must take you to his Palace.
paragraphs.cn: “我是城门守卫，既然你们坚持要见伟大的奥兹大王，我就必须带你们去他的宫殿。

paragraphs.en: But first you must put on the spectacles.”
paragraphs.cn: 但首先你们必须戴上眼镜。”

paragraphs.en: “Why?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “为什么？” 多萝西 问道。

paragraphs.en: “Because if you did not wear spectacles the brightness and glory of the Emerald City would blind you.
paragraphs.cn: “因为如果你不戴眼镜，翡翠城 的光芒会把你的眼睛闪瞎的。

paragraphs.en: Even those who live in the City must wear spectacles night and day.
paragraphs.cn: 即使住在城里的人，也得日日夜夜戴着眼镜。

paragraphs.en: They are all locked on, for Oz so ordered it when the City was first built, and I have the only key that will unlock them.”
paragraphs.cn: 这些眼镜都被锁住了，因为 奥兹大王 在建城时就是这么吩咐的，而我呢，有唯一能打开它们的钥匙。”

paragraphs.en: He opened the big box, and Dorothy saw that it was filled with spectacles of every size and shape.
paragraphs.cn: 他打开大盒子，多萝西 看到里面装满了各种大小和形状的眼镜。

paragraphs.en: All of them had green glasses in them.
paragraphs.cn: 所有的眼镜片都是绿色的。

paragraphs.en: The Guardian of the Gates found a pair that would just fit Dorothy and put them over her eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 城门守卫 找到一副刚好适合 多萝西 的眼镜，给她戴上。

paragraphs.en: There were two golden bands fastened to them that passed around the back of her head, where they were locked together by a little key that was at the end of a chain the Guardian of the Gates wore around his neck.
paragraphs.cn: 眼镜上固定着两条金色的带子，绕过她的后脑勺，被一把小钥匙锁住了。这把小钥匙就系在 城门守卫 脖子上的一条链子上。

paragraphs.en: When they were on, Dorothy could not take them off had she wished, but of course she did not wish to be blinded by the glare of the Emerald City, so she said nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 戴上后，多萝西 想摘也摘不下来了。不过她当然不想被 翡翠城 的光芒闪瞎，所以她什么也没说。

paragraphs.en: Then the green man fitted spectacles for the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion, and even on little Toto; and all were locked fast with the key.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，那个绿衣服的人又给 稻草人、铁皮人、狮子 戴上了眼镜，甚至给小小的 托托 也戴上了；所有的眼镜都用钥匙牢牢地锁住了。

paragraphs.en: Then the Guardian of the Gates put on his own glasses and told them he was ready to show them to the Palace.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，城门守卫 戴上自己的眼镜，告诉他们，他已经准备好带他们去皇宫了。

paragraphs.en: Taking a big golden key from a peg on the wall, he opened another gate, and they all followed him through the portal into the streets of the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 他从墙上的一个挂钩上取下一把大金钥匙，打开了另一扇门。他们都跟着他穿过大门，走进了 翡翠城 的街道。

paragraphs.en: Even with eyes protected by the green spectacles, Dorothy and her friends were at first dazzled by the brilliancy of the wonderful City.
paragraphs.cn: 即使眼睛有绿色眼镜的保护，多萝西 和她的朋友们最初还是被这座神奇城市的明亮光芒晃得睁不开眼。

paragraphs.en: The streets were lined with beautiful houses all built of green marble and studded everywhere with sparkling emeralds.
paragraphs.cn: 街道两旁都是漂亮的房子，它们全是用绿色大理石建成的，上面还镶满了闪闪发光的绿宝石。

paragraphs.en: They walked over a pavement of the same green marble, and where the blocks were joined together were rows of emeralds, set closely, and glittering in the brightness of the sun.
paragraphs.cn: 他们走在同样是绿色大理石铺成的路上，大理石块连接的地方，都密密地镶着一排排的绿宝石，在阳光下闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: The window panes were of green glass; even the sky above the City had a green tint, and the rays of the sun were green.
paragraphs.cn: 窗户的玻璃是绿色的；就连城市上方的天空也带着一点绿色，太阳的光线也是绿色的。

paragraphs.en: There were many people—men, women, and children—walking about, and these were all dressed in green clothes and had greenish skins.
paragraphs.cn: 街上有很多人在走动——有男人、女人和小孩——他们都穿着绿色的衣服，皮肤也带着一点绿色。

paragraphs.en: They looked at Dorothy and her strangely assorted company with wondering eyes, and the children all ran away and hid behind their mothers when they saw the Lion; but no one spoke to them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们好奇地看着 多萝西 和她那群奇奇怪怪的同伴。当孩子们看到 狮子 时，都跑开躲到妈妈身后了；但没有人跟他们说话。

paragraphs.en: Many shops stood in the street, and Dorothy saw that everything in them was green.
paragraphs.cn: 街上有很多商店，多萝西 看到店里所有的东西都是绿色的。

paragraphs.en: Green candy and green pop-corn were offered for sale, as well as green shoes, green hats, and green clothes of all sorts.
paragraphs.cn: 有绿色的糖果、绿色的爆米花在卖，还有绿色的鞋子、绿色的帽子和各种各样的绿色衣服。

paragraphs.en: At one place a man was selling green lemonade, and when the children bought it Dorothy could see that they paid for it with green pennies.
paragraphs.cn: 有个地方，一个人在卖绿色的柠檬水，当孩子们买的时候，多萝西 看到他们用绿色的硬币付钱。

paragraphs.en: There seemed to be no horses nor animals of any kind; the men carried things around in little green carts, which they pushed before them.
paragraphs.cn: 好像没有马，也没有任何动物；男人们把东西放在绿色的小推车里，在前面推着走。

paragraphs.en: Everyone seemed happy and contented and prosperous.
paragraphs.cn: 每个人看起来都高高兴兴、很满足、生活得很好。

paragraphs.en: The Guardian of the Gates led them through the streets until they came to a big building, exactly in the middle of the City, which was the Palace of Oz, the Great Wizard.
paragraphs.cn: 城门守卫 带着他们穿过街道，直到来到城市正中央的一座大建筑，那就是大巫师 奥兹大王 的宫殿。

paragraphs.en: There was a soldier before the door, dressed in a green uniform and wearing a long green beard.
paragraphs.cn: 门前站着一个士兵，穿着绿色的制服，留着长长的绿色胡子。

paragraphs.en: “Here are strangers,” said the Guardian of the Gates to him, “and they demand to see the Great Oz.”
paragraphs.cn: “这里有陌生人，”城门守卫 对他说，“他们想见大巫师 奥兹大王。”

paragraphs.en: “Step inside,” answered the soldier, “and I will carry your message to him.”
paragraphs.cn: “请进，”士兵回答，“我会把你们的话告诉他的。”

paragraphs.en: So they passed through the Palace Gates and were led into a big room with a green carpet and lovely green furniture set with emeralds.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们穿过宫殿大门，被带进一个大房间，里面铺着绿色的地毯，摆着漂亮的绿色家具，上面还镶嵌着绿宝石。

paragraphs.en: The soldier made them all wipe their feet upon a green mat before entering this room, and when they were seated he said politely:
paragraphs.cn: 士兵让他们在进这个房间前，都把脚在绿色的垫子上擦干净。等他们坐下后，他礼貌地说：

paragraphs.en: “Please make yourselves comfortable while I go to the door of the Throne Room and tell Oz you are here.”
paragraphs.cn: “请大家舒服地坐着，我这就去宝座厅门口，告诉 奥兹大王 你们来了。”

paragraphs.en: They had to wait a long time before the soldier returned.
paragraphs.cn: 他们等了好久，士兵才回来。

paragraphs.en: When, at last, he came back, Dorothy asked:
paragraphs.cn: 士兵终于回来了，多萝西问：

paragraphs.en: “Have you seen Oz?”
paragraphs.cn: “你见到奥兹大王了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no,” returned the soldier; “I have never seen him.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，没有，”士兵说，“我从来没见过他。”

paragraphs.en: But I spoke to him as he sat behind his screen and gave him your message.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我跟他说了话，他当时坐在屏风后面。我还把你的话告诉了他。

paragraphs.en: He said he will grant you an audience, if you so desire; but each one of you must enter his presence alone, and he will admit but one each day.
paragraphs.cn: 他说如果你想见他，他会让你进去。不过你们每个人都得单独进去，而且他一天只让一个人进去。

paragraphs.en: Therefore, as you must remain in the Palace for several days, I will have you shown to rooms where you may rest in comfort after your journey.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以，你们得在宫殿里住几天。我会让人带你们去房间，这样你们就能好好休息了，因为你们赶了很远的路。”

paragraphs.en: “Thank you,” replied the girl; “that is very kind of Oz.”
paragraphs.cn: “谢谢你，”女孩说，“奥兹大王人真好。”

paragraphs.en: The soldier now blew upon a green whistle, and at once a young girl, dressed in a pretty green silk gown, entered the room.
paragraphs.cn: 士兵吹了一声绿色的哨子，一个穿着漂亮绿丝绸裙子的女孩马上走进了房间。

paragraphs.en: She had lovely green hair and green eyes, and she bowed low before Dorothy as she said, “Follow me and I will show you your room.”
paragraphs.cn: 她有着绿色的头发和绿色的眼睛。她向多萝西鞠了一躬，说：“跟我来，我带你去你的房间。”

paragraphs.en: So Dorothy said good-bye to all her friends except Toto, and taking the dog in her arms followed the green girl through seven passages and up three flights of stairs until they came to a room at the front of the Palace.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，多萝西跟所有朋友说了再见，只留下托托。她抱着小狗，跟着绿衣女孩穿过七条走廊，又走了三段楼梯，终于来到了宫殿前面的一间房间。

paragraphs.en: It was the sweetest little room in the world, with a soft comfortable bed that had sheets of green silk and a green velvet counterpane.
paragraphs.cn: 这是世界上最可爱的小房间了！床又软又舒服，铺着绿色的丝绸床单和绿色的天鹅绒被子。

paragraphs.en: There was a tiny fountain in the middle of the room, that shot a spray of green perfume into the air, to fall back into a beautifully carved green marble basin.
paragraphs.cn: 房间中间有一个小喷泉，喷出绿色的香水雾气。这些雾气又落回到一个雕刻得很漂亮的绿色大理石盆子里。

paragraphs.en: Beautiful green flowers stood in the windows, and there was a shelf with a row of little green books.
paragraphs.cn: 窗户上放着美丽的绿色鲜花，书架上还摆着一排排绿色的小书。

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy had time to open these books she found them full of queer green pictures that made her laugh, they were so funny.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西有空打开这些书的时候，发现里面都是奇怪的绿色图画，逗得她哈哈大笑，太好玩了。

paragraphs.en: In a wardrobe were many green dresses, made of silk and satin and velvet; and all of them fitted Dorothy exactly.
paragraphs.cn: 衣柜里有很多绿色的裙子，是用丝绸、缎子和天鹅绒做的。每件都特别合多萝西的身。

paragraphs.en: “Make yourself perfectly at home,” said the green girl, “and if you wish for anything ring the bell.
paragraphs.cn: “你就当这里是自己家一样，”绿衣女孩说，“想要什么就按铃。”

paragraphs.en: Oz will send for you tomorrow morning.”
paragraphs.cn: 奥兹大王明天早上会派人来叫你。”

paragraphs.en: She left Dorothy alone and went back to the others.
paragraphs.cn: 她把多萝西一个人留在房间里，然后回去找其他人了。

paragraphs.en: These she also led to rooms, and each one of them found himself lodged in a very pleasant part of the Palace.
paragraphs.cn: 她也把这些人带到了房间，他们每个人都发现自己住在了宫殿里一个很舒服的地方。

paragraphs.en: Of course this politeness was wasted on the Scarecrow; for when he found himself alone in his room he stood stupidly in one spot, just within the doorway, to wait till morning.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，这份好心对稻草人来说一点用都没有。因为他发现自己一个人在房间里时，就傻傻地站在门口，一直等到天亮。

paragraphs.en: It would not rest him to lie down, and he could not close his eyes; so he remained all night staring at a little spider which was weaving its web in a corner of the room, just as if it were not one of the most wonderful rooms in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 躺下对他来说没用，他也闭不上眼睛。所以他整晚都盯着一只小蜘蛛，这只小蜘蛛正在房间角落里织网。他好像根本不知道这是世界上最棒的房间之一。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman lay down on his bed from force of habit, for he remembered when he was made of flesh; but not being able to sleep, he passed the night moving his joints up and down to make sure they kept in good working order.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人习惯性地躺在床上，因为他记得自己以前是肉做的。但他睡不着，只好整晚不停地动来动去，检查自己的关节有没有坏掉。

paragraphs.en: The Lion would have preferred a bed of dried leaves in the forest, and did not like being shut up in a room; but he had too much sense to let this worry him, so he sprang upon the bed and rolled himself up like a cat and purred himself asleep in a minute.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子更喜欢森林里用干树叶做的床，不喜欢被关在房间里。但他很聪明，没让自己烦恼。所以他跳到床上，像猫一样卷成一团，很快就舒服地睡着了。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, after breakfast, the green maiden came to fetch Dorothy, and she dressed her in one of the prettiest gowns, made of green brocaded satin.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，吃过早饭后，绿衣女孩来接多萝西。她给多萝西穿上了一件最漂亮的绿色丝绸裙子。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy put on a green silk apron and tied a green ribbon around Toto’s neck, and they started for the Throne Room of the Great Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西穿上了一件绿色丝绸围裙，给托托的脖子上系了一条绿色丝带。然后他们一起去大奥兹大王的宝座室了。

paragraphs.en: First they came to a great hall in which were many ladies and gentlemen of the court, all dressed in rich costumes.
paragraphs.cn: 首先，他们来到了一个大厅。里面有很多穿着漂亮衣服的贵族。

paragraphs.en: These people had nothing to do but talk to each other, but they always came to wait outside the Throne Room every morning, although they were never permitted to see Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 这些人除了聊天没什么事可做，但他们每天早上都会来宝座室外面等着，虽然他们从来都不能见到奥兹大王。

paragraphs.en: As Dorothy entered they looked at her curiously, and one of them whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西进去的时候，他们都好奇地看着她，其中一个人小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Are you really going to look upon the face of Oz the Terrible?”
paragraphs.cn: “你真的要去见可怕的奥兹大王吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Of course,” answered the girl, “if he will see me.”
paragraphs.cn: “当然啦，”女孩说，“如果他肯见我。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, he will see you,” said the soldier who had taken her message to the Wizard, “although he does not like to have people ask to see him.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，他会见你的！”那个替她给魔法师传话的士兵说，“虽然他不喜欢别人求他见面。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, at first he was angry and said I should send you back where you came from.
paragraphs.cn: 真的，一开始他还很生气，说要把你送回老家去。

paragraphs.en: Then he asked me what you looked like, and when I mentioned your silver shoes he was very much interested.
paragraphs.cn: 后来他问你长什么样，当我提到你的银鞋时，他可感兴趣啦。

paragraphs.en: At last I told him about the mark upon your forehead, and he decided he would admit you to his presence.”
paragraphs.cn: 最后，我又告诉他你额头上的印记，他才决定让你去见他。”

paragraphs.en: Just then a bell rang, and the green girl said to Dorothy, “That is the signal.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，铃声响了，绿衣女孩对多萝西说：“这是信号。

paragraphs.en: You must go into the Throne Room alone.”
paragraphs.cn: 你必须一个人走进宝座大厅。”

paragraphs.en: She opened a little door and Dorothy walked boldly through and found herself in a wonderful place.
paragraphs.cn: 她打开一扇小门，多萝西勇敢地走了进去，发现自己在一个很棒的地方。

paragraphs.en: It was a big, round room with a high arched roof, and the walls and ceiling and floor were covered with large emeralds set closely together.
paragraphs.cn: 这是一个又大又圆的房间，屋顶很高很高。墙上、天花板上和地板上，都紧紧地镶满了大大的祖母绿宝石。

paragraphs.en: In the center of the roof was a great light, as bright as the sun, which made the emeralds sparkle in a wonderful manner.
paragraphs.cn: 屋顶中间有一盏很亮的灯，亮得像太阳一样，把那些祖母绿宝石照得闪闪发光，真漂亮。

paragraphs.en: But what interested Dorothy most was the big throne of green marble that stood in the middle of the room.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，最让多萝西感兴趣的，是房间中央那把绿色的、大理石做的大宝座。

paragraphs.en: It was shaped like a chair and sparkled with gems, as did everything else.
paragraphs.cn: 它长得像一把椅子，上面镶满了闪闪发光的宝石，其他东西也是这样。

paragraphs.en: In the center of the chair was an enormous Head, without a body to support it or any arms or legs whatever.
paragraphs.cn: 椅子中间有一个巨大的头，没有身子，也没有胳膊和腿。

paragraphs.en: There was no hair upon this head, but it had eyes and a nose and mouth, and was much bigger than the head of the biggest giant.
paragraphs.cn: 这个头没有头发，可它有眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴，比最大的巨人的头还要大好多好多。

paragraphs.en: As Dorothy gazed upon this in wonder and fear, the eyes turned slowly and looked at her sharply and steadily.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西又好奇又害怕地看着这个大头，它的眼睛慢慢转动，又尖锐又一直盯着她看。

paragraphs.en: Then the mouth moved, and Dorothy heard a voice say:
paragraphs.cn: 然后，嘴巴动了，多萝西听到一个声音说：

paragraphs.en: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible.
paragraphs.cn: “我是奥兹大王，伟大又可怕的。

paragraphs.en: Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
paragraphs.cn: 你是谁呀？为什么要来找我呀？”

paragraphs.en: It was not such an awful voice as she had expected to come from the big Head; so she took courage and answered:
paragraphs.cn: 这声音没有她想象中从大头里发出的那么可怕；于是她鼓起勇气回答说：

paragraphs.en: “I am Dorothy, the Small and Meek.
paragraphs.cn: “我是多萝西，又小又乖的。

paragraphs.en: I have come to you for help.”
paragraphs.cn: 我是来请你帮忙的。”

paragraphs.en: The eyes looked at her thoughtfully for a full minute.
paragraphs.cn: 眼睛想了想，看了她整整一分钟。

paragraphs.en: Then said the voice:
paragraphs.cn: 然后，那个声音说：

paragraphs.en: “Where did you get the silver shoes?”
paragraphs.cn: “你的银鞋是从哪里来的呀？”

paragraphs.en: “I got them from the Wicked Witch of the East, when my house fell on her and killed her,” she replied.
paragraphs.cn: “我是从东方坏女巫那里得到的，我的房子掉下来，砸死了她。”她回答说。

paragraphs.en: “Where did you get the mark upon your forehead?” continued the voice.
paragraphs.cn: “你额头上的印记是怎么来的呀？”那个声音接着问。

paragraphs.en: “That is where the Good Witch of the North kissed me when she bade me good-bye and sent me to you,” said the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “那是北方好女巫亲我的时候，跟我说再见，然后送我来找你的。”女孩说。

paragraphs.en: Again the eyes looked at her sharply, and they saw she was telling the truth.
paragraphs.cn: 眼睛又尖锐地看了看她，发现她说的是真话。

paragraphs.en: Then Oz asked, “What do you wish me to do?”
paragraphs.cn: 然后，奥兹大王问：“你希望我为你做什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Send me back to Kansas, where my Aunt Em and Uncle Henry are,” she answered earnestly.
paragraphs.cn: “送我回堪萨斯去吧，我的艾姆婶婶和亨利叔叔都在那里呢。”她很认真地回答说。

paragraphs.en: “I don’t like your country, although it is so beautiful.
paragraphs.cn: “我不喜欢你的国家，虽然它很漂亮。

paragraphs.en: And I am sure Aunt Em will be dreadfully worried over my being away so long.”
paragraphs.cn: 我肯定 艾姆婶婶 会很担心我离开这么久。”

paragraphs.en: The eyes winked three times, and then they turned up to the ceiling and down to the floor and rolled around so queerly that they seemed to see every part of the room.
paragraphs.cn: 那双眼睛眨了三下，然后往天花板上看，又往地板上看，还古怪地转来转去，好像看到了房间的每个角落。

paragraphs.en: And at last they looked at Dorothy again.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，它们又看向了 多萝西。
