paragraphs.en: “Why should I do this for you?” asked Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “我为什么要帮你做这个呢？” 奥兹大王 问。

paragraphs.en: “Because you are strong and I am weak; because you are a Great Wizard and I am only a little girl.”
paragraphs.cn: “因为你很强壮，我很弱小；因为你是个大巫师，我只是个小女孩。”

paragraphs.en: “But you were strong enough to kill the Wicked Witch of the East,” said Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “可是，你已经很厉害了，能杀死 东方坏女巫，” 奥兹大王 说。

paragraphs.en: “That just happened,” returned Dorothy simply; “I could not help it.”
paragraphs.cn: “那只是碰巧发生的，” 多萝西 简单地说，“我控制不了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said the Head, “I will give you my answer.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，”那个头说，“我会给你我的答案。

paragraphs.en: You have no right to expect me to send you back to Kansas unless you do something for me in return.
paragraphs.cn: 你不应该指望我送你回 堪萨斯，除非你也能为我做点什么。

paragraphs.en: In this country everyone must pay for everything he gets.
paragraphs.cn: 在这个国家，每个人得到东西都要付出代价。

paragraphs.en: If you wish me to use my magic power to send you home again you must do something for me first.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你想我用魔法送你回家，你必须先为我做件事。

paragraphs.en: Help me and I will help you.”
paragraphs.cn: 你帮我，我帮你。”

paragraphs.en: “What must I do?” asked the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “我必须做什么呢？”小女孩问。

paragraphs.en: “Kill the Wicked Witch of the West,” answered Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “杀死 西方坏女巫，” 奥兹大王 回答。

paragraphs.en: “But I cannot!” exclaimed Dorothy, greatly surprised.
paragraphs.cn: “可是我做不到啊！” 多萝西 非常吃惊地叫道。

paragraphs.en: “You killed the Witch of the East and you wear the silver shoes, which bear a powerful charm.
paragraphs.cn: “你杀死了东方的女巫，还穿着那双带有强大魔力的银鞋。

paragraphs.en: There is now but one Wicked Witch left in all this land, and when you can tell me she is dead I will send you back to Kansas—but not before.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在这个地方只剩下了一个 坏女巫，等你告诉我她死了，我就会送你回 堪萨斯——但不是现在。”

paragraphs.en: The little girl began to weep, she was so much disappointed; and the eyes winked again and looked upon her anxiously, as if the Great Oz felt that she could help him if she would.
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩开始哭了，她太失望了；那双眼睛又眨了眨，焦急地看着她，好像伟大的 奥兹大王 觉得她要是愿意就可以帮到他。

paragraphs.en: “I never killed anything, willingly,” she sobbed.
paragraphs.cn: “我从来没有故意杀死过任何东西，”她抽泣着说。

paragraphs.en: “Even if I wanted to, how could I kill the Wicked Witch?
paragraphs.cn: “就算我想做，我怎么能杀死 坏女巫 呢？

paragraphs.en: If you, who are Great and Terrible, cannot kill her yourself, how do you expect me to do it?”
paragraphs.cn: 连您这样又伟大又可怕的都杀不死她，您怎么能指望我去做呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I do not know,” said the Head; “but that is my answer, and until the Wicked Witch dies you will not see your uncle and aunt again.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，”那个头说，“但这就是我的答案，在 坏女巫 死之前，你不会再见到你的叔叔和婶婶了。

paragraphs.en: Remember that the Witch is Wicked—tremendously Wicked—and ought to be killed.
paragraphs.cn: 记住，这个女巫是邪恶的——非常邪恶——应该被杀死。

paragraphs.en: Now go, and do not ask to see me again until you have done your task.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在走吧，在你完成任务之前，不要再要求见我。”

paragraphs.en: Sorrowfully Dorothy left the Throne Room and went back where the Lion and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were waiting to hear what Oz had said to her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 伤心地离开了王座大厅，回到 狮子、稻草人 和 铁皮人 正在等她，想听听 奥兹大王 对她说了什么的地方。

paragraphs.en: “There is no hope for me,” she said sadly, “for Oz will not send me home until I have killed the Wicked Witch of the West; and that I can never do.”
paragraphs.cn: “我没有希望了，”她伤心地说，“因为 奥兹大王 不会送我回家，除非我杀死了 西方坏女巫；而那是我永远也做不到的。”

paragraphs.en: Her friends were sorry, but could do nothing to help her; so Dorothy went to her own room and lay down on the bed and cried herself to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 她的朋友们都很难过，但帮不了她什么；于是 多萝西 回到自己的房间，躺在床上，哭着睡着了。

paragraphs.en: The next morning the soldier with the green whiskers came to the Scarecrow and said:
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，那个留着绿色胡子的士兵来到 稻草人 面前，说：

paragraphs.en: “Come with me, for Oz has sent for you.”
paragraphs.cn: “跟我来，因为 奥兹大王 找你。”

paragraphs.en: So the Scarecrow followed him and was admitted into the great Throne Room, where he saw, sitting in the emerald throne, a most lovely Lady.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，稻草人跟着他，进了一个大大的王座厅。他看到一位很漂亮的女士，正坐在绿色的宝座上。

paragraphs.en: She was dressed in green silk gauze and wore upon her flowing green locks a crown of jewels.
paragraphs.cn: 她穿着绿色的丝绸裙子，头上戴着一个亮晶晶的宝石皇冠。

paragraphs.en: Growing from her shoulders were wings, gorgeous in color and so light that they fluttered if the slightest breath of air reached them.
paragraphs.cn: 她的肩膀上长着一对翅膀，颜色特别好看，轻得连一点点风都能让它们扇动起来。

paragraphs.en: When the Scarecrow had bowed, as prettily as his straw stuffing would let him, before this beautiful creature, she looked upon him sweetly, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人努力地向这位美丽的女士鞠了个躬（他身体里都是稻草，鞠躬可不容易）。女士甜甜地看着他，说：

paragraphs.en: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible.
paragraphs.cn: “我是奥兹大王，又厉害又吓人。”

paragraphs.en: Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
paragraphs.cn: “你是谁呀？为什么来找我呢？”

paragraphs.en: Now the Scarecrow, who had expected to see the great Head Dorothy had told him of, was much astonished; but he answered her bravely.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人原本以为会看到多萝西说过的大脑袋，结果很吃惊。但他还是勇敢地回答了。

paragraphs.en: “I am only a Scarecrow, stuffed with straw.
paragraphs.cn: “我只是一个身体里装满稻草的稻草人。”

paragraphs.en: Therefore I have no brains, and I come to you praying that you will put brains in my head instead of straw, so that I may become as much a man as any other in your dominions.”
paragraphs.cn: “所以我没有脑子。我来求您，请您把脑子放进我的头里，不要再装稻草了。这样我就可以像您王国里的其他人一样，变成一个真正的人了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why should I do this for you?” asked the Lady.
paragraphs.cn: “我为什么要帮你做这个呢？”女士问。

paragraphs.en: “Because you are wise and powerful, and no one else can help me,” answered the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “因为您又聪明又厉害，别人都帮不了我。”稻草人回答。

paragraphs.en: “I never grant favors without some return,” said Oz; “but this much I will promise.
paragraphs.cn: “我从来不白白帮人忙。”奥兹大王说，“但是我可以答应你一件事。”

paragraphs.en: If you will kill for me the Wicked Witch of the West, I will bestow upon you a great many brains, and such good brains that you will be the wisest man in all the Land of Oz.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果你帮我杀死西方坏女巫，我就会给你很多很多脑子，而且是很棒的脑子！你会成为整个奥兹国里最聪明的人。”

paragraphs.en: “I thought you asked Dorothy to kill the Witch,” said the Scarecrow, in surprise.
paragraphs.cn: “我以为您让多萝西去杀女巫呢。”稻草人很惊讶地说。

paragraphs.en: “So I did.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，我确实是这么说的。”

paragraphs.en: I don’t care who kills her.
paragraphs.cn: “我才不在乎是谁杀了她呢。”

paragraphs.en: But until she is dead I will not grant your wish.
paragraphs.cn: “但如果她没死，我就不会帮你实现愿望。”

paragraphs.en: Now go, and do not seek me again until you have earned the brains you so greatly desire.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在走吧，等你得到了你特别想要的脑子以后，再来找我。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow went sorrowfully back to his friends and told them what Oz had said; and Dorothy was surprised to find that the Great Wizard was not a Head, as she had seen him, but a lovely Lady.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人伤心地回到朋友身边，告诉他们奥兹大王说了什么。多萝西很惊讶地发现，原来那个伟大的魔法师不是她以前见过的大脑袋，而是一位漂亮的女士。

paragraphs.en: “All the same,” said the Scarecrow, “she needs a heart as much as the Tin Woodman.”
paragraphs.cn: “不过呀，”稻草人说，“她和铁皮人一样，也需要一颗心。”

paragraphs.en: On the next morning the soldier with the green whiskers came to the Tin Woodman and said:
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，那个长着绿色胡子的士兵来到铁皮人面前，对他说：

paragraphs.en: “Oz has sent for you.
paragraphs.cn: “奥兹大王让你过去。”

paragraphs.en: Follow me.”
paragraphs.cn: “跟着我来。”

paragraphs.en: So the Tin Woodman followed him and came to the great Throne Room.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，铁皮人跟着他，来到了大大的王座厅。

paragraphs.en: He did not know whether he would find Oz a lovely Lady or a Head, but he hoped it would be the lovely Lady.
paragraphs.cn: 他不知道这次看到奥兹大王会是漂亮的女士还是大脑袋，但他希望是那位漂亮的女士。

paragraphs.en: “For,” he said to himself, “if it is the head, I am sure I shall not be given a heart, since a head has no heart of its own and therefore cannot feel for me.
paragraphs.cn: “因为呀，”他心里想，“如果是那个大脑袋，我肯定得不到一颗心。大脑袋自己没有心，所以也不会明白我的感受。”

paragraphs.en: But if it is the lovely Lady I shall beg hard for a heart, for all ladies are themselves said to be kindly hearted.”
paragraphs.cn: “但如果是那位漂亮的女士，我就会拼命求她给我一颗心。因为大家都说，女士们的心都很善良。”

paragraphs.en: But when the Woodman entered the great Throne Room he saw neither the Head nor the Lady, for Oz had taken the shape of a most terrible Beast.
paragraphs.cn: 但当铁皮人走进大大的王座厅时，他没有看到大脑袋，也没有看到那位女士。因为奥兹大王变成了一只特别可怕的野兽。

paragraphs.en: It was nearly as big as an elephant, and the green throne seemed hardly strong enough to hold its weight.
paragraphs.cn: 它差不多和大象一样大，那个绿色的宝座好像都快承受不住它的重量了。

paragraphs.en: The Beast had a head like that of a rhinoceros, only there were five eyes in its face.
paragraphs.cn: 这只野兽的头长得像犀牛，不过它的脸上长了五只眼睛。

paragraphs.en: There were five long arms growing out of its body, and it also had five long, slim legs.
paragraphs.cn: 它身上长着五条长长的胳膊，还有五条又长又细的腿。

paragraphs.en: Thick, woolly hair covered every part of it, and a more dreadful-looking monster could not be imagined.
paragraphs.cn: 它全身都盖着厚厚的羊毛状的毛，真是想不到还有比它更可怕的怪兽了。

paragraphs.en: It was fortunate the Tin Woodman had no heart at that moment, for it would have beat loud and fast from terror.
paragraphs.cn: 幸好那个时候，铁皮人没有心脏，不然它会因为害怕而心跳得又响又快。

paragraphs.en: But being only tin, the Woodman was not at all afraid, although he was much disappointed.
paragraphs.cn: 但因为铁皮人只是个铁皮人，所以一点也不害怕，虽然它很失望。

paragraphs.en: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible,” spoke the Beast, in a voice that was one great roar.
paragraphs.cn: “我是奥兹大王，那个又伟大又可怕的，”野兽吼着说，声音像一声巨吼。

paragraphs.en: “Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
paragraphs.cn: “你是谁？为什么要找我？”

paragraphs.en: “I am a Woodman, and made of tin.
paragraphs.cn: “我是一个铁皮人，是用铁皮做的。”

paragraphs.en: Therefore I have no heart, and cannot love.
paragraphs.cn: “所以我没有心，也无法爱人。”

paragraphs.en: I pray you to give me a heart that I may be as other men are.”
paragraphs.cn: “我求你给我一颗心，让我能像其他人一样。”

paragraphs.en: “Why should I do this?” demanded the Beast.
paragraphs.cn: “我为什么要这么做？”野兽问道。

paragraphs.en: “Because I ask it, and you alone can grant my request,” answered the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “因为我请求你，而且只有你才能帮我这个忙，”铁皮人回答。

paragraphs.en: Oz gave a low growl at this, but said, gruffly: “If you indeed desire a heart, you must earn it.”
paragraphs.cn: 听到这话，奥兹大王低吼了一声，然后粗声说：“如果你真的想要一颗心，你就必须去争取。”

paragraphs.en: “How?” asked the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “怎么争取？”铁皮人问。

paragraphs.en: “Help Dorothy to kill the Wicked Witch of the West,” replied the Beast.
paragraphs.cn: “帮多萝西杀死西方坏女巫，”野兽回答。

paragraphs.en: “When the Witch is dead, come to me, and I will then give you the biggest and kindest and most loving heart in all the Land of Oz.”
paragraphs.cn: “当女巫死了，你再来找我，我就会给你整个奥兹国里最大、最善良、最有爱心的心。”

paragraphs.en: So the Tin Woodman was forced to return sorrowfully to his friends and tell them of the terrible Beast he had seen.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，铁皮人只好伤心地回到朋友们身边，告诉他们它看到的那个可怕的野兽。

paragraphs.en: They all wondered greatly at the many forms the Great Wizard could take upon himself, and the Lion said:
paragraphs.cn: 他们都很好奇，大魔法师能变成这么多样子，狮子说：

paragraphs.en: “If he is a Beast when I go to see him, I shall roar my loudest, and so frighten him that he will grant all I ask.
paragraphs.cn: “如果我去见他时，他是一只野兽，我就大声吼叫，吓得他答应我所有的要求。”

paragraphs.en: And if he is the lovely Lady, I shall pretend to spring upon her, and so compel her to do my bidding.
paragraphs.cn: “如果他是一个可爱的女士，我就假装扑向她，逼她听我的话。”

paragraphs.en: And if he is the great Head, he will be at my mercy; for I will roll this head all about the room until he promises to give us what we desire.
paragraphs.cn: “如果他是一个巨大的头，那他就会任我摆布；我会把这个头在房间里滚来滚去，直到他答应给我们想要的东西。”

paragraphs.en: So be of good cheer, my friends, for all will yet be well.”
paragraphs.cn: “所以，我的朋友们，开心点吧，一切都会好起来的。”

paragraphs.en: The next morning the soldier with the green whiskers led the Lion to the great Throne Room and bade him enter the presence of Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，那个留着绿色胡子的士兵带着狮子来到巨大的宝座室，让它进去见奥兹大王。

paragraphs.en: The Lion at once passed through the door, and glancing around saw, to his surprise, that before the throne was a Ball of Fire, so fierce and glowing he could scarcely bear to gaze upon it.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子立刻穿过门，环顾四周，惊讶地看到宝座前有一个火球，又凶又亮，它几乎不敢直视。

paragraphs.en: His first thought was that Oz had by accident caught on fire and was burning up; but when he tried to go nearer, the heat was so intense that it singed his whiskers, and he crept back tremblingly to a spot nearer the door.
paragraphs.cn: 它第一个念头是奥兹大王不小心着火了，正在燃烧；但当它试图走近时，热量太大了，把它的胡须都烧焦了，它颤抖着爬回离门更近的地方。

paragraphs.en: Then a low, quiet voice came from the Ball of Fire, and these were the words it spoke:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，一个低沉、安静的声音从火球中传来，它说的话是：

paragraphs.en: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible.
paragraphs.cn: “我是奥兹大王，那个又伟大又可怕的。”

paragraphs.en: Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
paragraphs.cn: “你是谁？为什么要找我？”

paragraphs.en: And the Lion answered, “I am a Cowardly Lion, afraid of everything.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子回答说：“我是一个胆小的狮子，什么都怕。”

paragraphs.en: I came to you to beg that you give me courage, so that in reality I may become the King of Beasts, as men call me.”
paragraphs.cn: “我来求你给我勇气，这样我才能真正成为人们口中的万兽之王。”

paragraphs.en: “Why should I give you courage?” demanded Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “我为什么要给你勇气？”奥兹大王问道。

paragraphs.en: “Because of all Wizards you are the greatest, and alone have power to grant my request,” answered the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “因为在所有巫师里，您最厉害，只有您能帮我实现愿望，”狮子回答说。

paragraphs.en: The Ball of Fire burned fiercely for a time, and the voice said, “Bring me proof that the Wicked Witch is dead, and that moment I will give you courage.
paragraphs.cn: 火球猛烈地烧了一会儿，那个声音说：“如果你能证明坏女巫已经死了，我立刻就给你勇气。

paragraphs.en: But as long as the Witch lives, you must remain a coward.”
paragraphs.cn: “但是只要巫婆还活着，你就只能是个胆小鬼。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion was angry at this speech, but could say nothing in reply, and while he stood silently gazing at the Ball of Fire it became so furiously hot that he turned tail and rushed from the room.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子听了这番话很生气，却说不出话来反驳。他静静地看着火球，火球变得太热了，他只好转身冲出了房间。

paragraphs.en: He was glad to find his friends waiting for him, and told them of his terrible interview with the Wizard.
paragraphs.cn: 他很高兴看到朋友们在等他，然后把和巫师糟糕的谈话告诉了他们。

paragraphs.en: “What shall we do now?” asked Dorothy sadly.
paragraphs.cn: “我们现在该怎么办呢？”多萝西伤心地问。

paragraphs.en: “There is only one thing we can do,” returned the Lion, “and that is to go to the land of the Winkies, seek out the Wicked Witch, and destroy her.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们只有一件事可以做，”狮子回答说，“那就是去温基人的土地，找到坏女巫，然后消灭她。”

paragraphs.en: “But suppose we cannot?” said the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “但如果我们做不到呢？”女孩说。

paragraphs.en: “Then I shall never have courage,” declared the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “那我就永远没有勇气了，”狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “And I shall never have brains,” added the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “那我就永远没有脑子了，”稻草人补充说。

paragraphs.en: “And I shall never have a heart,” spoke the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “那我就永远没有心了，”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “And I shall never see Aunt Em and Uncle Henry,” said Dorothy, beginning to cry.
paragraphs.cn: “那我就永远见不到艾姆婶婶和亨利叔叔了，”多萝西说着，开始哭了。

paragraphs.en: “Be careful!” cried the green girl. “The tears will fall on your green silk gown and spot it.”
paragraphs.cn: “小心！”那个绿衣女孩喊道，“眼泪会滴到你的绿丝裙上，弄脏它的。”

paragraphs.en: So Dorothy dried her eyes and said, “I suppose we must try it; but I am sure I do not want to kill anybody, even to see Aunt Em again.”
paragraphs.cn: 于是多萝西擦干了眼睛说：“我想我们必须试试；但我真的不想杀任何人，哪怕是为了再见到艾姆婶婶。”

paragraphs.en: “I will go with you; but I’m too much of a coward to kill the Witch,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “我跟你们一起去；但我太胆小了，不敢杀巫婆，”狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “I will go too,” declared the Scarecrow; “but I shall not be of much help to you, I am such a fool.”
paragraphs.cn: “我也去，”稻草人说；“但我帮不了你们太多忙，我太笨了。”

paragraphs.en: “I haven’t the heart to harm even a Witch,” remarked the Tin Woodman; “but if you go I certainly shall go with you.”
paragraphs.cn: “我可没有心去伤害哪怕一个巫婆，”铁皮人说；“但如果你们去，我一定会跟着你们。”

paragraphs.en: Therefore it was decided to start upon their journey the next morning, and the Woodman sharpened his axe on a green grindstone and had all his joints properly oiled.
paragraphs.cn: 于是大家决定第二天早上就开始旅程，铁皮人在一个绿色的磨刀石上磨了他的斧头，还把他的关节都好好地上了油。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow stuffed himself with fresh straw and Dorothy put new paint on his eyes that he might see better.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人给自己塞满了新鲜的稻草，多萝西在他的眼睛上涂了新颜料，这样他就能看得更清楚了。

paragraphs.en: The green girl, who was very kind to them, filled Dorothy’s basket with good things to eat, and fastened a little bell around Toto’s neck with a green ribbon.
paragraphs.cn: 那个对他们很好的绿衣女孩，给多萝西的篮子里装满了好吃的东西，还用一条绿色的丝带在托托的脖子上系了一个小铃铛。

paragraphs.en: They went to bed quite early and slept soundly until daylight, when they were awakened by the crowing of a green cock that lived in the back yard of the Palace, and the cackling of a hen that had laid a green egg.
paragraphs.cn: 他们很早就睡了，一直睡得很香，直到天亮。天亮时，他们被住在宫殿后院的一只绿色公鸡的叫声，和一只下了绿色蛋的母鸡的咯咯声吵醒了。

chapters.title_en: The Search for the Wicked Witch

paragraphs.en: The soldier with the green whiskers led them through the streets of the Emerald City until they reached the room where the Guardian of the Gates lived.
paragraphs.cn: 那个绿胡子士兵带着他们穿过翡翠城的街道，直到他们到达了城门守卫住的房间。

paragraphs.en: This officer unlocked their spectacles to put them back in his great box, and then he politely opened the gate for our friends.
paragraphs.cn: 这位官员解开了他们的眼镜，把它们放回他的大盒子里，然后他礼貌地为我们的朋友们打开了大门。

paragraphs.en: “Which road leads to the Wicked Witch of the West?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “哪条路通向西方坏女巫？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “There is no road,” answered the Guardian of the Gates.
paragraphs.cn: “没有路，”城门守卫回答说。

paragraphs.en: “No one ever wishes to go that way.”
paragraphs.cn: “从来没有人想走那条路。”

paragraphs.en: “How, then, are we to find her?” inquired the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “那我们怎么才能找到她呢？”女孩问道。

paragraphs.en: “That will be easy,” replied the man, “for when she knows you are in the country of the Winkies she will find you, and make you all her slaves.”
paragraphs.cn: “那很容易，”那人回答说，“因为当她知道你们在温基人的国家时，她会找到你们，并把你们都变成她的奴隶。”

paragraphs.en: “Perhaps not,” said the Scarecrow, “for we mean to destroy her.”
paragraphs.cn: “也许不会，”稻草人说，“因为我们打算消灭她。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that is different,” said the Guardian of the Gates.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，那可不一样了，”城门守卫说。

paragraphs.en: “No one has ever destroyed her before, so I naturally thought she would make slaves of you, as she has of the rest.
paragraphs.cn: “以前没人打败过她，我以为她会把你们变成奴隶，就像对其他人那样。

paragraphs.en: But take care; for she is wicked and fierce, and may not allow you to destroy her.
paragraphs.cn: 不过你们要小心哦！她很坏很凶，可能不会让你们打败她。

paragraphs.en: Keep to the West, where the sun sets, and you cannot fail to find her.”
paragraphs.cn: 一直往西边走，就是太阳下山的地方，你们肯定能找到她。”

paragraphs.en: They thanked him and bade him good-bye, and turned toward the West, walking over fields of soft grass dotted here and there with daisies and buttercups.
paragraphs.cn: 他们谢谢他，跟他说了再见，就往西边走。他们走过软软的草地，草地上开着小雏菊和金凤花。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy still wore the pretty silk dress she had put on in the palace, but now, to her surprise, she found it was no longer green, but pure white.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西还穿着在宫殿里的漂亮丝绸裙子，但让她惊讶的是，裙子不再是绿色，而是纯白色了。

paragraphs.en: The ribbon around Toto’s neck had also lost its green color and was as white as Dorothy’s dress.
paragraphs.cn: 托托脖子上的丝带也变白了，和多萝西的裙子一样白。

paragraphs.en: The Emerald City was soon left far behind.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，翡翠城就被远远地甩在后面了。

paragraphs.en: As they advanced the ground became rougher and hillier, for there were no farms nor houses in this country of the West, and the ground was untilled.
paragraphs.cn: 他们往前走，地面变得越来越不平坦，还出现了小山坡。因为西边的这片土地上，没有农场，没有房子，也没有人耕地。

paragraphs.en: In the afternoon the sun shone hot in their faces, for there were no trees to offer them shade; so that before night Dorothy and Toto and the Lion were tired, and lay down upon the grass and fell asleep, with the Woodman and the Scarecrow keeping watch.
paragraphs.cn: 下午，太阳晒得他们的脸热热的，因为这里没有大树遮荫。所以天黑前，多萝西、托托和狮子都累了，躺在草地上睡着了。铁皮人和稻草人帮他们守夜。

paragraphs.en: Now the Wicked Witch of the West had but one eye, yet that was as powerful as a telescope, and could see everywhere.
paragraphs.cn: 那个西方坏女巫只有一只眼睛，但这只眼睛像望远镜一样厉害，能看到所有地方。

paragraphs.en: So, as she sat in the door of her castle, she happened to look around and saw Dorothy lying asleep, with her friends all about her.
paragraphs.cn: 她坐在城堡门口，不经意间往四周一看，就看见睡着的多萝西，她的朋友们都在她身边。

paragraphs.en: They were a long distance off, but the Wicked Witch was angry to find them in her country; so she blew upon a silver whistle that hung around her neck.
paragraphs.cn: 他们离得很远，但坏女巫发现他们在自己的地盘上，非常生气。于是，她吹响了挂在脖子上的银哨子。

paragraphs.en: At once there came running to her from all directions a pack of great wolves.
paragraphs.cn: 一下子，一大群大灰狼就从四面八方跑到了她身边。

paragraphs.en: They had long legs and fierce eyes and sharp teeth.
paragraphs.cn: 它们有长长的腿，凶狠的眼睛，还有尖尖的牙齿。

paragraphs.en: “Go to those people,” said the Witch, “and tear them to pieces.”
paragraphs.cn: “去把那些人撕成碎片！”女巫说。

paragraphs.en: “Are you not going to make them your slaves?” asked the leader of the wolves.
paragraphs.cn: “你不是要把他们变成奴隶吗？”狼头领问。

paragraphs.en: “No,” she answered, “one is of tin, and one of straw; one is a girl and another a Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “不，”她回答，“一个是铁皮，一个是稻草；一个是小女孩，另一个是狮子。

paragraphs.en: None of them is fit to work, so you may tear them into small pieces.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们没一个能干活的，所以你们可以把他们撕成小碎片。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well,” said the wolf, and he dashed away at full speed, followed by the others.
paragraphs.cn: “好嘞！”狼说，然后它就飞快地冲了出去，其他狼也跟着它。

paragraphs.en: It was lucky the Scarecrow and the Woodman were wide awake and heard the wolves coming.
paragraphs.cn: 幸好稻草人和铁皮人都醒着，听到了狼群来了。

paragraphs.en: “This is my fight,” said the Woodman, “so get behind me and I will meet them as they come.”
paragraphs.cn: “这是我的战斗，”铁皮人说，“你们躲在我后面，我来对付它们。”

paragraphs.en: He seized his axe, which he had made very sharp, and as the leader of the wolves came on the Tin Woodman swung his arm and chopped the wolf’s head from its body, so that it immediately died.
paragraphs.cn: 他拿起磨得很锋利的斧子。当狼头领冲上来时，铁皮人一挥手，就把狼的头砍了下来，狼立刻就死了。

paragraphs.en: As soon as he could raise his axe another wolf came up, and he also fell under the sharp edge of the Tin Woodman’s weapon.
paragraphs.cn: 他刚举起斧子，又一只狼冲了上来，也倒在了铁皮人的锋利武器下。

paragraphs.en: There were forty wolves, and forty times a wolf was killed, so that at last they all lay dead in a heap before the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: 一共有四十只狼，铁皮人杀了四十只，最后它们都堆在铁皮人面前死掉了。

paragraphs.en: Then he put down his axe and sat beside the Scarecrow, who said, “It was a good fight, friend.”
paragraphs.cn: 然后他放下斧子，坐在稻草人旁边，稻草人说：“朋友，你打得真棒！”

paragraphs.en: They waited until Dorothy awoke the next morning.
paragraphs.cn: 他们等到第二天早上多萝西醒来。

paragraphs.en: The little girl was quite frightened when she saw the great pile of shaggy wolves, but the Tin Woodman told her all.
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩看到一大堆毛茸茸的狼，吓得不轻，但铁皮人把所有事情都告诉了她。

paragraphs.en: She thanked him for saving them and sat down to breakfast, after which they started again upon their journey.
paragraphs.cn: 她谢谢他救了大家，然后坐下来吃早饭。吃完饭，他们又继续赶路了。

paragraphs.en: Now this same morning the Wicked Witch came to the door of her castle and looked out with her one eye that could see far off.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这天早上，坏女巫来到城堡门口，用她那只看得可远的眼睛往外看。

paragraphs.en: She saw all her wolves lying dead, and the strangers still traveling through her country.
paragraphs.cn: 她看到自己的狼都死了，那些陌生人还在她的地盘上走着。

paragraphs.en: This made her angrier than before, and she blew her silver whistle twice.
paragraphs.cn: 这让她更生气了，她吹了两下银哨子。

paragraphs.en: Straightway a great flock of wild crows came flying toward her, enough to darken the sky.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，一大群野乌鸦飞来了，它们多得把天空都遮住了。

paragraphs.en: And the Wicked Witch said to the King Crow, “Fly at once to the strangers; peck out their eyes and tear them to pieces.”
paragraphs.cn: 那个坏女巫对乌鸦王说：“快飞过去，把陌生人的眼睛啄出来，把他们撕碎！”

paragraphs.en: The wild crows flew in one great flock toward Dorothy and her companions.
paragraphs.cn: 野乌鸦一大群地飞向多萝西和她的朋友们。

paragraphs.en: When the little girl saw them coming she was afraid.
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩看到乌鸦飞来，有点害怕。

paragraphs.en: But the Scarecrow said, “This is my battle, so lie down beside me and you will not be harmed.”
paragraphs.cn: 但是稻草人说：“这是我的事情，你们躺在我旁边，就不会受伤。”

paragraphs.en: So they all lay upon the ground except the Scarecrow, and he stood up and stretched out his arms.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，除了稻草人，大家都躺在地上。他站起来，伸开双臂。

paragraphs.en: And when the crows saw him they were frightened, as these birds always are by scarecrows, and did not dare to come any nearer.
paragraphs.cn: 乌鸦们看到他，吓了一跳。因为这些鸟总是害怕稻草人，所以不敢再靠近。

paragraphs.en: But the King Crow said:
paragraphs.cn: 但是乌鸦王说：

paragraphs.en: “It is only a stuffed man.
paragraphs.cn: “这只是个用稻草做的假人。”

paragraphs.en: I will peck his eyes out.”
paragraphs.cn: “我要把他的眼睛啄出来。”

paragraphs.en: The King Crow flew at the Scarecrow, who caught it by the head and twisted its neck until it died.
paragraphs.cn: 乌鸦王飞向稻草人，稻草人抓住了它的头，把它的脖子扭断，乌鸦就死了。

paragraphs.en: And then another crow flew at him, and the Scarecrow twisted its neck also.
paragraphs.cn: 然后另一只乌鸦飞过来，稻草人也扭断了它的脖子。

paragraphs.en: There were forty crows, and forty times the Scarecrow twisted a neck, until at last all were lying dead beside him.
paragraphs.cn: 一共有四十只乌鸦，稻草人扭了四十次脖子，直到所有的乌鸦都死了，躺在他身边。

paragraphs.en: Then he called to his companions to rise, and again they went upon their journey.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他叫伙伴们起来，他们又继续赶路了。

paragraphs.en: When the Wicked Witch looked out again and saw all her crows lying in a heap, she got into a terrible rage, and blew three times upon her silver whistle.
paragraphs.cn: 那个坏女巫又往外看，看到她的乌鸦都死成一堆，她气得不得了，吹了三下银哨子。

paragraphs.en: Forthwith there was heard a great buzzing in the air, and a swarm of black bees came flying toward her.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，空中传来一阵嗡嗡声，一大群黑蜜蜂飞向她。

paragraphs.en: “Go to the strangers and sting them to death!” commanded the Witch, and the bees turned and flew rapidly until they came to where Dorothy and her friends were walking.
paragraphs.cn: “去把陌生人蜇死！”女巫命令道。蜜蜂们很快飞到多萝西和她朋友们的地方。

paragraphs.en: But the Woodman had seen them coming, and the Scarecrow had decided what to do.
paragraphs.cn: 但是铁皮人已经看到它们飞来了，稻草人也想好了办法。

paragraphs.en: “Take out my straw and scatter it over the little girl and the dog and the Lion,” he said to the Woodman, “and the bees cannot sting them.”
paragraphs.cn: 他对铁皮人说：“把我身上的稻草拿出来，撒在小女孩、小狗和狮子身上，这样蜜蜂就蜇不到他们了。”

paragraphs.en: This the Woodman did, and as Dorothy lay close beside the Lion and held Toto in her arms, the straw covered them entirely.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人照做了。当多萝西紧紧地躺在狮子旁边，怀里抱着托托时，稻草把他们全都盖住了。

paragraphs.en: The bees came and found no one but the Woodman to sting, so they flew at him and broke off all their stings against the tin, without hurting the Woodman at all.
paragraphs.cn: 蜜蜂飞来，发现只有铁皮人可以蜇，于是它们都飞向他，把所有的毒刺都刺在铁皮上，一点也没伤到铁皮人。

paragraphs.en: And as bees cannot live when their stings are broken that was the end of the black bees, and they lay scattered thick about the Woodman, like little heaps of fine coal.
paragraphs.cn: 蜜蜂的毒刺断了就活不了。所以那些黑蜜蜂都死了，它们密密麻麻地散落在铁皮人身边，就像一小堆堆细小的煤炭。

paragraphs.en: Then Dorothy and the Lion got up, and the girl helped the Tin Woodman put the straw back into the Scarecrow again, until he was as good as ever.
paragraphs.cn: 然后多萝西和狮子站起来，小女孩帮铁皮人把稻草重新放回稻草人里面，他又变得和以前一样好。

paragraphs.en: So they started upon their journey once more.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们又出发了。

paragraphs.en: The Wicked Witch was so angry when she saw her black bees in little heaps like fine coal that she stamped her foot and tore her hair and gnashed her teeth.
paragraphs.cn: 那个坏女巫看到黑蜜蜂死成一小堆堆像细煤炭一样，气得直跺脚，撕扯自己的头发，还咬牙切齿。

paragraphs.en: And then she called a dozen of her slaves, who were the Winkies, and gave them sharp spears, telling them to go to the strangers and destroy them.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她叫来十几个奴隶，也就是那些温基人，给了他们锋利的矛，让他们去把陌生人消灭掉。

paragraphs.en: The Winkies were not a brave people, but they had to do as they were told.
paragraphs.cn: 那些温基人不是很勇敢，但他们必须听命令。

paragraphs.en: So they marched away until they came near to Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们出发了，一直走到快靠近多萝西的地方。

paragraphs.en: Then the Lion gave a great roar and sprang towards them, and the poor Winkies were so frightened that they ran back as fast as they could.
paragraphs.cn: 然后狮子大吼一声，跳向他们，可怜的温基人吓坏了，撒腿就跑了回去。

paragraphs.en: When they returned to the castle the Wicked Witch beat them well with a strap, and sent them back to their work, after which she sat down to think what she should do next.
paragraphs.cn: 当他们回到城堡，坏女巫用鞭子好好地教训了他们，然后让他们继续工作。接着，她坐下来想，接下来该怎么做。

paragraphs.en: She could not understand how all her plans to destroy these strangers had failed; but she was a powerful Witch, as well as a wicked one, and she soon made up her mind how to act.
paragraphs.cn: 她不明白，为什么她想赶走这些陌生人的办法都失败了。不过她是个很厉害、也很坏的女巫，所以她很快就想好了下一步该怎么做。

paragraphs.en: There was, in her cupboard, a Golden Cap, with a circle of diamonds and rubies running round it.
paragraphs.cn: 在她的柜子里，有一个金冠。它上面有一圈亮晶晶的钻石和红宝石。

paragraphs.en: This Golden Cap had a charm.
paragraphs.cn: 这个金冠有魔力。

paragraphs.en: Whoever owned it could call three times upon the Winged Monkeys, who would obey any order they were given.
paragraphs.cn: 谁戴上它，就能叫飞猴三次。飞猴会听从他说的任何命令。

paragraphs.en: But no person could command these strange creatures more than three times.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，没有人能命令这些奇怪的家伙超过三次。

paragraphs.en: Twice already the Wicked Witch had used the charm of the Cap.
paragraphs.cn: 坏女巫已经用过帽子上的魔力两次了。

paragraphs.en: Once was when she had made the Winkies her slaves, and set herself to rule over their country.
paragraphs.cn: 第一次是她把温基人变成了自己的奴隶，还当上了他们的国王。

paragraphs.en: The Winged Monkeys had helped her do this.
paragraphs.cn: 飞猴帮她做到了这件事。

paragraphs.en: The second time was when she had fought against the Great Oz himself, and driven him out of the land of the West.
paragraphs.cn: 第二次是她和厉害的奥兹大王打架，把他赶出了西边的土地。

paragraphs.en: The Winged Monkeys had also helped her in doing this.
paragraphs.cn: 飞猴也帮她做到了这件事。

paragraphs.en: Only once more could she use this Golden Cap, for which reason she did not like to do so until all her other powers were exhausted.
paragraphs.cn: 她只能再用这个金冠一次了。所以，除非她其他的厉害本领都用完了，她才不想用它。

paragraphs.en: But now that her fierce wolves and her wild crows and her stinging bees were gone, and her slaves had been scared away by the Cowardly Lion, she saw there was only one way left to destroy Dorothy and her friends.
paragraphs.cn: 可是现在，她的坏狼、野乌鸦和会蜇人的蜜蜂都跑光了。她的奴隶也被胆小的狮子吓走了。她发现，只剩下最后一个办法可以赶走多萝西和她的朋友们了。

paragraphs.en: So the Wicked Witch took the Golden Cap from her cupboard and placed it upon her head.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，坏女巫从柜子里拿出金冠，戴在自己头上。

paragraphs.en: Then she stood upon her left foot and said, slowly:
paragraphs.cn: 然后她用左脚站着，慢慢地说：

paragraphs.en: “Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke!”
paragraphs.cn: “Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke！”

paragraphs.en: Next she stood upon her right foot and said:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，她用右脚站着，说：

paragraphs.en: “Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo!”
paragraphs.cn: “Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo！”

paragraphs.en: After this she stood upon both feet and cried in a loud voice:
paragraphs.cn: 说完，她两只脚都站好了，大声喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik!”
paragraphs.cn: “Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik！”

paragraphs.en: Now the charm began to work.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，魔力开始起作用了。

paragraphs.en: The sky was darkened, and a low rumbling sound was heard in the air.
paragraphs.cn: 天空变黑了，空气中传来一阵低沉的“轰隆隆”的声音。

paragraphs.en: There was a rushing of many wings, a great chattering and laughing, and the sun came out of the dark sky to show the Wicked Witch surrounded by a crowd of monkeys, each with a pair of immense and powerful wings on his shoulders.
paragraphs.cn: 好多翅膀“呼啦啦”地飞过，还传来一阵阵吱吱喳喳的说话声和笑声。太阳从黑乎乎的天空中露出来，大家看到坏女巫被一群猴子围住了。每只猴子的肩膀上都有一对很大很有力的翅膀。

paragraphs.en: One, much bigger than the others, seemed to be their leader.
paragraphs.cn: 其中有一只，比别的猴子大好多，它好像是猴子们的头儿。

paragraphs.en: He flew close to the Witch and said, “You have called us for the third and last time.
paragraphs.cn: 它飞到女巫身边说：“你已经叫我们第三次了，也是最后一次了。

paragraphs.en: What do you command?”
paragraphs.cn: 你有什么吩咐呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Go to the strangers who are within my land and destroy them all except the Lion,” said the Wicked Witch.
paragraphs.cn: “去我这里，把那些陌生人都赶走，除了狮子，”坏女巫说。

paragraphs.en: “Bring that beast to me, for I have a mind to harness him like a horse, and make him work.”
paragraphs.cn: “把那个怪兽带给我，我想把它像马一样套上绳子，让它干活。”

paragraphs.en: “Your commands shall be obeyed,” said the leader.
paragraphs.cn: “你的命令我们会照做，”猴子头儿说。

paragraphs.en: Then, with a great deal of chattering and noise, the Winged Monkeys flew away to the place where Dorothy and her friends were walking.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，飞猴吱吱喳喳地叫着，闹哄哄地飞走了，飞到了多萝西和她的朋友们正在走路的地方。

paragraphs.en: Some of the Monkeys seized the Tin Woodman and carried him through the air until they were over a country thickly covered with sharp rocks.
paragraphs.cn: 一些猴子抓住了 铁皮人，带着他飞到空中，一直飞到一片到处都是尖尖石头的地方。

paragraphs.en: Here they dropped the poor Woodman, who fell a great distance to the rocks, where he lay so battered and dented that he could neither move nor groan.
paragraphs.cn: 它们把可怜的 铁皮人 从高空扔了下去，他重重地摔在石头上，摔得扁扁的，动也动不了，哼都哼不出声。

paragraphs.en: Others of the Monkeys caught the Scarecrow, and with their long fingers pulled all of the straw out of his clothes and head.
paragraphs.cn: 另一些猴子抓住了 稻草人，用它们长长的手指把衣服和头里的稻草都拉了出来。

paragraphs.en: They made his hat and boots and clothes into a small bundle and threw it into the top branches of a tall tree.
paragraphs.cn: 它们把他的帽子、靴子和衣服捆成一小捆，扔到了一棵高高的大树顶上。

paragraphs.en: The remaining Monkeys threw pieces of stout rope around the Lion and wound many coils about his body and head and legs, until he was unable to bite or scratch or struggle in any way.
paragraphs.cn: 剩下的猴子用粗粗的绳子套住 狮子，把他的身子、头和腿都紧紧地缠起来，让他不能咬，不能抓，也不能挣扎了。

paragraphs.en: Then they lifted him up and flew away with him to the Witch’s castle, where he was placed in a small yard with a high iron fence around it, so that he could not escape.
paragraphs.cn: 然后它们抬起他，带着他飞到了女巫的城堡，把他关在一个有高高铁栏杆的小院子里，让他逃不掉。

paragraphs.en: But Dorothy they did not harm at all.
paragraphs.cn: 但是 多萝西 它们一点儿也没伤害。

paragraphs.en: She stood, with Toto in her arms, watching the sad fate of her comrades and thinking it would soon be her turn.
paragraphs.cn: 她抱着 托托 站在那里，看着她的朋友们遇到麻烦，想着很快就会轮到自己了。

paragraphs.en: The leader of the Winged Monkeys flew up to her, his long, hairy arms stretched out and his ugly face grinning terribly; but he saw the mark of the Good Witch’s kiss upon her forehead and stopped short, motioning the others not to touch her.
paragraphs.cn: 飞猴 的头儿飞到她身边，他伸出长长的、毛茸茸的胳膊，丑陋的脸上露出可怕的笑容；但他看到了 好女巫 亲吻在她额头上的印记，立刻停了下来，示意别的猴子不要碰她。

paragraphs.en: “We dare not harm this little girl,” he said to them, “for she is protected by the Power of Good, and that is greater than the Power of Evil.
paragraphs.cn: “我们不敢伤害这个小女孩，”他对它们说，“因为有善良的力量保护她，那比邪恶的力量更强大。

paragraphs.en: All we can do is to carry her to the castle of the Wicked Witch and leave her there.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们能做的只有把她带到 坏女巫 的城堡，把她留在那里。”

paragraphs.en: So, carefully and gently, they lifted Dorothy in their arms and carried her swiftly through the air until they came to the castle, where they set her down upon the front doorstep.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，它们小心翼翼地抱起 多萝西，带着她飞快地穿过空中，一直飞到城堡，把她放在大门口的台阶上。

paragraphs.en: Then the leader said to the Witch:
paragraphs.cn: 然后头儿对女巫说：

paragraphs.en: “We have obeyed you as far as we were able.
paragraphs.cn: “我们已经尽力听你的话了。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow are destroyed, and the Lion is tied up in your yard.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 和 稻草人 被毁了，狮子 也被绑在你的院子里了。

paragraphs.en: The little girl we dare not harm, nor the dog she carries in her arms.
paragraphs.cn: 那个小女孩我们不敢伤害，她怀里的狗狗我们也不敢伤害。

paragraphs.en: Your power over our band is now ended, and you will never see us again.”
paragraphs.cn: 你对我们这群猴子的控制结束了，你再也见不到我们了。”

paragraphs.en: Then all the Winged Monkeys, with much laughing and chattering and noise, flew into the air and were soon out of sight.
paragraphs.cn: 然后所有的 飞猴 大声笑着、说着、吵着，飞到空中，很快就不见了。

paragraphs.en: The Wicked Witch was both surprised and worried when she saw the mark on Dorothy’s forehead, for she knew well that neither the Winged Monkeys nor she, herself, dare hurt the girl in any way.
paragraphs.cn: 当 坏女巫 看到 多萝西 额头上的印记时，既惊讶又担心，因为她很清楚，无论是 飞猴 还是她自己，都不敢伤害这个小女孩。

paragraphs.en: She looked down at Dorothy’s feet, and seeing the Silver Shoes, began to tremble with fear, for she knew what a powerful charm belonged to them.
paragraphs.cn: 她低头看着 多萝西 的脚，看到 银鞋 后，吓得发抖，因为她知道 银鞋 有多么强大的魔法。

paragraphs.en: At first the Witch was tempted to run away from Dorothy; but she happened to look into the child’s eyes and saw how simple the soul behind them was, and that the little girl did not know of the wonderful power the Silver Shoes gave her.
paragraphs.cn: 女巫一开始差点儿就想从 多萝西 身边跑掉；但她碰巧看到了小女孩的眼睛，发现她的心灵多么纯真，而且小女孩根本不知道 银鞋 给了她多么神奇的力量。

paragraphs.en: So the Wicked Witch laughed to herself, and thought, “I can still make her my slave, for she does not know how to use her power.”
paragraphs.cn: 于是 坏女巫 偷偷地笑了，心想：“我还是可以把她变成我的仆人，因为她不知道怎么使用她的力量。”

paragraphs.en: Then she said to Dorothy, harshly and severely:
paragraphs.cn: 然后她凶巴巴地，很严厉地对 多萝西 说：

paragraphs.en: “Come with me; and see that you mind everything I tell you, for if you do not I will make an end of you, as I did of the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow.”
paragraphs.cn: “跟我来；记住，要听我的话，如果不听，我就会像对付 铁皮人 和 稻草人 那样，把你消灭掉。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle until they came to the kitchen, where the Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 跟着她穿过城堡里许多漂亮的房间，一直到了厨房，女巫让她擦锅碗瓢盆，扫地，还要给炉子添柴火。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy went to work meekly, with her mind made up to work as hard as she could; for she was glad the Wicked Witch had decided not to kill her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 顺从地开始干活，她决定要努力干活；因为她很高兴 坏女巫 决定不杀她。

paragraphs.en: With Dorothy hard at work, the Witch thought she would go into the courtyard and harness the Cowardly Lion like a horse; it would amuse her, she was sure, to make him draw her chariot whenever she wished to go to drive.
paragraphs.cn: 看到 多萝西 在努力干活，女巫心想她要去院子里，把 胆小的狮子 像马一样套起来；她相信，每次她想出去的时候，就让 胆小的狮子 给她拉马车，这会让她觉得好玩。

paragraphs.en: But as she opened the gate the Lion gave a loud roar and bounded at her so fiercely that the Witch was afraid, and ran out and shut the gate again.
paragraphs.cn: 但当她打开门的时候，狮子 大吼一声，凶猛地扑向她，女巫吓坏了，跑出去，又把门关上了。

paragraphs.en: “If I cannot harness you,” said the Witch to the Lion, speaking through the bars of the gate, “I can starve you.
paragraphs.cn: “如果我不能把你套起来，”女巫隔着门上的栏杆对 狮子 说，“我就可以把你饿死。

paragraphs.en: You shall have nothing to eat until you do as I wish.”
paragraphs.cn: 在你听我的话之前，什么也别想吃。”

paragraphs.en: So after that she took no food to the imprisoned Lion; but every day she came to the gate at noon and asked, “Are you ready to be harnessed like a horse?”
paragraphs.cn: 从那以后，她就不再给关着的狮子送吃的了；但是每天中午，她都会来到门口问：“你准备好像马一样被套上绳子了吗？”

paragraphs.en: And the Lion would answer, “No. If you come in this yard, I will bite you.”
paragraphs.cn: 而狮子会回答说：“不。如果你进这个院子，我就咬你。”

paragraphs.en: The reason the Lion did not have to do as the Witch wished was that every night, while the woman was asleep, Dorothy carried him food from the cupboard.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子不用按女巫希望的去做，是因为每天晚上，当女巫睡着的时候，多萝西会从柜子里给他拿吃的。

paragraphs.en: After he had eaten he would lie down on his bed of straw, and Dorothy would lie beside him and put her head on his soft, shaggy mane, while they talked of their troubles and tried to plan some way to escape.
paragraphs.cn: 他吃完后，就会躺在草床上，多萝西会躺在他身边，把头放在他柔软蓬松的鬃毛上，他们一边说着自己的烦恼，一边想办法逃跑。

paragraphs.en: But they could find no way to get out of the castle, for it was constantly guarded by the yellow Winkies, who were the slaves of the Wicked Witch and too afraid of her not to do as she told them.
paragraphs.cn: 但是他们找不到办法逃出城堡，因为城堡一直被黄色的温基人守着，它们是坏女巫的奴隶，太害怕她了，所以不敢不听她的话。

paragraphs.en: The girl had to work hard during the day, and often the Witch threatened to beat her with the same old umbrella she always carried in her hand.
paragraphs.cn: 白天，小女孩要努力干活，女巫经常威胁要用她手里那把旧伞打她。

paragraphs.en: But, in truth, she did not dare to strike Dorothy, because of the mark upon her forehead.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，其实她不敢打多萝西，因为她额头上的印记。

paragraphs.en: The child did not know this, and was full of fear for herself and Toto.
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩不知道这件事，她很害怕自己和托托。

paragraphs.en: Once the Witch struck Toto a blow with her umbrella and the brave little dog flew at her and bit her leg in return.
paragraphs.cn: 有一次女巫用伞打了托托一下，勇敢的小狗就扑过去咬了她的腿。

paragraphs.en: The Witch did not bleed where she was bitten, for she was so wicked that the blood in her had dried up many years before.
paragraphs.cn: 女巫被咬的地方没有流血，因为她太坏了，她身体里的血很多年前就干了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy’s life became very sad as she grew to understand that it would be harder than ever to get back to Kansas and Aunt Em again.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西的生活变得很伤心，因为她渐渐明白，再想回到堪萨斯和艾姆婶婶身边会比以前更难了。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes she would cry bitterly for hours, with Toto sitting at her feet and looking into her face, whining dismally to show how sorry he was for his little mistress.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候她会伤心地哭好几个小时，托托会坐在她脚边，看着她的脸，悲伤地呜咽着，表示它很心疼小主人。

paragraphs.en: Toto did not really care whether he was in Kansas or the Land of Oz so long as Dorothy was with him; but he knew the little girl was unhappy, and that made him unhappy too.
paragraphs.cn: 托托其实不在乎自己是在堪萨斯还是在奥兹国，只要多萝西在他身边就好；但是他知道小女孩不开心，这也让他不开心。

paragraphs.en: Now the Wicked Witch had a great longing to have for her own the Silver Shoes which the girl always wore.
paragraphs.cn: 现在坏女巫非常想要把小女孩一直穿在身上的银鞋占为己有。

paragraphs.en: Her bees and her crows and her wolves were lying in heaps and drying up, and she had used up all the power of the Golden Cap; but if she could only get hold of the Silver Shoes, they would give her more power than all the other things she had lost.
paragraphs.cn: 她的蜜蜂、乌鸦和狼都堆成一堆，枯萎了，她也用光了金冠所有的魔力；但是如果她能得到银鞋，它们会给她比她失去的所有东西加起来还要多的力量。

paragraphs.en: She watched Dorothy carefully, to see if she ever took off her shoes, thinking she might steal them.
paragraphs.cn: 她仔细地盯着多萝西，想看看她有没有脱下鞋子，觉得她可以偷走它们。

paragraphs.en: But the child was so proud of her pretty shoes that she never took them off except at night and when she took her bath.
paragraphs.cn: 但是小女孩很喜欢她的漂亮鞋子，所以除了晚上和洗澡的时候，她从不脱下它们。

paragraphs.en: The Witch was too much afraid of the dark to dare go in Dorothy’s room at night to take the shoes, and her dread of water was greater than her fear of the dark, so she never came near when Dorothy was bathing.
paragraphs.cn: 女巫太害怕黑暗了，不敢晚上去多萝西的房间拿鞋子，她对水的恐惧比对黑暗的恐惧更大，所以当多萝西洗澡的时候，她从不靠近。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, the old Witch never touched water, nor ever let water touch her in any way.
paragraphs.cn: 确实，这个老女巫从不碰水，也从不让水碰到她。

paragraphs.en: But the wicked creature was very cunning, and she finally thought of a trick that would give her what she wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 但是这个坏家伙很狡猾，她终于想到了一个能让她得到想要东西的办法。

paragraphs.en: She placed a bar of iron in the middle of the kitchen floor, and then by her magic arts made the iron invisible to human eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 她在厨房地板中间放了一根铁棍，然后用魔法让铁棍在人的眼睛里看不见。

paragraphs.en: So that when Dorothy walked across the floor she stumbled over the bar, not being able to see it, and fell at full length.
paragraphs.cn: 这样当多萝西走过地板时，她会绊倒在铁棍上，因为她看不见它，然后就摔了个大跟头。

paragraphs.en: She was not much hurt, but in her fall one of the Silver Shoes came off; and before she could reach it, the Witch had snatched it away and put it on her own skinny foot.
paragraphs.cn: 她没有受太大的伤，但是她摔倒的时候，一只银鞋掉了下来；还没等她捡起来，女巫就一把抢走了，穿在了自己瘦瘦的脚上。

paragraphs.en: The wicked woman was greatly pleased with the success of her trick, for as long as she had one of the shoes she owned half the power of their charm, and Dorothy could not use it against her, even had she known how to do so.
paragraphs.cn: 这个坏女人对自己的计谋成功非常高兴，因为只要她有一只鞋子，她就拥有它们一半的魔力，而且多萝西也无法用它来对抗她，即使她知道怎么做。

paragraphs.en: The little girl, seeing she had lost one of her pretty shoes, grew angry, and said to the Witch, “Give me back my shoe!”
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩看到自己丢了一只漂亮的鞋子，就生气了，对女巫说：“把我的鞋子还给我！”

paragraphs.en: “I will not,” retorted the Witch, “for it is now my shoe, and not yours.”
paragraphs.cn: “我才不！”女巫反驳道，“因为这现在是我的鞋子，不是你的。”

paragraphs.en: “You are a wicked creature!” cried Dorothy. “You have no right to take my shoe from me.”
paragraphs.cn: “你这个坏家伙！”多萝西叫道，“你没权利拿走我的鞋子！”

paragraphs.en: “I shall keep it, just the same,” said the Witch, laughing at her, “and someday I shall get the other one from you, too.”
paragraphs.cn: “我还是要留着它，”女巫嘲笑着她说道，“总有一天，我还会从你那里拿到另一只的。”

paragraphs.en: This made Dorothy so very angry that she picked up the bucket of water that stood near and dashed it over the Witch, wetting her from head to foot.
paragraphs.cn: 这让多萝西非常生气，以至于她拿起旁边的一桶水，朝女巫泼过去，把她从头到脚都弄湿了。

paragraphs.en: Instantly the wicked woman gave a loud cry of fear, and then, as Dorothy looked at her in wonder, the Witch began to shrink and fall away.
paragraphs.cn: 坏女人立刻发出一声害怕的大叫，然后，当多萝西好奇地看着她的时候，女巫开始缩小并消失了。

paragraphs.en: “See what you have done!” she screamed. “In a minute I shall melt away.”
paragraphs.cn: “看你做了什么！”她大叫。“我很快就要融化了。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m very sorry, indeed,” said Dorothy, who was truly frightened to see the Witch actually melting away like brown sugar before her very eyes.
paragraphs.cn: “我真的对不起，”多萝西说，她吓坏了，因为女巫真的像糖一样在她眼前融化了。

paragraphs.en: “Didn’t you know water would be the end of me?” asked the Witch, in a wailing, despairing voice.
paragraphs.cn: “你不知道水会让我消失吗？”女巫哭着、绝望地问。

paragraphs.en: “Of course not,” answered Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “当然不知道啊。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “How should I?”
paragraphs.cn: “我怎么会知道呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, in a few minutes I shall be all melted, and you will have the castle to yourself.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，过几分钟我就完全融化了，城堡就是你的啦。

paragraphs.en: I have been wicked in my day, but I never thought a little girl like you would ever be able to melt me and end my wicked deeds.
paragraphs.cn: 我以前很坏，但我从没想过，像你这样的小女孩能把我融化，让我不能再做坏事了。

paragraphs.en: Look out—here I go!”
paragraphs.cn: 小心啦——我要消失啦！”

paragraphs.en: With these words the Witch fell down in a brown, melted, shapeless mass and began to spread over the clean boards of the kitchen floor.
paragraphs.cn: 女巫说完，就变成一滩棕色、融化的东西，铺满了厨房干净的地板。

paragraphs.en: Seeing that she had really melted away to nothing, Dorothy drew another bucket of water and threw it over the mess.
paragraphs.cn: 看到女巫真的完全融化不见了，多萝西又提了一桶水，泼在那些融化了的东西上。

paragraphs.en: She then swept it all out the door.
paragraphs.cn: 她把它们全都扫出门外。

paragraphs.en: After picking out the silver shoe, which was all that was left of the old woman, she cleaned and dried it with a cloth, and put it on her foot again.
paragraphs.cn: 她捡起那只银鞋，那是老巫婆身上唯一剩下的。她用布擦干净，擦干，又穿回了脚上。

paragraphs.en: Then, being at last free to do as she chose, she ran out to the courtyard to tell the Lion that the Wicked Witch of the West had come to an end, and that they were no longer prisoners in a strange land.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，她终于可以做自己想做的事了。她跑到院子里，告诉狮子，西方坏女巫已经消失了，他们再也不是这陌生地方的囚犯了。

paragraphs.en: The Cowardly Lion was much pleased to hear that the Wicked Witch had been melted by a bucket of water, and Dorothy at once unlocked the gate of his prison and set him free.
paragraphs.cn: 胆小的狮子听说坏女巫被一桶水融化了，非常开心。多萝西立刻打开了牢房的门，放他出来了。

paragraphs.en: They went in together to the castle, where Dorothy’s first act was to call all the Winkies together and tell them that they were no longer slaves.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一起走进城堡。多萝西做的第一件事，就是把所有温基人叫到一起，告诉他们，他们再也不是奴隶了。

paragraphs.en: There was great rejoicing among the yellow Winkies, for they had been made to work hard during many years for the Wicked Witch, who had always treated them with great cruelty.
paragraphs.cn: 黄色的温基人们都非常高兴，因为他们被坏女巫逼着辛苦工作了很多年。坏女巫总是对他们很坏。

paragraphs.en: They kept this day as a holiday, then and ever after, and spent the time in feasting and dancing.
paragraphs.cn: 从那天起，他们就把这一天当作节日，一直庆祝下去，唱歌跳舞，开心地吃喝玩乐。

paragraphs.en: “If our friends, the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, were only with us,” said the Lion, “I should be quite happy.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果我们的朋友，稻草人和铁皮人也能跟我们在一起，”狮子说，“我就会很开心了。”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t you suppose we could rescue them?” asked the girl anxiously.
paragraphs.cn: “我们不能去救他们吗？”女孩着急地问。

paragraphs.en: “We can try,” answered the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “我们可以试试看。”狮子回答。

paragraphs.en: So they called the yellow Winkies and asked them if they would help to rescue their friends, and the Winkies said that they would be delighted to do all in their power for Dorothy, who had set them free from bondage.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们叫来黄色的温基人，问他们愿不愿意帮忙救朋友。温基人说，他们很乐意为多萝西做任何事，因为多萝西把他们从苦日子里救了出来。

paragraphs.en: So she chose a number of the Winkies who looked as if they knew the most, and they all started away.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她选了一些看起来最聪明的温基人，他们就出发了。

paragraphs.en: They traveled that day and part of the next until they came to the rocky plain where the Tin Woodman lay, all battered and bent.
paragraphs.cn: 他们那天走了很久，第二天也走了一段路，终于来到了那片都是石头的平原。铁皮人就躺在那里，破破烂烂的，都弯了。

paragraphs.en: His axe was near him, but the blade was rusted and the handle broken off short.
paragraphs.cn: 他的斧头就在旁边，可是斧刃生锈了，斧柄也断成了两截。

paragraphs.en: The Winkies lifted him tenderly in their arms, and carried him back to the Yellow Castle again, Dorothy shedding a few tears by the way at the sad plight of her old friend, and the Lion looking sober and sorry.
paragraphs.cn: 温基人们轻轻地把他抱起来，又把他带回了黄色的城堡。一路上，多萝西看到老朋友这么可怜，流了几滴眼泪。狮子看着也很严肃，很难过。

paragraphs.en: When they reached the castle Dorothy said to the Winkies:
paragraphs.cn: 他们到了城堡后，多萝西对温基人说：

paragraphs.en: “Are any of your people tinsmiths?”
paragraphs.cn: “你们中间有人会修理锡器吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，有啊。

paragraphs.en: Some of us are very good tinsmiths,” they told her.
paragraphs.cn: 我们中间有些人很会修锡器呢！”他们告诉她。

paragraphs.en: “Then bring them to me,” she said.
paragraphs.cn: “那就把他们带来给我吧。”她说。

paragraphs.en: And when the tinsmiths came, bringing with them all their tools in baskets, she inquired, “Can you straighten out those dents in the Tin Woodman, and bend him back into shape again, and solder him together where he is broken?”
paragraphs.cn: 铁匠们提着工具筐来了。她问：“你们能把铁皮人身上的坑弄平，让他变回原来的样子，再把断掉的地方焊起来吗？”

paragraphs.en: The tinsmiths looked the Woodman over carefully and then answered that they thought they could mend him so he would be as good as ever.
paragraphs.cn: 铁匠们仔细看了看铁皮人，然后说他们能把他修好，让他和以前一样。

paragraphs.en: So they set to work in one of the big yellow rooms of the castle and worked for three days and four nights, hammering and twisting and bending and soldering and polishing and pounding at the legs and body and head of the Tin Woodman, until at last he was straightened out into his old form, and his joints worked as well as ever.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们在城堡里一间大大的黄房间里干活，忙了三天四夜。他们又是敲又是打，又是焊又是磨，在铁皮人的腿、身体和头上忙活，直到他变回了原来的样子，关节也和以前一样灵活了。

paragraphs.en: To be sure, there were several patches on him, but the tinsmiths did a good job, and as the Woodman was not a vain man he did not mind the patches at all.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，他身上多了几块补丁，但铁匠们手艺很好。而且铁皮人一点也不臭美，所以他一点也不介意这些补丁。

paragraphs.en: When, at last, he walked into Dorothy’s room and thanked her for rescuing him, he was so pleased that he wept tears of joy, and Dorothy had to wipe every tear carefully from his face with her apron, so his joints would not be rusted.
paragraphs.cn: 他终于走进多萝西的房间，感谢她救了他。他高兴得流下了眼泪，多萝西赶紧用围裙擦掉他脸上的每一滴泪水，免得他的关节生锈。

paragraphs.en: At the same time her own tears fell thick and fast at the joy of meeting her old friend again, and these tears did not need to be wiped away.
paragraphs.cn: 同时，她也因为又见到老朋友而高兴得哗哗地流下了眼泪，这些眼泪倒不用擦掉。

paragraphs.en: As for the Lion, he wiped his eyes so often with the tip of his tail that it became quite wet, and he was obliged to go out into the courtyard and hold it in the sun till it dried.
paragraphs.cn: 而狮子呢，他用尾巴尖擦眼睛擦得太频繁了，结果尾巴尖都湿透了。他只好跑到院子里，把尾巴放在太阳下晒干。

paragraphs.en: “If we only had the Scarecrow with us again,” said the Tin Woodman, when Dorothy had finished telling him everything that had happened, “I should be quite happy.”
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西讲完所有事情后，铁皮人说：“要是稻草人也能跟我们在一起就好了，那我就会非常开心了。”

paragraphs.en: “We must try to find him,” said the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “我们得把他找回来，”女孩说。

paragraphs.en: So she called the Winkies to help her, and they walked all that day and part of the next until they came to the tall tree in the branches of which the Winged Monkeys had tossed the Scarecrow’s clothes.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她叫上温基人帮忙，他们走了一天一夜，直到来到那棵大树前。飞猴曾把稻草人的衣服扔在那棵树上。

paragraphs.en: It was a very tall tree, and the trunk was so smooth that no one could climb it; but the Woodman said at once, “I’ll chop it down, and then we can get the Scarecrow’s clothes.”
paragraphs.cn: 那是一棵很高很高的树，树干太光滑了，没有人能爬上去。但铁皮人马上说：“我把它砍倒，这样我们就能拿到稻草人的衣服了。”

paragraphs.en: Now while the tinsmiths had been at work mending the Woodman himself, another of the Winkies, who was a goldsmith, had made an axe-handle of solid gold and fitted it to the Woodman’s axe, instead of the old broken handle.
paragraphs.cn: 就在铁匠们修理铁皮人的时候，另一个温基人（他是个金匠）用纯金给铁皮人做了一个新斧柄，替换掉了旧的坏掉的斧柄。

paragraphs.en: Others polished the blade until all the rust was removed and it glistened like burnished silver.
paragraphs.cn: 还有的人把斧刃磨得亮亮的，直到一点锈都没有了，闪着银色的光。

paragraphs.en: As soon as he had spoken, the Tin Woodman began to chop, and in a short time the tree fell over with a crash, whereupon the Scarecrow’s clothes fell out of the branches and rolled off on the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 他刚说完，铁皮人就开始砍树了。没多久，大树就轰隆一声倒了下来，稻草人的衣服也从树枝上掉了下来，滚到地上。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy picked them up and had the Winkies carry them back to the castle, where they were stuffed with nice, clean straw; and behold! here was the Scarecrow, as good as ever, thanking them over and over again for saving him.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西把衣服捡起来，让温基人背回城堡。在那里，人们把衣服里塞满了干净的稻草。瞧！稻草人又变回了原来的样子，不停地感谢他们救了他。

paragraphs.en: Now that they were reunited, Dorothy and her friends spent a few happy days at the Yellow Castle, where they found everything they needed to make them comfortable.
paragraphs.cn: 大家又聚到一起了，多萝西和她的朋友们在黄城堡里度过了几天开心的日子。在那里，他们想要什么就有什么，过得很舒服。

paragraphs.en: But one day the girl thought of Aunt Em, and said, “We must go back to Oz, and claim his promise.”
paragraphs.cn: 但有一天，女孩想起了艾姆婶婶，说：“我们得回到奥兹大王那里，让他兑现承诺了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” said the Woodman, “at last I shall get my heart.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，”铁皮人说，“我终于能拿到我的心了。”

paragraphs.en: “And I shall get my brains,” added the Scarecrow joyfully.
paragraphs.cn: “我也会拿到我的大脑了！”稻草人高兴地补充道。

paragraphs.en: “And I shall get my courage,” said the Lion thoughtfully.
paragraphs.cn: “我也会拿到我的勇气了。”狮子认真地说。

paragraphs.en: “And I shall get back to Kansas,” cried Dorothy, clapping her hands.
paragraphs.cn: “我也可以回到堪萨斯那里了！”多萝西拍着手叫道。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, let us start for the Emerald City tomorrow!”
paragraphs.cn: “啊，我们明天就去翡翠城吧！”

paragraphs.en: This they decided to do.
paragraphs.cn: 他们决定就这样做。

paragraphs.en: The next day they called the Winkies together and bade them good-bye.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天，他们把温基人叫到一起，跟他们告别。

paragraphs.en: The Winkies were sorry to have them go, and they had grown so fond of the Tin Woodman that they begged him to stay and rule over them and the Yellow Land of the West.
paragraphs.cn: 温基人舍不得他们走，他们太喜欢铁皮人了，求他留下，管理他们和黄色的西方土地。

paragraphs.en: Finding they were determined to go, the Winkies gave Toto and the Lion each a golden collar; and to Dorothy they presented a beautiful bracelet studded with diamonds; and to the Scarecrow they gave a gold-headed walking stick, to keep him from stumbling; and to the Tin Woodman they offered a silver oil-can, inlaid with gold and set with precious jewels.
paragraphs.cn: 看到他们非走不可，温基人送给托托和狮子每人一个金项圈；送给多萝西一个镶满钻石的手镯；送给稻草人一根金头拐杖，这样他走路就不会摔倒了；送给铁皮人一个银油壶，上面镶着金子和漂亮的宝石。

paragraphs.en: Every one of the travelers made the Winkies a pretty speech in return, and all shook hands with them until their arms ached.
paragraphs.cn: 旅行者们都对温基人说了感谢的话，大家跟他们一一握手，直到胳膊都酸了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy went to the Witch’s cupboard to fill her basket with food for the journey, and there she saw the Golden Cap.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西去女巫的柜子里，给自己的篮子装上路上吃的食物，她在那里看到了金冠。

paragraphs.en: She tried it on her own head and found that it fitted her exactly.
paragraphs.cn: 她把它戴在自己头上，发现刚刚好。

paragraphs.en: She did not know anything about the charm of the Golden Cap, but she saw that it was pretty, so she made up her mind to wear it and carry her sunbonnet in the basket.
paragraphs.cn: 她不知道金冠有什么魔力，但她觉得它很漂亮，于是她决定戴上它，把自己的遮阳帽放在篮子里。

paragraphs.en: Then, being prepared for the journey, they all started for the Emerald City; and the Winkies gave them three cheers and many good wishes to carry with them.
paragraphs.cn: 准备好后，他们就出发去翡翠城了。温基人给他们欢呼，祝他们一路顺风。

paragraphs.en: You will remember there was no road—not even a pathway—between the castle of the Wicked Witch and the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 你还记得吗？从坏女巫的城堡到翡翠城，根本没有路，连小道都没有。

paragraphs.en: When the four travelers went in search of the Witch she had seen them coming, and so sent the Winged Monkeys to bring them to her.
paragraphs.cn: 四个旅行者去找巫婆时，巫婆看到了他们。于是她派飞猴把他们带到她那儿。

paragraphs.en: It was much harder to find their way back through the big fields of buttercups and yellow daisies than it was being carried.
paragraphs.cn: 穿过一大片毛茛花和黄色雏菊地，要自己找路回去，比被带着走难多了。

paragraphs.en: They knew, of course, they must go straight east, toward the rising sun; and they started off in the right way.
paragraphs.cn: 他们知道，他们必须一直往东走，朝着太阳升起的方向。他们一开始走得很对。

paragraphs.en: But at noon, when the sun was over their heads, they did not know which was east and which was west, and that was the reason they were lost in the great fields.
paragraphs.cn: 但到了中午，太阳在他们头顶时，他们就分不清哪里是东哪里是西了。所以他们迷失在了大片田地里。

paragraphs.en: They kept on walking, however, and at night the moon came out and shone brightly.
paragraphs.cn: 不过他们继续往前走。到了晚上，月亮出来了，亮亮地照着。

paragraphs.en: So they lay down among the sweet smelling yellow flowers and slept soundly until morning—all but the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们躺在香香的黄花中间，睡得很香，直到天亮——除了稻草人和铁皮人。

paragraphs.en: The next morning the sun was behind a cloud, but they started on, as if they were quite sure which way they were going.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，太阳躲在云后面，但他们还是出发了，好像他们很确定要走哪条路一样。

paragraphs.en: “If we walk far enough,” said Dorothy, “I am sure we shall sometime come to some place.”
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西说：“如果我们走得够远，我肯定我们总会走到某个地方的。”

paragraphs.en: But day by day passed away, and they still saw nothing before them but the scarlet fields.
paragraphs.cn: 但一天天过去了，他们眼前除了那红色的田野，什么也没看到。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow began to grumble a bit.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人开始有点抱怨了。

paragraphs.en: “We have surely lost our way,” he said, “and unless we find it again in time to reach the Emerald City, I shall never get my brains.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“我们肯定迷路了。如果我们不能及时找到路去翡翠城，我就永远得不到我的智慧了。”

paragraphs.en: “Nor I my heart,” declared the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人说：“我也得不到我的心了。”

paragraphs.en: “It seems to me I can scarcely wait till I get to Oz, and you must admit this is a very long journey.”
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得我等不及要去奥兹大王了。你们也得承认，这路程太长了。”

paragraphs.en: “You see,” said the Cowardly Lion, with a whimper, “I haven’t the courage to keep tramping forever, without getting anywhere at all.”
paragraphs.cn: 胆小的狮子带着哭腔说：“你看，我可没有勇气一直走下去，什么地方也到不了。”

paragraphs.en: Then Dorothy lost heart.
paragraphs.cn: 然后多萝西泄气了。

paragraphs.en: She sat down on the grass and looked at her companions, and they sat down and looked at her, and Toto found that for the first time in his life he was too tired to chase a butterfly that flew past his head.
paragraphs.cn: 她坐在草地上，看着她的同伴们。他们也坐下来看着她。托托发现，他生平第一次累得追不上从头顶飞过的蝴蝶了。

paragraphs.en: So he put out his tongue and panted and looked at Dorothy as if to ask what they should do next.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他伸出舌头，喘着气，看着多萝西，好像在问他们接下来该怎么办。

paragraphs.en: “Suppose we call the field mice,” she suggested.
paragraphs.cn: 她建议：“不如我们叫田鼠来吧。”

paragraphs.en: “They could probably tell us the way to the Emerald City.”
paragraphs.cn: “它们也许能告诉我们去翡翠城的路。”

paragraphs.en: “To be sure they could,” cried the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人大喊：“它们当然可以！”

paragraphs.en: “Why didn’t we think of that before?”
paragraphs.cn: “我们怎么早没想到呢？”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy blew the little whistle she had always carried about her neck since the Queen of the Mice had given it to her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西吹响了她一直挂在脖子上的小哨子，那是鼠后送给她的。

paragraphs.en: In a few minutes they heard the pattering of tiny feet, and many of the small gray mice came running up to her.
paragraphs.cn: 几分钟后，他们听到小脚跑动的声音，许多灰色的小老鼠跑了过来。

paragraphs.en: Among them was the Queen herself, who asked, in her squeaky little voice:
paragraphs.cn: 鼠后也在其中。她用尖尖的小声音问道：

paragraphs.en: “What can I do for my friends?”
paragraphs.cn: “我能为我的朋友们做些什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “We have lost our way,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西说：“我们迷路了。”

paragraphs.en: “Can you tell us where the Emerald City is?”
paragraphs.cn: “你能告诉我们翡翠城在哪里吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Certainly,” answered the Queen; “but it is a great way off, for you have had it at your backs all this time.”
paragraphs.cn: 鼠后回答：“当然可以。但它很远呢，因为这段时间它一直都在你们身后。”

paragraphs.en: Then she noticed Dorothy’s Golden Cap, and said, “Why don’t you use the charm of the Cap, and call the Winged Monkeys to you?
paragraphs.cn: 然后她看到 多萝西 的 金冠，说：“你为什么不用帽子的魔力，把 飞猴 叫过来呢？

paragraphs.en: They will carry you to the City of Oz in less than an hour.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们不到一小时就会把你送到 奥兹国。”

paragraphs.en: “I didn’t know there was a charm,” answered Dorothy, in surprise.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道有这种魔力啊，”多萝西 惊讶地回答说。

paragraphs.en: “What is it?”
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “It is written inside the Golden Cap,” replied the Queen of the Mice.
paragraphs.cn: “它写在 金冠 里面，”老鼠女王回答说。

paragraphs.en: “But if you are going to call the Winged Monkeys we must run away, for they are full of mischief and think it great fun to plague us.”
paragraphs.cn: “但是如果你要叫 飞猴 来的话，我们就得跑开，因为它们很淘气，觉得捉弄我们很好玩。”

paragraphs.en: “Won’t they hurt me?” asked the girl anxiously.
paragraphs.cn: “它们不会伤害我吧？”小女孩担心地问。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不会的。

paragraphs.en: They must obey the wearer of the Cap.
paragraphs.cn: 它们必须听戴帽子的人的话。

paragraphs.en: Good-bye!”
paragraphs.cn: 再见！”

paragraphs.en: And she scampered out of sight, with all the mice hurrying after her.
paragraphs.cn: 她一溜烟跑得不见了，所有的老鼠都跟着她跑开了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy looked inside the Golden Cap and saw some words written upon the lining.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 看了看 金冠 里面，看到衬里上写着一些字。

paragraphs.en: These, she thought, must be the charm, so she read the directions carefully and put the Cap upon her head.
paragraphs.cn: 她想，这些一定是魔力，所以她仔细地读了说明，然后把帽子戴在头上。

paragraphs.en: “Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke!” she said, standing on her left foot.
paragraphs.cn: 她单脚站在左脚上，说：“艾普-佩，佩普-佩，卡克-克！”

paragraphs.en: “What did you say?” asked the Scarecrow, who did not know what she was doing.
paragraphs.cn: “你说了什么？”稻草人 问，它不知道她在做什么。

paragraphs.en: “Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo!”
paragraphs.cn: “希尔-洛，霍尔-洛，赫尔-洛！”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy went on, standing this time on her right foot.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 继续说，这次她单脚站在右脚上。

paragraphs.en: “Hello!” replied the Tin Woodman calmly.
paragraphs.cn: “你好！”铁皮人 平静地回答说。

paragraphs.en: “Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik!” said Dorothy, who was now standing on both feet.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 这次两只脚都站着，说：“兹兹-西，祖祖-西，西克！”

paragraphs.en: This ended the saying of the charm, and they heard a great chattering and flapping of wings, as the band of Winged Monkeys flew up to them.
paragraphs.cn: 这样魔咒就念完了，他们听到一阵很大的叫声和翅膀拍打声，一群 飞猴 朝他们飞了过来。

paragraphs.en: The King bowed low before Dorothy, and asked, “What is your command?”
paragraphs.cn: 国王在 多萝西 面前深深地鞠了一躬，问：“有什么吩咐吗？”

paragraphs.en: “We wish to go to the Emerald City,” said the child, “and we have lost our way.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们想去 翡翠城，”孩子说，“我们迷路了。”

paragraphs.en: “We will carry you,” replied the King, and no sooner had he spoken than two of the Monkeys caught Dorothy in their arms and flew away with her.
paragraphs.cn: “我们会带你们去的，”国王回答说，他刚说完，两只猴子就抱起 多萝西 飞走了。

paragraphs.en: Others took the Scarecrow and the Woodman and the Lion, and one little Monkey seized Toto and flew after them, although the dog tried hard to bite him.
paragraphs.cn: 其他的猴子带着 稻草人、铁皮人 和 狮子，一只小猴子抓起 托托 追了上去，尽管狗狗努力想咬它。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were rather frightened at first, for they remembered how badly the Winged Monkeys had treated them before; but they saw that no harm was intended, so they rode through the air quite cheerfully, and had a fine time looking at the pretty gardens and woods far below them.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 和 铁皮人 一开始有点害怕，因为它们记得 飞猴 以前对它们很不好；但它们看到 飞猴 没有恶意，于是它们开心地在空中飞，欣赏着下面美丽的园林和森林。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy found herself riding easily between two of the biggest Monkeys, one of them the King himself.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 发现自己很舒服地坐在两只最大的猴子中间，其中一只就是国王。

paragraphs.en: They had made a chair of their hands and were careful not to hurt her.
paragraphs.cn: 它们用手搭成了一把椅子，而且很小心，没有弄伤她。

paragraphs.en: “Why do you have to obey the charm of the Golden Cap?” she asked.
paragraphs.cn: “你们为什么要听 金冠 的魔力呢？”她问。

paragraphs.en: “That is a long story,” answered the King, with a winged laugh; “but as we have a long journey before us, I will pass the time by telling you about it, if you wish.”
paragraphs.cn: “那是个很长的故事，”国王笑着回答说；“不过我们还有很长的路要走，如果你愿意，我就讲给你听，打发时间。”

paragraphs.en: “I shall be glad to hear it,” she replied.
paragraphs.cn: “我很乐意听，”她回答。

paragraphs.en: “Once,” began the leader, “we were a free people, living happily in the great forest, flying from tree to tree, eating nuts and fruit, and doing just as we pleased without calling anybody master.
paragraphs.cn: “很久很久以前，”领头的那只猴子说，“我们是一群自由的猴子，开心地住在森林里。我们在树上飞来飞去，吃坚果和水果，想做什么就做什么，没有主人管我们。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps some of us were rather too full of mischief at times, flying down to pull the tails of the animals that had no wings, chasing birds, and throwing nuts at the people who walked in the forest.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候，我们很调皮。我们会飞下去，拉那些没有翅膀的小动物的尾巴，追赶小鸟，还会朝在森林里走路的人扔坚果。

paragraphs.en: But we were careless and happy and full of fun, and enjoyed every minute of the day.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，我们那时无忧无虑，非常开心，每天都玩得很尽兴。

paragraphs.en: This was many years ago, long before Oz came out of the clouds to rule over this land.
paragraphs.cn: 这是很多年前的事了，比奥兹大王从云朵里出来统治这片土地还要早很多。

paragraphs.en: “There lived here then, away at the North, a beautiful princess, who was also a powerful sorceress.
paragraphs.cn: “当时，在这片土地的北方，住着一位美丽的公主。她也是一位很厉害的女巫。

paragraphs.en: All her magic was used to help the people, and she was never known to hurt anyone who was good.
paragraphs.cn: 她的魔法都是用来帮助别人的，她从没伤害过好人。

paragraphs.en: Her name was Gayelette, and she lived in a handsome palace built from great blocks of ruby.
paragraphs.cn: 她叫盖耶莱特，住在一座漂亮的宫殿里，宫殿是用大块红宝石建成的。

paragraphs.en: Everyone loved her, but her greatest sorrow was that she could find no one to love in return, since all the men were much too stupid and ugly to mate with one so beautiful and wise.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都喜欢她，但她最伤心的是，找不到一个能真心喜欢她的人。因为所有男人都又笨又丑，配不上她这样又美又聪明的公主。

paragraphs.en: At last, however, she found a boy who was handsome and manly and wise beyond his years.
paragraphs.cn: 终于，她找到了一个男孩。他又帅气又勇敢，而且比同龄人更聪明。

paragraphs.en: Gayelette made up her mind that when he grew to be a man she would make him her husband, so she took him to her ruby palace and used all her magic powers to make him as strong and good and lovely as any woman could wish.
paragraphs.cn: 盖耶莱特决定，等他长大成人，就嫁给他。于是，她把他带回自己的红宝石宫殿，用尽所有魔法，让他变得又强壮又善良，还像任何女人希望的那样可爱。

paragraphs.en: When he grew to manhood, Quelala, as he was called, was said to be the best and wisest man in all the land, while his manly beauty was so great that Gayelette loved him dearly, and hastened to make everything ready for the wedding.
paragraphs.cn: 等他长大成人，人们都说他叫奎拉拉，是这片土地上最好、最聪明的人。他又帅气又英武，盖耶莱特非常爱他，赶紧准备他们的婚礼。

paragraphs.en: “My grandfather was at that time the King of the Winged Monkeys which lived in the forest near Gayelette’s palace, and the old fellow loved a joke better than a good dinner.
paragraphs.cn: “我的爷爷那时候是飞猴的国王，他们住在盖耶莱特宫殿附近的森林里。我爷爷这老头子啊，就爱开玩笑，比喜欢美食还爱。

paragraphs.en: One day, just before the wedding, my grandfather was flying out with his band when he saw Quelala walking beside the river.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天，就在婚礼前不久，我爷爷带着他的猴子们飞出去，看到奎拉拉在河边散步。

paragraphs.en: He was dressed in a rich costume of pink silk and purple velvet, and my grandfather thought he would see what he could do.
paragraphs.cn: 他穿着一套华丽的衣服，是粉色丝绸和紫色天鹅绒做的。我爷爷心想，他要捉弄一下他。

paragraphs.en: At his word the band flew down and seized Quelala, carried him in their arms until they were over the middle of the river, and then dropped him into the water.
paragraphs.cn: 爷爷一声令下，猴子们就飞下去抓住了奎拉拉，把他抬起来，一直飞到河中央，然后把他扔进了水里。

paragraphs.en: “‘Swim out, my fine fellow,’ cried my grandfather, ‘and see if the water has spotted your clothes.’
paragraphs.cn: “‘游出来吧，小伙子！’我爷爷大声喊，‘看看水是不是把你的衣服弄脏了。’

paragraphs.en: Quelala was much too wise not to swim, and he was not in the least spoiled by all his good fortune.
paragraphs.cn: 奎拉拉很聪明，他知道要游泳。他并没有因为好运而变得娇气。

paragraphs.en: He laughed, when he came to the top of the water, and swam in to shore.
paragraphs.cn: 当他浮出水面时，他笑了，然后游到了岸边。

paragraphs.en: But when Gayelette came running out to him she found his silks and velvet all ruined by the river.
paragraphs.cn: 可是当盖耶莱特跑出来找他时，发现他的丝绸和天鹅绒衣服都被河水弄坏了。

paragraphs.en: “The princess was angry, and she knew, of course, who did it.
paragraphs.cn: “公主很生气，她当然知道是谁做的。

paragraphs.en: She had all the Winged Monkeys brought before her, and she said at first that their wings should be tied and they should be treated as they had treated Quelala, and dropped in the river.
paragraphs.cn: 她把所有的飞猴都叫到她面前，一开始她说要把它们的翅膀绑起来，像它们对待奎拉拉一样，把它们扔进河里。

paragraphs.en: But my grandfather pleaded hard, for he knew the Monkeys would drown in the river with their wings tied, and Quelala said a kind word for them also; so that Gayelette finally spared them, on condition that the Winged Monkeys should ever after do three times the bidding of the owner of the Golden Cap.
paragraphs.cn: 但是我爷爷努力求情，因为他知道猴子们翅膀被绑住会淹死在河里。奎拉拉也替它们说了好话。所以盖耶莱特最后饶了它们，条件是：从今以后，飞猴要听金冠的主人三次命令。

paragraphs.en: This Cap had been made for a wedding present to Quelala, and it is said to have cost the princess half her kingdom.
paragraphs.cn: 这顶帽子是给奎拉拉做的结婚礼物，据说公主为了它，花掉了半个国家。

paragraphs.en: Of course my grandfather and all the other Monkeys at once agreed to the condition, and that is how it happens that we are three times the slaves of the owner of the Golden Cap, whosoever he may be.”
paragraphs.cn: 当然，我爷爷和所有其他猴子立刻同意了这个条件。所以啊，我们成了金冠主人的三次奴隶，不管他是谁。”

paragraphs.en: “And what became of them?” asked Dorothy, who had been greatly interested in the story.
paragraphs.cn: “后来它们怎么样了？”多萝西问，她听故事听得很有兴趣。

paragraphs.en: “Quelala being the first owner of the Golden Cap,” replied the Monkey, “he was the first to lay his wishes upon us.
paragraphs.cn: “奎拉拉是金冠的第一个主人，”猴子回答说，“他是第一个命令我们做事的。

paragraphs.en: As his bride could not bear the sight of us, he called us all to him in the forest after he had married her and ordered us always to keep where she could never again set eyes on a Winged Monkey, which we were glad to do, for we were all afraid of her.
paragraphs.cn: 因为他的新娘受不了看到我们，所以他结婚后把我们都叫到森林里，命令我们永远待在她看不见飞猴的地方。我们也很乐意这样做，因为我们都很怕她。

paragraphs.en: “This was all we ever had to do until the Golden Cap fell into the hands of the Wicked Witch of the West, who made us enslave the Winkies, and afterward drive Oz himself out of the Land of the West.
paragraphs.cn: “我们一直都只做这些事，直到金冠落到了西方坏女巫手里。他让我们去奴役温基人，后来又把奥兹大王赶出了西方之地。

paragraphs.en: Now the Golden Cap is yours, and three times you have the right to lay your wishes upon us.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，这顶金冠是你的了，你有三次权利来命令我们。”

paragraphs.en: As the Monkey King finished his story Dorothy looked down and saw the green, shining walls of the Emerald City before them.
paragraphs.cn: 猴子王讲完故事，多萝西低头一看，只见翡翠城的绿色发光的墙壁就在他们眼前。

paragraphs.en: She wondered at the rapid flight of the Monkeys, but was glad the journey was over.
paragraphs.cn: 她看到猴子飞得很快，感到很惊奇，但很高兴旅程结束了。

paragraphs.en: The strange creatures set the travelers down carefully before the gate of the City, the King bowed low to Dorothy, and then flew swiftly away, followed by all his band.
paragraphs.cn: 这些奇怪的家伙小心地把旅行者们放在城门前，猴王向多萝西深深地鞠了一躬，然后带着所有猴子飞走了。

paragraphs.en: “That was a good ride,” said the little girl.
paragraphs.cn: “这次飞得真棒！”小女孩说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, and a quick way out of our troubles,” replied the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，这样我们就能很快摆脱麻烦了！”狮子回答说。

paragraphs.en: “How lucky it was you brought away that wonderful Cap!”
paragraphs.cn: “你把那顶很棒的帽子带走，真是太幸运了！”

chapters.title_en: The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible

paragraphs.en: The four travelers walked up to the great gate of Emerald City and rang the bell.
paragraphs.cn: 四个旅行者走到翡翠城的大门前，按响了门铃。

paragraphs.en: After ringing several times, it was opened by the same Guardian of the Gates they had met before.
paragraphs.cn: 按了几次门铃后，还是以前他们见过的那个城门守卫开了门。

paragraphs.en: “What! are you back again?” he asked, in surprise.
paragraphs.cn: “什么！你们又回来了？”他很惊讶地问。

paragraphs.en: “Do you not see us?” answered the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你没看见我们吗？”稻草人回答说。

paragraphs.en: “But I thought you had gone to visit the Wicked Witch of the West.”
paragraphs.cn: “可我以为你们是去拜访西方坏女巫了呢。”

paragraphs.en: “We did visit her,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我们确实去拜访她了，”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “And she let you go again?” asked the man, in wonder.
paragraphs.cn: “她又让你们走了吗？”那人很疑惑地问。

paragraphs.en: “She could not help it, for she is melted,” explained the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “她没办法，因为她融化了，”稻草人解释说。

paragraphs.en: “Melted!
paragraphs.cn: “融化了！

paragraphs.en: Well, that is good news, indeed,” said the man.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，那真是个好消息！”那人说。

paragraphs.en: “Who melted her?”
paragraphs.cn: “谁把她融化的？”

paragraphs.en: “It was Dorothy,” said the Lion gravely.
paragraphs.cn: “是多萝西，”狮子很认真地说。

paragraphs.en: “Good gracious!” exclaimed the man, and he bowed very low indeed before her.
paragraphs.cn: “天哪！”那人喊道，然后在她面前深深地鞠了一躬。

paragraphs.en: Then he led them into his little room and locked the spectacles from the great box on all their eyes, just as he had done before.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，他把他们带进自己的小房间，从大盒子里拿出眼镜，给他们每个人戴上，就像以前一样。

paragraphs.en: Afterward they passed on through the gate into the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他们穿过大门，走进了翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: When the people heard from the Guardian of the Gates that Dorothy had melted the Wicked Witch of the West, they all gathered around the travelers and followed them in a great crowd to the Palace of Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 当人们从城门守卫那里听说多萝西融化了西方坏女巫时，他们都围住旅行者，一大群人跟着他们来到了奥兹大王的宫殿。

paragraphs.en: The soldier with the green whiskers was still on guard before the door, but he let them in at once, and they were again met by the beautiful green girl, who showed each of them to their old rooms at once, so they might rest until the Great Oz was ready to receive them.
paragraphs.cn: 那个留着绿胡子的士兵还在门前站岗，但他立刻让他们进去了。美丽的绿衣女孩又来迎接他们，马上把他们带回了以前的房间，这样他们就可以休息，直到伟大的奥兹大王准备好接见他们。

paragraphs.en: The soldier had the news carried straight to Oz that Dorothy and the other travelers had come back again, after destroying the Wicked Witch; but Oz made no reply.
paragraphs.cn: 士兵把消息直接带给了奥兹大王，说多萝西和其他旅行者在消灭了坏女巫之后又回来了；但奥兹大王没有回答。

paragraphs.en: They thought the Great Wizard would send for them at once, but he did not.
paragraphs.cn: 他们以为伟大的巫师会立刻派人请他们，但他没有。

paragraphs.en: They had no word from him the next day, nor the next, nor the next.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天、第三天、第四天，他们都没有收到他的消息。

paragraphs.en: The waiting was tiresome and wearing, and at last they grew vexed that Oz should treat them in so poor a fashion, after sending them to undergo hardships and slavery.
paragraphs.cn: 等待让人很疲倦，很烦躁。最后他们很生气，觉得奥兹大王让他们去受苦受难后，竟然这样对待他们。

paragraphs.en: So the Scarecrow at last asked the green girl to take another message to Oz, saying if he did not let them in to see him at once they would call the Winged Monkeys to help them, and find out whether he kept his promises or not.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，稻草人终于让绿衣女孩再带个口信给奥兹大王，说如果他不马上让他们进去见他，他们就要请飞猴来帮忙，看看他有没有遵守诺言。

paragraphs.en: When the Wizard was given this message he was so frightened that he sent word for them to come to the Throne Room at four minutes after nine o’clock the next morning.
paragraphs.cn: 巫师听到这个口信后，吓坏了，他让人传话说，让他们第二天早上九点零四分到王座室来。

paragraphs.en: He had once met the Winged Monkeys in the Land of the West, and he did not wish to meet them again.
paragraphs.cn: 他以前在西方国家见过飞猴，不想再见到他们了。

paragraphs.en: The four travelers passed a sleepless night, each thinking of the gift Oz had promised to bestow on him.
paragraphs.cn: 四个旅行者度过了一个不眠之夜，每个人都在想着奥兹大王答应要给他们的礼物。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy fell asleep only once, and then she dreamed she was in Kansas, where Aunt Em was telling her how glad she was to have her little girl at home again.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西只睡着了一会儿，她就梦到自己去了堪萨斯。在梦里，艾姆婶婶告诉她，小女儿回家她有多开心。

paragraphs.en: Promptly at nine o’clock the next morning the green-whiskered soldier came to them, and four minutes later they all went into the Throne Room of the Great Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上九点，绿胡子士兵准时来了。四分钟后，他们都进了大奥兹大王的王座厅。

paragraphs.en: Of course each one of them expected to see the Wizard in the shape he had taken before, and all were greatly surprised when they looked about and saw no one at all in the room.
paragraphs.cn: 他们都以为会看到巫师变成以前的样子，结果一看房间里一个人都没有，大家都非常吃惊。

paragraphs.en: They kept close to the door and closer to one another, for the stillness of the empty room was more dreadful than any of the forms they had seen Oz take.
paragraphs.cn: 他们紧紧靠着门，也紧紧靠着彼此。空房间的安静比他们见过的任何一个奥兹大王的样子都可怕。

paragraphs.en: Presently they heard a solemn Voice, that seemed to come from somewhere near the top of the great dome, and it said:
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他们听到一个很庄重又很响亮的声音，好像是从大圆顶上面传来的。声音说：

paragraphs.en: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible.
paragraphs.cn: “我是奥兹大王，伟大又可怕的巫师。”

paragraphs.en: Why do you seek me?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们为什么来找我？”

paragraphs.en: They looked again in every part of the room, and then, seeing no one, Dorothy asked, “Where are you?”
paragraphs.cn: 他们又把房间每个地方都看了看，还是没看到人。然后，多萝西问：“你在哪里呀？”

paragraphs.en: “I am everywhere,” answered the Voice, “but to the eyes of common mortals I am invisible.
paragraphs.cn: “我无处不在，”声音回答，“但普通人是看不见我的。”

paragraphs.en: I will now seat myself upon my throne, that you may converse with me.”
paragraphs.cn: 我现在要坐在我的王座上，你们可以和我说话了。”

paragraphs.en: Indeed, the Voice seemed just then to come straight from the throne itself; so they walked toward it and stood in a row while Dorothy said:
paragraphs.cn: 确实，声音好像是从王座那里直接传来的。于是他们走向王座，排成一排站着。多萝西说：

paragraphs.en: “We have come to claim our promise, O Oz.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们来要你给我们的承诺，哦，奥兹大王。”

paragraphs.en: “What promise?” asked Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “什么承诺？”奥兹大王问。

paragraphs.en: “You promised to send me back to Kansas when the Wicked Witch was destroyed,” said the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “你答应过我，如果坏女巫被消灭了，就把我送回堪萨斯，”小女孩说。

paragraphs.en: “And you promised to give me brains,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你还答应给我智慧的大脑，”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “And you promised to give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “你还答应给我一颗心，”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “And you promised to give me courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “你还答应给我勇气，”胆小的狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “Is the Wicked Witch really destroyed?” asked the Voice, and Dorothy thought it trembled a little.
paragraphs.cn: “坏女巫真的被消灭了吗？”声音问道，多萝西觉得声音好像有点颤抖。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” she answered, “I melted her with a bucket of water.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，”她回答，“我用一桶水把她融化了。”

paragraphs.en: “Dear me,” said the Voice, “how sudden!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，”声音说，“这么快就发生了！”

paragraphs.en: Well, come to me tomorrow, for I must have time to think it over.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，你们明天再来找我吧，我需要时间好好想想。”

paragraphs.en: “You’ve had plenty of time already,” said the Tin Woodman angrily.
paragraphs.cn: “你已经想了很久了！”铁皮人生气地说。

paragraphs.en: “We shan’t wait a day longer,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我们一天都不能再等了！”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “You must keep your promises to us!” exclaimed Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “你一定要遵守对我们的承诺！”多萝西大声说。

paragraphs.en: The Lion thought it might be as well to frighten the Wizard, so he gave a large, loud roar, which was so fierce and dreadful that Toto jumped away from him in alarm and tipped over the screen that stood in a corner.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子觉得也许吓唬一下巫师也不错，于是他大声地吼了一声。吼声又猛烈又可怕，把托托吓了一跳，赶紧跳开，还把墙角的一个屏风碰倒了。
