paragraphs.en: As it fell with a crash they looked that way, and the next moment all of them were filled with wonder.
paragraphs.cn: 屏风轰的一声倒下时，他们都往那边看去。下一刻，大家都非常惊讶。

paragraphs.en: For they saw, standing in just the spot the screen had hidden, a little old man, with a bald head and a wrinkled face, who seemed to be as much surprised as they were.
paragraphs.cn: 因为他们看到，就在屏风后面，站着一个头发很少、满脸皱纹的小老头。他看起来和他们一样吃惊。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman, raising his axe, rushed toward the little man and cried out, “Who are you?”
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人举起斧头，冲向小老头，大声喊道：“你是谁？”

paragraphs.en: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible,” said the little man, in a trembling voice.
paragraphs.cn: “我是奥兹大王，伟大又可怕的巫师，”小老头颤抖着声音说。

paragraphs.en: “But don’t strike me—please don’t—and I’ll do anything you want me to.”
paragraphs.cn: “但别打我——求你了别打我——你要我做什么都行。”

paragraphs.en: Our friends looked at him in surprise and dismay.
paragraphs.cn: 朋友们很惊讶，也很失望地看着他。

paragraphs.en: “I thought Oz was a great Head,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我以为 奥兹大王 是个很厉害的大脑袋呢，” 多萝西 说。

paragraphs.en: “And I thought Oz was a lovely Lady,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我以为 奥兹大王 是个漂亮的女士呢，” 稻草人 说。

paragraphs.en: “And I thought Oz was a terrible Beast,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “我以为 奥兹大王 是个可怕的野兽呢，” 铁皮人 说。

paragraphs.en: “And I thought Oz was a Ball of Fire,” exclaimed the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “我以为 奥兹大王 是个火球呢！” 狮子 叫道。

paragraphs.en: “No, you are all wrong,” said the little man meekly.
paragraphs.cn: “不，你们都想错了，”小个子男人轻轻地说。

paragraphs.en: “I have been making believe.”
paragraphs.cn: “我一直在假装。”

paragraphs.en: “Making believe!” cried Dorothy. “Are you not a Great Wizard?”
paragraphs.cn: “假装？” 多萝西 喊道。“你不是个很厉害的魔法师吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, my dear,” he said.
paragraphs.cn: “嘘，亲爱的，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Don’t speak so loud, or you will be overheard—and I should be ruined.
paragraphs.cn: “别说那么大声，不然会被别人听到的——我就完蛋了。

paragraphs.en: I’m supposed to be a Great Wizard.”
paragraphs.cn: 大家都以为我是个很厉害的魔法师呢。”

paragraphs.en: “And aren’t you?” she asked.
paragraphs.cn: “你不是吗？”她问。

paragraphs.en: “Not a bit of it, my dear; I’m just a common man.”
paragraphs.cn: “一点也不是，亲爱的；我只是个普通人。”

paragraphs.en: “You’re more than that,” said the Scarecrow, in a grieved tone; “you’re a humbug.”
paragraphs.cn: “你可不止那样，” 稻草人 伤心地说，“你是个骗子。”

paragraphs.en: “Exactly so!” declared the little man, rubbing his hands together as if it pleased him. “I am a humbug.”
paragraphs.cn: “没错！”小个子男人说，高兴地搓着手，“我就是个骗子。”

paragraphs.en: “But this is terrible,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “但这太糟糕了！” 铁皮人 说。

paragraphs.en: “How shall I ever get my heart?”
paragraphs.cn: “那我的心要怎么才能拿到呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Or I my courage?” asked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “那我的勇气呢？” 狮子 问。

paragraphs.en: “Or I my brains?” wailed the Scarecrow, wiping the tears from his eyes with his coat sleeve.
paragraphs.cn: “那我的脑子呢？” 稻草人 哭着说，用衣袖擦掉眼泪。

paragraphs.en: “My dear friends,” said Oz, “I pray you not to speak of these little things.
paragraphs.cn: “我亲爱的朋友们，” 奥兹大王 说，“求你们别提这些小事了。

paragraphs.en: Think of me, and the terrible trouble I’m in at being found out.”
paragraphs.cn: 想想我吧，我被发现了，这麻烦可大了！”

paragraphs.en: “Doesn’t anyone else know you’re a humbug?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “难道没有别人知道你是个骗子吗？” 多萝西 问。

paragraphs.en: “No one knows it but you four—and myself,” replied Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “除了你们四个——还有我，没有人知道，” 奥兹大王 回答说。

paragraphs.en: “I have fooled everyone so long that I thought I should never be found out.
paragraphs.cn: “我骗了大家这么久，以为永远不会被发现呢。

paragraphs.en: It was a great mistake my ever letting you into the Throne Room.
paragraphs.cn: 让你们进到王座厅里来，真是个大错啊。

paragraphs.en: Usually I will not see even my subjects, and so they believe I am something terrible.”
paragraphs.cn: 平时我连我的子民都不见，所以他们都觉得我很可怕。”

paragraphs.en: “But, I don’t understand,” said Dorothy, in bewilderment.
paragraphs.cn: “可是，我不明白，” 多萝西 迷茫地说。

paragraphs.en: “How was it that you appeared to me as a great Head?”
paragraphs.cn: “你怎么会变成一个大脑袋出现在我面前的呢？”

paragraphs.en: “That was one of my tricks,” answered Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “那是我变的一个小把戏，” 奥兹大王 回答说。

paragraphs.en: “Step this way, please, and I will tell you all about it.”
paragraphs.cn: “请往这边走，我会把所有事情都告诉你们。”

paragraphs.en: He led the way to a small chamber in the rear of the Throne Room, and they all followed him.
paragraphs.cn: 他带大家走到王座厅后面的一个小房间，大家都跟着他进去了。

paragraphs.en: He pointed to one corner, in which lay the great Head, made out of many thicknesses of paper, and with a carefully painted face.
paragraphs.cn: 他指着一个角落，那里有一个大脑袋。它用很多层纸做的，脸上还画得很漂亮。

paragraphs.en: “This I hung from the ceiling by a wire,” said Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “我把这个用铁丝挂在天花板上。”奥兹大王说。

paragraphs.en: “I stood behind the screen and pulled a thread, to make the eyes move and the mouth open.”
paragraphs.cn: “我躲在屏风后面，拉一拉线，就能让眼睛动，嘴巴张开。”

paragraphs.en: “But how about the voice?” she inquired.
paragraphs.cn: “那声音呢？声音是从哪里来的？”她问。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I am a ventriloquist,” said the little man.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，我是一个会腹语的人。”小个子男人说。

paragraphs.en: “I can throw the sound of my voice wherever I wish, so that you thought it was coming out of the Head.
paragraphs.cn: “我想让声音从哪里出来，它就能从哪里出来。所以你们才以为是从大脑袋里发出来的。”

paragraphs.en: Here are the other things I used to deceive you.”
paragraphs.cn: “这些就是我用来骗你们的其他东西。”

paragraphs.en: He showed the Scarecrow the dress and the mask he had worn when he seemed to be the lovely Lady.
paragraphs.cn: 他给稻草人看了，他扮成漂亮女士时穿的裙子和戴的面具。

paragraphs.en: And the Tin Woodman saw that his terrible Beast was nothing but a lot of skins, sewn together, with slats to keep their sides out.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人发现，他那只可怕的野兽，原来只是一堆皮缝起来的，里面还有木条撑着。

paragraphs.en: As for the Ball of Fire, the false Wizard had hung that also from the ceiling.
paragraphs.cn: 那个火球呢，假巫师也把它挂在天花板上。

paragraphs.en: It was really a ball of cotton, but when oil was poured upon it the ball burned fiercely.
paragraphs.cn: 它其实是一个棉花球，只要把油倒在上面，棉花球就会烧得很旺。

paragraphs.en: “Really,” said the Scarecrow, “you ought to be ashamed of yourself for being such a humbug.”
paragraphs.cn: “真是的，”稻草人说，“你这么骗人，真应该觉得不好意思。”

paragraphs.en: “I am—I certainly am,” answered the little man sorrowfully; “but it was the only thing I could do.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊——我当然不好意思啦。”小个子男人难过地说，“可我只能那样做。”

paragraphs.en: Sit down, please, there are plenty of chairs; and I will tell you my story.”
paragraphs.cn: “请坐下吧，有很多椅子呢。我来给你们讲我的故事。”

paragraphs.en: So they sat down and listened while he told the following tale.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们坐下来，听他讲起下面的故事。

paragraphs.en: “I was born in Omaha—”
paragraphs.cn: “我出生在奥马哈——”

paragraphs.en: “Why, that isn’t very far from Kansas!” cried Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，那离堪萨斯不远嘛！”多萝西叫道。

paragraphs.en: “No, but it’s farther from here,” he said, shaking his head at her sadly.
paragraphs.cn: “不，可是离这里更远。”他难过地对她摇了摇头说。

paragraphs.en: “When I grew up I became a ventriloquist, and at that I was very well trained by a great master.
paragraphs.cn: “我长大后，成了一个会腹语的人，跟一个很厉害的老师学得可好了。”

paragraphs.en: I can imitate any kind of a bird or beast.”
paragraphs.cn: “我能学各种各样的鸟叫和动物叫。”

paragraphs.en: Here he mewed so like a kitten that Toto pricked up his ears and looked everywhere to see where she was.
paragraphs.cn: 他“喵”了一声，学得太像小猫了，托托赶紧竖起耳朵，到处找小猫在哪儿呢。

paragraphs.en: “After a time,” continued Oz, “I tired of that, and became a balloonist.”
paragraphs.cn: “过了一段时间，”奥兹大王继续说，“我玩腻了，就去开热气球了。”

paragraphs.en: “What is that?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么呀？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “A man who goes up in a balloon on circus day, so as to draw a crowd of people together and get them to pay to see the circus,” he explained.
paragraphs.cn: “就是马戏团表演那天，坐热气球飞上天的人。他想把大家都吸引过来，让大家买票去看马戏。”他解释说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” she said, “I know.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，”她说，“我明白了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, one day I went up in a balloon and the ropes got twisted, so that I couldn’t come down again.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，有一天我坐热气球飞上天，绳子缠住了，我就再也下不来了。”

paragraphs.en: It went way up above the clouds, so far that a current of air struck it and carried it many, many miles away.
paragraphs.cn: 它飞到云层上面很高很高的地方，一阵风吹过来，把它吹到很远很远的地方去了。

paragraphs.en: For a day and a night I traveled through the air, and on the morning of the second day I awoke and found the balloon floating over a strange and beautiful country.
paragraphs.cn: 我在天上飞了一天一夜，第二天早上醒来时，发现热气球正飘在一个陌生又漂亮的地方上空。

paragraphs.en: “It came down gradually, and I was not hurt a bit.
paragraphs.cn: “它慢慢地降下来了，我一点儿也没受伤。”

paragraphs.en: But I found myself in the midst of a strange people, who, seeing me come from the clouds, thought I was a great Wizard.
paragraphs.cn: 但我发现我身边都是奇怪的人，他们看到我从天上下来，就以为我是个厉害的魔法师。

paragraphs.en: Of course I let them think so, because they were afraid of me, and promised to do anything I wished them to.
paragraphs.cn: 我当然让他们那样想了，因为他们都怕我，还答应我说什么就做什么。

paragraphs.en: “Just to amuse myself, and keep the good people busy, I ordered them to build this City, and my Palace; and they did it all willingly and well.
paragraphs.cn: “我只是想找点乐子，也想让大家都有事做，就让他们建了这座城市和我的宫殿。他们都非常乐意，也做得很好。

paragraphs.en: Then I thought, as the country was so green and beautiful, I would call it the Emerald City; and to make the name fit better I put green spectacles on all the people, so that everything they saw was green.”
paragraphs.cn: 然后我想，这个地方这么绿，这么美，我就叫它翡翠城。为了让名字更好听，我给所有人都戴上了绿色的眼镜，这样他们看什么都是绿色的。”

paragraphs.en: “But isn’t everything here green?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “可是，这里所有东西不都是绿色的吗？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “No more than in any other city,” replied Oz; “but when you wear green spectacles, why of course everything you see looks green to you.
paragraphs.cn: “不比别的城市更绿。”奥兹大王回答，“不过，当你戴着绿眼镜时，当然看什么都是绿色的啦。

paragraphs.en: The Emerald City was built a great many years ago, for I was a young man when the balloon brought me here, and I am a very old man now.
paragraphs.cn: 翡翠城是在很多很多年前建的，气球把我带来的时候我还很年轻，现在我已经是个老爷爷了。

paragraphs.en: But my people have worn green glasses on their eyes so long that most of them think it really is an Emerald City, and it certainly is a beautiful place, abounding in jewels and precious metals, and every good thing that is needed to make one happy.
paragraphs.cn: 但我的人民戴绿眼镜戴了很久，所以大部分人都觉得这里真的是翡翠城。这里确实很美，有好多宝石、值钱的金属，还有好多好东西能让人开心。

paragraphs.en: I have been good to the people, and they like me; but ever since this Palace was built, I have shut myself up and would not see any of them.
paragraphs.cn: 我对大家很好，他们也喜欢我。但自从这座宫殿建好后，我就把自己关起来，再也不见他们了。

paragraphs.en: “One of my greatest fears was the Witches, for while I had no magical powers at all I soon found out that the Witches were really able to do wonderful things.
paragraphs.cn: “我最害怕的就是女巫们。虽然我一点魔法都不会，但我很快就发现女巫们真的能做出很厉害的事情。

paragraphs.en: There were four of them in this country, and they ruled the people who live in the North and South and East and West.
paragraphs.cn: 这个国家有四个女巫，她们管理着住在北方、南方、东方和西方的人。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, the Witches of the North and South were good, and I knew they would do me no harm; but the Witches of the East and West were terribly wicked, and had they not thought I was more powerful than they themselves, they would surely have destroyed me.
paragraphs.cn: 幸好，北方和南方的女巫是好人，我知道她们不会伤害我。但东方和西方的女巫非常坏，如果她们没有觉得我比她们更厉害，她们肯定会把我消灭掉。

paragraphs.en: As it was, I lived in deadly fear of them for many years; so you can imagine how pleased I was when I heard your house had fallen on the Wicked Witch of the East.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，我好多年都非常害怕她们。所以你可以想象，当我听说你的房子压在东方坏女巫身上时，我有多开心。

paragraphs.en: When you came to me, I was willing to promise anything if you would only do away with the other Witch; but, now that you have melted her, I am ashamed to say that I cannot keep my promises.”
paragraphs.cn: 你来找我的时候，我愿意答应你任何事，只要你能把另一个女巫除掉。可是，现在你已经把她融化了，我很不好意思地说，我不能遵守我的诺言了。”

paragraphs.en: “I think you are a very bad man,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得你是个很坏很坏的人。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no, my dear; I’m really a very good man, but I’m a very bad Wizard, I must admit.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不，亲爱的；我其实是个很好很好的人，但我真是个很笨的魔法师，我得承认。”

paragraphs.en: “Can’t you give me brains?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你不能给我一些脑子吗？”稻草人问。

paragraphs.en: “You don’t need them.
paragraphs.cn: “你不需要那些东西。

paragraphs.en: You are learning something every day.
paragraphs.cn: 你每天都在学习新东西。

paragraphs.en: A baby has brains, but it doesn’t know much.
paragraphs.cn: 小宝宝有脑子，但它知道的不多。

paragraphs.en: Experience is the only thing that brings knowledge, and the longer you are on earth the more experience you are sure to get.”
paragraphs.cn: 经验是唯一能让你学到东西的方法。你在世界上待得越久，就会有越多的经验。”

paragraphs.en: “That may all be true,” said the Scarecrow, “but I shall be very unhappy unless you give me brains.”
paragraphs.cn: “这些可能都是真的。”稻草人说，“但如果你不给我脑子，我就会很不开心。”

paragraphs.en: The false Wizard looked at him carefully.
paragraphs.cn: 那个假魔法师仔细地看着他。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” he said with a sigh, “I’m not much of a magician, as I said; but if you will come to me tomorrow morning, I will stuff your head with brains.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧。”他叹了口气说，“我不是什么厉害的魔法师，就像我说的那样。不过，如果你明天早上来找我，我会把你的脑袋塞满脑子。

paragraphs.en: I cannot tell you how to use them, however; you must find that out for yourself.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过，我不能告诉你怎么用它们哦！你得自己去想办法。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, thank you—thank you!” cried the Scarecrow. “I’ll find a way to use them, never fear!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，谢谢你——谢谢你！”稻草人大声说，“我一定会找到办法用它们的，别怕！”

paragraphs.en: “But how about my courage?” asked the Lion anxiously.
paragraphs.cn: “那我的勇气呢？”狮子很着急地问。

paragraphs.en: “You have plenty of courage, I am sure,” answered Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “你有很多很多勇气，我确定。”奥兹大王回答。

paragraphs.en: “All you need is confidence in yourself.
paragraphs.cn: 你只需要相信你自己就行了。

paragraphs.en: There is no living thing that is not afraid when it faces danger.
paragraphs.cn: 面对危险的时候，没有哪个小动物或人是不害怕的。

paragraphs.en: The True courage is in facing danger when you are afraid, and that kind of courage you have in plenty.”
paragraphs.cn: 真正的勇气就是，就算心里害怕，也要去面对危险。你有很多这样的勇气。”

paragraphs.en: “Perhaps I have, but I’m scared just the same,” said the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “也许我有，但我还是有点害怕。” 狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “I shall really be very unhappy unless you give me the sort of courage that makes one forget he is afraid.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果你不给我那种让人忘了害怕的勇气，我真的会很不开心。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well, I will give you that sort of courage tomorrow,” replied Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “好的，我明天就给你那种勇气。” 奥兹大王回答。

paragraphs.en: “How about my heart?” asked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “那我的心呢？” 铁皮人问。

paragraphs.en: “Why, as for that,” answered Oz, “I think you are wrong to want a heart.
paragraphs.cn: “噢，至于心嘛，” 奥兹大王说，“我觉得你想要心是错的。

paragraphs.en: It makes most people unhappy.
paragraphs.cn: 心会让很多人不开心。

paragraphs.en: If you only knew it, you are in luck not to have a heart.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你知道，没有心，你其实是很幸运的。”

paragraphs.en: “That must be a matter of opinion,” said the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “那可能是每个人想法不一样吧。” 铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “For my part, I will bear all the unhappiness without a murmur, if you will give me the heart.”
paragraphs.cn: “我呢，如果你给我一颗心，就算不开心，我也不会抱怨。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well,” answered Oz meekly.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧。” 奥兹大王乖乖地回答。

paragraphs.en: “Come to me tomorrow and you shall have a heart.
paragraphs.cn: “你明天来找我，我就会给你一颗心。

paragraphs.en: I have played Wizard for so many years that I may as well continue the part a little longer.”
paragraphs.cn: 我当巫师这么多年了，再多当一会儿也没关系。”

paragraphs.en: “And now,” said Dorothy, “how am I to get back to Kansas?”
paragraphs.cn: “那现在呢，” 多萝西说，“我怎么才能回到 堪萨斯呢？”

paragraphs.en: “We shall have to think about that,” replied the little man.
paragraphs.cn: “我们得好好想想这个。” 小矮人回答。

paragraphs.en: “Give me two or three days to consider the matter and I’ll try to find a way to carry you over the desert.
paragraphs.cn: “给我两三天时间想想，我会想办法带你们穿过沙漠。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime you shall all be treated as my guests, and while you live in the Palace my people will wait upon you and obey your slightest wish.
paragraphs.cn: 在这几天里，你们都是我的客人。你们住在宫殿里的时候，我的人会好好照顾你们，听你们的话。

paragraphs.en: There is only one thing I ask in return for my help—such as it is.
paragraphs.cn: 我帮你们，只求你们做一件事。

paragraphs.en: You must keep my secret and tell no one I am a humbug.”
paragraphs.cn: 你们一定要帮我保守秘密，不能告诉别人我只是一个骗子。”

paragraphs.en: They agreed to say nothing of what they had learned, and went back to their rooms in high spirits.
paragraphs.cn: 他们答应不说出自己知道的秘密，然后高高兴兴地回到了自己的房间。

paragraphs.en: Even Dorothy had hope that “The Great and Terrible Humbug,” as she called him, would find a way to send her back to Kansas, and if he did she was willing to forgive him everything.
paragraphs.cn: 连 多萝西 都相信，那个她叫做“又大又坏的骗子”会想办法送她回 堪萨斯。如果他做到了，她就愿意原谅他做过的一切。

chapters.title_en: The Magic Art of the Great Humbug

paragraphs.en: Next morning the Scarecrow said to his friends:
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，稻草人 对他的朋友们说：

paragraphs.en: “Congratulate me.
paragraphs.cn: “恭喜我！

paragraphs.en: I am going to Oz to get my brains at last.
paragraphs.cn: 我终于要去 奥兹大王 那里拿我的大脑了。

paragraphs.en: When I return I shall be as other men are.”
paragraphs.cn: 等我回来，我就会和别人一样聪明了。”

paragraphs.en: “I have always liked you as you were,” said Dorothy simply.
paragraphs.cn: “我一直都喜欢你现在的样子。” 多萝西 简单地说。

paragraphs.en: “It is kind of you to like a Scarecrow,” he replied.
paragraphs.cn: “你喜欢一个 稻草人，真是太好了。” 他回答。

paragraphs.en: “But surely you will think more of me when you hear the splendid thoughts my new brain is going to turn out.”
paragraphs.cn: “不过，等你听到我的新大脑想出那些很棒的点子，你一定会更喜欢我的。”

paragraphs.en: Then he said good-bye to them all in a cheerful voice and went to the Throne Room, where he rapped upon the door.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，他开心地跟大家说再见，去了王座室，敲了敲门。

paragraphs.en: “Come in,” said Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “进来。” 奥兹大王说。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow went in and found the little man sitting down by the window, engaged in deep thought.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人进去了，发现小矮人坐在窗边，在想事情呢。

paragraphs.en: “I have come for my brains,” remarked the Scarecrow, a little uneasily.
paragraphs.cn: “我来取我的脑子。” 稻草人有点不安地说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes; sit down in that chair, please,” replied Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，好的。请坐到那把椅子上。” 奥兹大王回答说。

paragraphs.en: “You must excuse me for taking your head off, but I shall have to do it in order to put your brains in their proper place.”
paragraphs.cn: “我得把你的头拿下来，真是不好意思。不过，只有这样，我才能把你的脑子放到对的地方。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “没关系。” 稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “You are quite welcome to take my head off, as long as it will be a better one when you put it on again.”
paragraphs.cn: “你尽管把我的头拿下来吧，只要你再给我装上的时候，我的头能变得更好就行。”

paragraphs.en: So the Wizard unfastened his head and emptied out the straw.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，魔法师解开了他的头，把里面的稻草都倒了出来。

paragraphs.en: Then he entered the back room and took up a measure of bran, which he mixed with a great many pins and needles.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他走进后面的房间，拿出一些麸皮，又把好多大头针和缝衣针混了进去。

paragraphs.en: Having shaken them together thoroughly, he filled the top of the Scarecrow’s head with the mixture and stuffed the rest of the space with straw, to hold it in place.
paragraphs.cn: 他把这些东西好好摇匀，然后把它们放进稻草人的头顶，再用稻草把剩下的地方塞满，让它们固定住。

paragraphs.en: When he had fastened the Scarecrow’s head on his body again he said to him, “Hereafter you will be a great man, for I have given you a lot of bran-new brains.”
paragraphs.cn: 等他把稻草人的头重新装好，他对稻草人说：“从今以后，你就是个聪明人了，因为我给了你好多全新的脑子！”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow was both pleased and proud at the fulfillment of his greatest wish, and having thanked Oz warmly he went back to his friends.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人非常开心又骄傲，因为他最大的愿望实现了。他热情地感谢了奥兹大王，然后回到了朋友身边。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy looked at him curiously.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西好奇地看着他。

paragraphs.en: His head was quite bulged out at the top with brains.
paragraphs.cn: 他的头顶鼓了起来，装满了脑子。

paragraphs.en: “How do you feel?” she asked.
paragraphs.cn: “你感觉怎么样？” 她问。

paragraphs.en: “I feel wise indeed,” he answered earnestly.
paragraphs.cn: “我真的觉得自己很聪明！” 他认真地回答。

paragraphs.en: “When I get used to my brains I shall know everything.”
paragraphs.cn: “等我习惯了这些脑子，我就什么都知道了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why are those needles and pins sticking out of your head?” asked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “为什么那些大头针和缝衣针从你的头里伸出来了？” 铁皮人问。

paragraphs.en: “That is proof that he is sharp,” remarked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “那是证明他很‘尖’呢。” 狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I must go to Oz and get my heart,” said the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我得去找奥兹大王拿我的心了。” 铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: So he walked to the Throne Room and knocked at the door.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他走到王座室，敲了敲门。

paragraphs.en: “Come in,” called Oz, and the Woodman entered and said, “I have come for my heart.”
paragraphs.cn: “请进！” 奥兹大王喊道。铁皮人走了进去，说：“我来取我的心。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well,” answered the little man.
paragraphs.cn: “好的。” 小矮人回答。

paragraphs.en: “But I shall have to cut a hole in your breast, so I can put your heart in the right place.
paragraphs.cn: “不过，我得在你的胸口上开个洞，这样才能把你的心放到对的地方。”

paragraphs.en: I hope it won’t hurt you.”
paragraphs.cn: “我希望你不会疼。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no,” answered the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不会的。” 铁皮人回答。

paragraphs.en: “I shall not feel it at all.”
paragraphs.cn: “我一点都不会感觉到疼。”

paragraphs.en: So Oz brought a pair of tinsmith’s shears and cut a small, square hole in the left side of the Tin Woodman’s breast.
paragraphs.cn: 于是奥兹大王拿来一把剪铁皮的剪刀，在铁皮人胸口的左边剪了一个小小的方洞。

paragraphs.en: Then, going to a chest of drawers, he took out a pretty heart, made entirely of silk and stuffed with sawdust.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，他走到一个抽屉柜旁边，拿出一个漂亮的心脏，这个心完全是用丝绸做的，里面塞满了木屑。

paragraphs.en: “Isn’t it a beauty?” he asked.
paragraphs.cn: “它是不是很漂亮？” 他问。

paragraphs.en: “It is, indeed!” replied the Woodman, who was greatly pleased. “But is it a kind heart?”
paragraphs.cn: “确实很漂亮！” 铁皮人非常高兴地回答。“但是，它是一颗善良的心吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, very!” answered Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，非常棒！”奥兹大王回答说。

paragraphs.en: He put the heart in the Woodman’s breast and then replaced the square of tin, soldering it neatly together where it had been cut.
paragraphs.cn: 他把心放进铁皮人的胸膛里，然后把那块锡片放回去，把切开的地方仔细地焊好了。

paragraphs.en: “There,” said he; “now you have a heart that any man might be proud of.
paragraphs.cn: “好了，”他说，“你现在有一颗人人都会感到骄傲的心了。

paragraphs.en: I’m sorry I had to put a patch on your breast, but it really couldn’t be helped.”
paragraphs.cn: 对不起，我不得不在你的胸口补一块，但真的没办法。”

paragraphs.en: “Never mind the patch,” exclaimed the happy Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “补丁没关系！”快乐的铁皮人大声说。

paragraphs.en: “I am very grateful to you, and shall never forget your kindness.”
paragraphs.cn: “我非常感谢你，永远不会忘记你的好意。”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t speak of it,” replied Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “别提了。”奥兹大王回答。

paragraphs.en: Then the Tin Woodman went back to his friends, who wished him every joy on account of his good fortune.
paragraphs.cn: 然后铁皮人回到朋友们身边，朋友们都为他的好运祝贺他。

paragraphs.en: The Lion now walked to the Throne Room and knocked at the door.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子现在走到王座室，敲了敲门。

paragraphs.en: “Come in,” said Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “进来吧。”奥兹大王说。

paragraphs.en: “I have come for my courage,” announced the Lion, entering the room.
paragraphs.cn: “我来取我的勇气。”狮子走进房间，大声说。

paragraphs.en: “Very well,” answered the little man; “I will get it for you.”
paragraphs.cn: “好的，”小个子男人回答，“我去帮你拿。”

paragraphs.en: He went to a cupboard and reaching up to a high shelf took down a square green bottle, the contents of which he poured into a green-gold dish, beautifully carved.
paragraphs.cn: 他走到一个柜子前，伸手从高高的架子上拿下一个绿色的方瓶子，把里面的东西倒进一个雕刻得很漂亮的绿金色盘子里。

paragraphs.en: Placing this before the Cowardly Lion, who sniffed at it as if he did not like it, the Wizard said:
paragraphs.cn: 他把盘子放在胆小的狮子面前，胆小的狮子闻了闻，好像不喜欢，巫师说：

paragraphs.en: “Drink.”
paragraphs.cn: “喝吧。”

paragraphs.en: “What is it?” asked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “这是什么？”狮子问。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” answered Oz, “if it were inside of you, it would be courage.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，”奥兹大王回答，“如果它在你身体里，那就是勇气。

paragraphs.en: You know, of course, that courage is always inside one; so that this really cannot be called courage until you have swallowed it.
paragraphs.cn: 你知道，勇气总是在人内心深处的；所以，在你吞下它之前，这还不能叫作勇气。

paragraphs.en: Therefore I advise you to drink it as soon as possible.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以，我建议你尽快喝掉它。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion hesitated no longer, but drank till the dish was empty.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子不再犹豫，一直喝到盘子空了。

paragraphs.en: “How do you feel now?” asked Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “你现在感觉怎么样？”奥兹大王问。

paragraphs.en: “Full of courage,” replied the Lion, who went joyfully back to his friends to tell them of his good fortune.
paragraphs.cn: “充满了勇气！”狮子回答说，他开心地回到朋友们身边，告诉他们他的好运气。

paragraphs.en: Oz, left to himself, smiled to think of his success in giving the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion exactly what they thought they wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 奥兹大王独自一人，想着他成功地给了稻草人、铁皮人和狮子他们想要的东西，就笑了。

paragraphs.en: “How can I help being a humbug,” he said, “when all these people make me do things that everybody knows can’t be done?
paragraphs.cn: “我怎么能不做个骗子呢？”他说，“所有人都让我做那些大家都知道做不到的事情。”

paragraphs.en: It was easy to make the Scarecrow and the Lion and the Woodman happy, because they imagined I could do anything.
paragraphs.cn: 让稻草人、狮子和铁皮人开心很容易，因为他们都觉得我什么都能做到。

paragraphs.en: But it will take more than imagination to carry Dorothy back to Kansas, and I’m sure I don’t know how it can be done.”
paragraphs.cn: 但要把多萝西送回堪萨斯那里，光靠想象是不够的，我真不知道该怎么做。”

paragraphs.en: For three days Dorothy heard nothing from Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 三天里，多萝西没有听到奥兹大王的任何消息。

paragraphs.en: These were sad days for the little girl, although her friends were all quite happy and contented.
paragraphs.cn: 对小女孩来说，这是伤心的日子，尽管她的朋友们都很开心满足。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow told them there were wonderful thoughts in his head; but he would not say what they were because he knew no one could understand them but himself.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人告诉他们，他脑子里有很多很棒的想法；但他不说是什么，因为他知道除了自己，没人能懂。

paragraphs.en: When the Tin Woodman walked about he felt his heart rattling around in his breast; and he told Dorothy he had discovered it to be a kinder and more tender heart than the one he had owned when he was made of flesh.
paragraphs.cn: 当铁皮人走来走去时，他感觉到心在胸膛里叮当作响；他告诉多萝西，他发现这颗心比他由血肉之躯组成时拥有的那颗心更善良、更温柔。

paragraphs.en: The Lion declared he was afraid of nothing on earth, and would gladly face an army or a dozen of the fierce Kalidahs.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子说他什么都不怕，他很乐意去面对一支军队，或者十几个凶猛的卡力达。

paragraphs.en: Thus each of the little party was satisfied except Dorothy, who longed more than ever to get back to Kansas.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都挺开心的，除了多萝西，她比以前更想回到堪萨斯。

paragraphs.en: On the fourth day, to her great joy, Oz sent for her, and when she entered the Throne Room he greeted her pleasantly:
paragraphs.cn: 第四天，让奥兹大王很高兴的是，奥兹大王派人请她过去，她走进王座室时，他开心地跟她打招呼说：

paragraphs.en: “Sit down, my dear; I think I have found the way to get you out of this country.”
paragraphs.cn: “坐下吧，孩子；我想我找到办法让你离开这里了。”

paragraphs.en: “And back to Kansas?” she asked eagerly.
paragraphs.cn: “能回到堪萨斯吗？”她急切地问。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’m not sure about Kansas,” said Oz, “for I haven’t the faintest notion which way it lies.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我不太确定能不能回到堪萨斯，”奥兹大王说，“因为我完全不知道堪萨斯在哪边。

paragraphs.en: But the first thing to do is to cross the desert, and then it should be easy to find your way home.”
paragraphs.cn: 但我们首先要做的是穿过沙漠，然后你就能很容易地找到回家的路了。”

paragraphs.en: “How can I cross the desert?” she inquired.
paragraphs.cn: “我怎么才能穿过沙漠呢？”她问。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll tell you what I think,” said the little man.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我来告诉你我的想法，”小个子男人说。

paragraphs.en: “You see, when I came to this country it was in a balloon.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，我来这里的时候是坐着气球来的。

paragraphs.en: You also came through the air, being carried by a cyclone.
paragraphs.cn: 你也是从天上来的，是龙卷风把你带过来的。

paragraphs.en: So I believe the best way to get across the desert will be through the air.
paragraphs.cn: 所以我相信，穿过沙漠最好的办法就是坐着东西飞过去。

paragraphs.en: Now, it is quite beyond my powers to make a cyclone; but I’ve been thinking the matter over, and I believe I can make a balloon.”
paragraphs.cn: 我可没本事造出龙卷风。但我一直在想这件事，我觉得我能做一个气球。”

paragraphs.en: “How?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “怎么做呢？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “A balloon,” said Oz, “is made of silk, which is coated with glue to keep the gas in it.
paragraphs.cn: “气球啊，”奥兹大王说，“是用丝绸做的，丝绸上会涂一层胶水，这样气体就不会跑出来。

paragraphs.en: I have plenty of silk in the Palace, so it will be no trouble to make the balloon.
paragraphs.cn: 皇宫里有很多丝绸，所以做气球不难。

paragraphs.en: But in all this country there is no gas to fill the balloon with, to make it float.”
paragraphs.cn: 但在这个国家，没有气体可以用来填充气球，让它飘起来。”

paragraphs.en: “If it won’t float,” remarked Dorothy, “it will be of no use to us.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果它飘不起来，”多萝西说，“那对我们来说就没用了。”

paragraphs.en: “True,” answered Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “没错，”奥兹大王回答。

paragraphs.en: “But there is another way to make it float, which is to fill it with hot air.
paragraphs.cn: “但还有另一种办法让它飘起来，就是往里面灌热空气。

paragraphs.en: Hot air isn’t as good as gas, for if the air should get cold the balloon would come down in the desert, and we should be lost.”
paragraphs.cn: 热空气不如气体好，因为如果空气变冷了，气球就会掉到沙漠里，我们就会迷路了。”

paragraphs.en: “We!” exclaimed the girl. “Are you going with me?”
paragraphs.cn: “我们？”女孩惊呼，“你要跟我一起去吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, of course,” replied Oz.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，当然了，”奥兹大王回答。

paragraphs.en: “I am tired of being such a humbug.
paragraphs.cn: “我厌倦了当一个骗子。

paragraphs.en: If I should go out of this Palace my people would soon discover I am not a Wizard, and then they would be vexed with me for having deceived them.
paragraphs.cn: 如果我走出这座皇宫，我的子民很快就会发现我不是巫师，然后他们会因为我骗了他们而生我的气。

paragraphs.en: So I have to stay shut up in these rooms all day, and it gets tiresome.
paragraphs.cn: 所以我整天都得待在这些房间里，这让我很烦。

paragraphs.en: I’d much rather go back to Kansas with you and be in a circus again.”
paragraphs.cn: 我更想跟你一起回到堪萨斯，重新回到马戏团表演。”

paragraphs.en: “I shall be glad to have your company,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我很乐意有你作伴，”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “Thank you,” he answered.
paragraphs.cn: “谢谢你，”他回答。

paragraphs.en: “Now, if you will help me sew the silk together, we will begin to work on our balloon.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在，如果你能帮我把丝绸缝起来，我们就可以开始做气球了。”

paragraphs.en: So Dorothy took a needle and thread, and as fast as Oz cut the strips of silk into proper shape the girl sewed them neatly together.
paragraphs.cn: 于是 多萝西 拿起针线。奥兹大王 剪好丝绸条，女孩就把它缝起来。

paragraphs.en: First there was a strip of light green silk, then a strip of dark green and then a strip of emerald green; for Oz had a fancy to make the balloon in different shades of the color about them.
paragraphs.cn: 先是一条浅绿色的丝绸，接着是深绿色，再是翠绿色。因为 奥兹大王 想把气球做成好多不同深浅的绿色。

paragraphs.en: It took three days to sew all the strips together, but when it was finished they had a big bag of green silk more than twenty feet long.
paragraphs.cn: 他们花了三天时间，才把所有的丝绸条缝好。做好后，他们就有了一个二十多英尺长的大大的绿色丝绸袋。

paragraphs.en: Then Oz painted it on the inside with a coat of thin glue, to make it airtight, after which he announced that the balloon was ready.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，奥兹大王 在气球里面涂了一层薄薄的胶水，让它不漏气。然后他说，气球已经准备好了。

paragraphs.en: “But we must have a basket to ride in,” he said.
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“但我们得有个篮子才能坐进去。”

paragraphs.en: So he sent the soldier with the green whiskers for a big clothes basket, which he fastened with many ropes to the bottom of the balloon.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他派那个留着绿色胡子的士兵去找一个大大的洗衣篮。然后他用好多绳子把篮子牢牢地系在气球底部。

paragraphs.en: When it was all ready, Oz sent word to his people that he was going to make a visit to a great brother Wizard who lived in the clouds.
paragraphs.cn: 东西都准备好后，奥兹大王 告诉大家，他要去拜访住在云朵里的一位很厉害的巫师哥哥。

paragraphs.en: The news spread rapidly throughout the city and everyone came to see the wonderful sight.
paragraphs.cn: 这个消息很快传遍了整个城市，大家都跑来看这个奇妙的景象。

paragraphs.en: Oz ordered the balloon carried out in front of the Palace, and the people gazed upon it with much curiosity.
paragraphs.cn: 奥兹大王 让人把气球抬到皇宫前面，大家好奇地看着它。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman had chopped a big pile of wood, and now he made a fire of it, and Oz held the bottom of the balloon over the fire so that the hot air that arose from it would be caught in the silken bag.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 已经砍了一大堆木头，现在他把木头点燃，奥兹大王 把气球底部放在火上，热气就跑进了丝绸袋里。

paragraphs.en: Gradually the balloon swelled out and rose into the air, until finally the basket just touched the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 气球慢慢地鼓起来，升到了空中，最后，篮子刚好碰到地面。

paragraphs.en: Then Oz got into the basket and said to all the people in a loud voice:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，奥兹大王 坐进篮子里，大声对大家说：

paragraphs.en: “I am now going away to make a visit.
paragraphs.cn: “我现在要走了，去拜访朋友。

paragraphs.en: While I am gone the Scarecrow will rule over you.
paragraphs.cn: 我不在的时候，稻草人 会管理你们。”

paragraphs.en: I command you to obey him as you would me.”
paragraphs.cn: 我命令你们要像听我的话一样，听他的话。”

paragraphs.en: The balloon was by this time tugging hard at the rope that held it to the ground, for the air within it was hot, and this made it so much lighter in weight than the air without that it pulled hard to rise into the sky.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，气球用力拉着绳子，因为它里面是热空气，比外面轻，很想飞上天。

paragraphs.en: “Come, Dorothy!” cried the Wizard. “Hurry up, or the balloon will fly away.”
paragraphs.cn: 巫师喊道：“快来，多萝西！快点，不然气球要飞走了！”

paragraphs.en: “I can’t find Toto anywhere,” replied Dorothy, who did not wish to leave her little dog behind.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 回答说：“我找不到 托托。”她不想把自己的小狗丢下。

paragraphs.en: Toto had run into the crowd to bark at a kitten, and Dorothy at last found him.
paragraphs.cn: 托托 跑进人群里冲着一只小猫叫，多萝西 终于找到了它。

paragraphs.en: She picked him up and ran towards the balloon.
paragraphs.cn: 她抱起它，跑向气球。

paragraphs.en: She was within a few steps of it, and Oz was holding out his hands to help her into the basket, when, crack! went the ropes, and the balloon rose into the air without her.
paragraphs.cn: 她离气球只有几步远了，奥兹大王 伸出手想帮她进篮子。就在这时，绳子“啪”地断了，气球没有她就飞走了。

paragraphs.en: “Come back!” she screamed. “I want to go, too!”
paragraphs.cn: 她大叫：“回来！我也要去！”

paragraphs.en: “I can’t come back, my dear,” called Oz from the basket.
paragraphs.cn: 奥兹大王 从篮子里喊道：“我回不来了，亲爱的。”

paragraphs.en: “Good-bye!”
paragraphs.cn: “再见！”

paragraphs.en: “Good-bye!” shouted everyone, and all eyes were turned upward to where the Wizard was riding in the basket, rising every moment farther and farther into the sky.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都喊着：“再见！”所有人的眼睛都看着天上。巫师坐在篮子里，每时每刻都飞得更高更远。

paragraphs.en: And that was the last any of them ever saw of Oz, the Wonderful Wizard, though he may have reached Omaha safely, and be there now, for all we know.
paragraphs.cn: 这是大家最后一次见到奇妙的巫师 奥兹大王 了。没人知道他是不是安全到了奥马哈，现在是不是还在那儿。

paragraphs.en: But the people remembered him lovingly, and said to one another:
paragraphs.cn: 但大家都很爱他，常常想起他。他们互相说：

paragraphs.en: “Oz was always our friend.
paragraphs.cn: “奥兹大王 永远是我们的朋友。

paragraphs.en: When he was here he built for us this beautiful Emerald City, and now he is gone he has left the Wise Scarecrow to rule over us.”
paragraphs.cn: 他在这里时，给我们建了这座漂亮的 翡翠城。现在他走了，留下了聪明的 稻草人 来管理我们。”

paragraphs.en: Still, for many days they grieved over the loss of the Wonderful Wizard, and would not be comforted.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，好多天里，大家还是很伤心，因为奇妙的巫师不见了。谁也哄不好他们。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy wept bitterly at the passing of her hope to get home to Kansas again; but when she thought it all over she was glad she had not gone up in a balloon.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 很难过，因为她不能回家看 堪萨斯 了。但她想了想，又觉得没坐气球是对的。

paragraphs.en: And she also felt sorry at losing Oz, and so did her companions.
paragraphs.cn: 她很难过，因为 奥兹大王 不见了。她的朋友们也一样难过。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman came to her and said:
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 走到她身边，对她说：

paragraphs.en: “Truly I should be ungrateful if I failed to mourn for the man who gave me my lovely heart.
paragraphs.cn: “要是我不为那个给我小心心的人难过，那我可就太不好了。

paragraphs.en: I should like to cry a little because Oz is gone, if you will kindly wipe away my tears, so that I shall not rust.”
paragraphs.cn: 奥兹大王 走了，我想哭一哭。请你帮我擦掉眼泪，这样我就不会生锈了。”

paragraphs.en: “With pleasure,” she answered, and brought a towel at once.
paragraphs.cn: “好的！”她说着，马上拿来一条毛巾。

paragraphs.en: Then the Tin Woodman wept for several minutes, and she watched the tears carefully and wiped them away with the towel.
paragraphs.cn: 然后 铁皮人 哭了很久，她小心地擦掉它的眼泪。

paragraphs.en: When he had finished, he thanked her kindly and oiled himself thoroughly with his jeweled oil-can, to guard against mishap.
paragraphs.cn: 他哭完后，谢谢她。然后用他的油壶给自己全身都抹了油，这样他就不会出问题了。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow was now the ruler of the Emerald City, and although he was not a Wizard the people were proud of him.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 现在是 翡翠城 的首领了。虽然他不是巫师，但大家都为他骄傲。

paragraphs.en: “For,” they said, “there is not another city in all the world that is ruled by a stuffed man.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们说：“因为，全世界没有哪个城市像我们这样，是由一个‘稻草人’来管的。”

paragraphs.en: And, so far as they knew, they were quite right.
paragraphs.cn: 他们知道的，就是这样。他们说得很对。

paragraphs.en: The morning after the balloon had gone up with Oz, the four travelers met in the Throne Room and talked matters over.
paragraphs.cn: 气球带着 奥兹大王 飞走后，第二天早上，四个好朋友在王宫里见面，一起商量事情。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow sat in the big throne and the others stood respectfully before him.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 坐在大大的王座上，其他人乖乖地站在他面前。

paragraphs.en: “We are not so unlucky,” said the new ruler, “for this Palace and the Emerald City belong to us, and we can do just as we please.
paragraphs.cn: 新首领说：“我们没有那么倒霉。因为这座王宫和 翡翠城 都是我们的了，我们可以想做什么就做什么。

paragraphs.en: When I remember that a short time ago I was up on a pole in a farmer’s cornfield, and that now I am the ruler of this beautiful City, I am quite satisfied with my lot.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想到不久前，我还在农夫的玉米地里被插在杆子上。现在我是这个漂亮城市的首领了，我对自己现在的生活很满意。”

paragraphs.en: “I also,” said the Tin Woodman, “am well-pleased with my new heart; and, really, that was the only thing I wished in all the world.”
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 说：“我也很喜欢我的新心。真的，这是我最想要的东西了。”

paragraphs.en: “For my part, I am content in knowing I am as brave as any beast that ever lived, if not braver,” said the Lion modestly.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子 害羞地说：“我觉得自己很开心，因为我知道我比任何小动物都勇敢，可能还更勇敢！”

paragraphs.en: “If Dorothy would only be contented to live in the Emerald City,” continued the Scarecrow, “we might all be happy together.”
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 说：“要是 多萝西 愿意住在 翡翠城 里，我们大家就可以一直开开心心地在一起了。”

paragraphs.en: “But I don’t want to live here,” cried Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 大声说：“我才不想住在这里呢！”

paragraphs.en: “I want to go to Kansas, and live with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry.”
paragraphs.cn: “我想去 堪萨斯，和 艾姆婶婶、亨利叔叔 住在一起。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, then, what can be done?” inquired the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: 铁皮人 问：“那我们能做什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow decided to think, and he thought so hard that the pins and needles began to stick out of his brains.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 决定好好想想。他想得太认真了，脑袋里都快冒出钉子和针了。

paragraphs.en: Finally he said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Why not call the Winged Monkeys, and ask them to carry you over the desert?”
paragraphs.cn: “为什么不叫 飞猴，让他们把你带过沙漠呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I never thought of that!” said Dorothy joyfully.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西 开心地说：“我从来没想过这个办法！”

paragraphs.en: “It’s just the thing.
paragraphs.cn: “就是这样！

paragraphs.en: I’ll go at once for the Golden Cap.”
paragraphs.cn: 我马上就去叫 金冠。”

paragraphs.en: When she brought it into the Throne Room she spoke the magic words, and soon the band of Winged Monkeys flew in through the open window and stood beside her.
paragraphs.cn: 她把 飞猴 带到王宫里，念了咒语。很快，一群 飞猴 就从开着的窗户飞了进来，停在她身边。

paragraphs.en: “This is the second time you have called us,” said the Monkey King, bowing before the little girl.
paragraphs.cn: 猴王对小女孩弯腰说：“这是你第二次叫我们了。”

paragraphs.en: “What do you wish?”
paragraphs.cn: “你想要什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I want you to fly with me to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我想让你和我一起飞到堪萨斯去。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: But the Monkey King shook his head.
paragraphs.cn: 但猴王摇了摇头。

paragraphs.en: “That cannot be done,” he said.
paragraphs.cn: “那可不行。”他说。

paragraphs.en: “We belong to this country alone, and cannot leave it.
paragraphs.cn: “我们只属于这个国家，不能离开。

paragraphs.en: There has never been a Winged Monkey in Kansas yet, and I suppose there never will be, for they don’t belong there.
paragraphs.cn: 在堪萨斯从来没有飞猴，我想以后也不会有，因为他们不属于那里。

paragraphs.en: We shall be glad to serve you in any way in our power, but we cannot cross the desert.
paragraphs.cn: 我们很乐意尽力帮你，但我们不能穿过沙漠。

paragraphs.en: Good-bye.”
paragraphs.cn: 再见。”

paragraphs.en: And with another bow, the Monkey King spread his wings and flew away through the window, followed by all his band.
paragraphs.cn: 猴王又鞠了一躬，张开翅膀，带着他的伙伴们飞出了窗外。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was ready to cry with disappointment.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西很失望，都快哭了。

paragraphs.en: “I have wasted the charm of the Golden Cap to no purpose,” she said, “for the Winged Monkeys cannot help me.”
paragraphs.cn: “我白白浪费了金冠的魔法。”她说，“因为飞猴帮不了我。”

paragraphs.en: “It is certainly too bad!” said the tender-hearted Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “这真是太糟糕了！”善良的铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow was thinking again, and his head bulged out so horribly that Dorothy feared it would burst.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人又开始想办法了，他的头鼓得特别大，多萝西担心它会爆炸。

paragraphs.en: “Let us call in the soldier with the green whiskers,” he said, “and ask his advice.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们把留着绿胡子的士兵叫进来吧。”他说，“问问他的意见。”

paragraphs.en: So the soldier was summoned and entered the Throne Room timidly, for while Oz was alive he never was allowed to come farther than the door.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，士兵被叫来了，他小心翼翼地走进王座室，因为在奥兹大王活着的时候，他从来不被允许走到门里面。

paragraphs.en: “This little girl,” said the Scarecrow to the soldier, “wishes to cross the desert.
paragraphs.cn: “这个小女孩。”稻草人对士兵说，“想穿过沙漠。

paragraphs.en: How can she do so?”
paragraphs.cn: 她怎么才能过去呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I cannot tell,” answered the soldier, “for nobody has ever crossed the desert, unless it is Oz himself.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。”士兵回答说，“因为除了奥兹大王自己，从没有人穿过沙漠。”

paragraphs.en: “Is there no one who can help me?” asked Dorothy earnestly.
paragraphs.cn: “没有人能帮我吗？”多萝西认真地问。

paragraphs.en: “Glinda might,” he suggested.
paragraphs.cn: “也许格林达可以。”他提议说。

paragraphs.en: “Who is Glinda?” inquired the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “格林达是谁？”稻草人问。

paragraphs.en: “The Witch of the South.
paragraphs.cn: “南方的女巫。

paragraphs.en: She is the most powerful of all the Witches, and rules over the Quadlings.
paragraphs.cn: 她是所有女巫里最厉害的，统治着奎德林人。

paragraphs.en: Besides, her castle stands on the edge of the desert, so she may know a way to cross it.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，她的城堡就在沙漠旁边，所以她也许知道怎么穿过沙漠。”

paragraphs.en: “Glinda is a Good Witch, isn’t she?” asked the child.
paragraphs.cn: “格林达是个好女巫，对吗？”孩子问。

paragraphs.en: “The Quadlings think she is good,” said the soldier, “and she is kind to everyone.
paragraphs.cn: “奎德林人觉得她是个好人。”士兵说，“她对每个人都很好。

paragraphs.en: I have heard that Glinda is a beautiful woman, who knows how to keep young in spite of the many years she has lived.”
paragraphs.cn: 我听说格林达是个漂亮的女人，她活了很多年，却知道怎么让自己一直年轻。”

paragraphs.en: “How can I get to her castle?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我怎么才能到她的城堡呢？”多萝西问。

paragraphs.en: “The road is straight to the South,” he answered, “but it is said to be full of dangers to travelers.
paragraphs.cn: “那条路一直往南走。”他回答说，“但听说那里对走路的人来说很危险。

paragraphs.en: There are wild beasts in the woods, and a race of queer men who do not like strangers to cross their country.
paragraphs.cn: 森林里有野兽，还有一群奇怪的人，他们不喜欢陌生人穿过他们的地盘。

paragraphs.en: For this reason none of the Quadlings ever come to the Emerald City.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以，从来没有奎德林人来过翡翠城。”

paragraphs.en: The soldier then left them and the Scarecrow said:
paragraphs.cn: 士兵离开了他们，然后 稻草人 说：

paragraphs.en: “It seems, in spite of dangers, that the best thing Dorothy can do is to travel to the Land of the South and ask Glinda to help her.
paragraphs.cn: “看来，虽然有危险，但 多萝西 最好还是去南方之地，请 格林达 帮忙。

paragraphs.en: For, of course, if Dorothy stays here she will never get back to Kansas.”
paragraphs.cn: 因为呀，如果 多萝西 留在这里，她就永远回不到 堪萨斯 那里了。”

paragraphs.en: “You must have been thinking again,” remarked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “你一定又在想事情了。” 铁皮人 说。

paragraphs.en: “I have,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “是的。” 稻草人 说。

paragraphs.en: “I shall go with Dorothy,” declared the Lion, “for I am tired of your city and long for the woods and the country again.
paragraphs.cn: “我要和 多萝西 一起去。” 狮子 说，“因为我厌倦了你们的城市，我又想念森林和乡村了。

paragraphs.en: I am really a wild beast, you know.
paragraphs.cn: 我其实是一只野兽，你知道的。

paragraphs.en: Besides, Dorothy will need someone to protect her.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，多萝西 也需要有人保护她。”

paragraphs.en: “That is true,” agreed the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “没错。” 铁皮人 同意。

paragraphs.en: “My axe may be of service to her; so I also will go with her to the Land of the South.”
paragraphs.cn: “我的斧头也许能帮到她；所以我也要和她一起去南方之地。”

paragraphs.en: “When shall we start?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我们什么时候出发呢？” 稻草人 问。

paragraphs.en: “Are you going?” they asked, in surprise.
paragraphs.cn: “你要去吗？” 他们惊讶地问。

paragraphs.en: “Certainly.
paragraphs.cn: “当然去。

paragraphs.en: If it wasn’t for Dorothy I should never have had brains.
paragraphs.cn: 要不是 多萝西，我就永远不会有脑子了。

paragraphs.en: She lifted me from the pole in the cornfield and brought me to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 她把我从玉米地里的杆子上拿下来，还把我带到了 翡翠城 那里。

paragraphs.en: So my good luck is all due to her, and I shall never leave her until she starts back to Kansas for good and all.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以我的好运气都是因为她，我永远不会离开她，直到她彻底回到 堪萨斯 那里。”

paragraphs.en: “Thank you,” said Dorothy gratefully.
paragraphs.cn: “谢谢你。” 多萝西 充满感激地说。

paragraphs.en: “You are all very kind to me.
paragraphs.cn: “你们都对我很好。

paragraphs.en: But I should like to start as soon as possible.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过，我希望能尽快出发。”

paragraphs.en: “We shall go tomorrow morning,” returned the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “我们明天早上就走。” 稻草人 回答。

paragraphs.en: “So now let us all get ready, for it will be a long journey.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在大家准备一下吧，这将是一段很长的旅程。”

paragraphs.en: The next morning Dorothy kissed the pretty green girl good-bye, and they all shook hands with the soldier with the green whiskers, who had walked with them as far as the gate.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，多萝西 亲了亲漂亮的绿衣女孩，和那个留着绿色胡子的士兵一一握手道别。士兵一直送他们到了大门口。

paragraphs.en: When the Guardian of the Gate saw them again he wondered greatly that they could leave the beautiful City to get into new trouble.
paragraphs.cn: 当 城门守卫 再次见到他们时，他很奇怪他们竟然会离开这座美丽的城市，去惹新的麻烦。

paragraphs.en: But he at once unlocked their spectacles, which he put back into the green box, and gave them many good wishes to carry with them.
paragraphs.cn: 但他立刻打开了他们的眼镜，放回绿盒子里，并祝愿他们一切顺利。

paragraphs.en: “You are now our ruler,” he said to the Scarecrow; “so you must come back to us as soon as possible.”
paragraphs.cn: “你现在是我们的统治者了。” 他对 稻草人 说，“所以你必须尽快回来。”

paragraphs.en: “I certainly shall if I am able,” the Scarecrow replied; “but I must help Dorothy to get home, first.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果我能的话，我当然会回来。” 稻草人 回答，“但首先，我必须帮助 多萝西 回家。”

paragraphs.en: As Dorothy bade the good-natured Guardian a last farewell she said:
paragraphs.cn: 当 多萝西 和那位好心的守护者最后告别时，她说：

paragraphs.en: “I have been very kindly treated in your lovely City, and everyone has been good to me.
paragraphs.cn: “在这美丽的城市里，我受到了很好的对待，每个人都对我很好。

paragraphs.en: I cannot tell you how grateful I am.”
paragraphs.cn: 我无法表达我有多么感激。”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t try, my dear,” he answered.
paragraphs.cn: “别说了，我的孩子。” 他回答。

paragraphs.en: “We should like to keep you with us, but if it is your wish to return to Kansas, I hope you will find a way.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们想让你跟我们在一起，但如果你想回 堪萨斯，我希望你能找到回去的路。

paragraphs.en: He then opened the gate of the outer wall, and they walked forth and started upon their journey.
paragraphs.cn: 他打开了外面的大门，他们就走了出去，开始赶路了。

paragraphs.en: The sun shone brightly as our friends turned their faces toward the Land of the South.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳亮亮地照着，朋友们朝南边的土地走去。

paragraphs.en: They were all in the best of spirits, and laughed and chatted together.
paragraphs.cn: 他们都非常高兴，又说又笑。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was once more filled with the hope of getting home, and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were glad to be of use to her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西又有了回家的希望，稻草人和铁皮人也很高兴能帮到她。

paragraphs.en: As for the Lion, he sniffed the fresh air with delight and whisked his tail from side to side in pure joy at being in the country again, while Toto ran around them and chased the moths and butterflies, barking merrily all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子开心地闻着新鲜空气，高兴地摇着尾巴，因为它又回到了乡下。托托在他们身边跑，追着飞蛾和蝴蝶，一直开心地叫。

paragraphs.en: “City life does not agree with me at all,” remarked the Lion, as they walked along at a brisk pace.
paragraphs.cn: “城市生活一点都不适合我，”狮子一边快步走着，一边说。

paragraphs.en: “I have lost much flesh since I lived there, and now I am anxious for a chance to show the other beasts how courageous I have grown.”
paragraphs.cn: “我住在那里瘦了很多，现在我希望能有机会让别的动物看看我有多勇敢。”

paragraphs.en: They now turned and took a last look at the Emerald City.
paragraphs.cn: 他们转过身，最后看了一眼翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: All they could see was a mass of towers and steeples behind the green walls, and high up above everything the spires and dome of the Palace of Oz.
paragraphs.cn: 他们看到绿色的城墙后面有很多高塔和尖顶，所有东西上面是奥兹大王宫殿的尖塔和圆顶。

paragraphs.en: “Oz was not such a bad Wizard, after all,” said the Tin Woodman, as he felt his heart rattling around in his breast.
paragraphs.cn: “奥兹大王其实也不是个坏巫师嘛，”铁皮人摸着自己砰砰跳的心脏说。

paragraphs.en: “He knew how to give me brains, and very good brains, too,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “他知道怎么给我智慧，而且是很好的智慧，”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “If Oz had taken a dose of the same courage he gave me,” added the Lion, “he would have been a brave man.”
paragraphs.cn: “要是奥兹大王也吃了点他给我的那种勇气，”狮子补充说，“他也会是个勇敢的人。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy said nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西什么也没说。

paragraphs.en: Oz had not kept the promise he made her, but he had done his best, so she forgave him.
paragraphs.cn: 奥兹大王没有遵守对她做的承诺，但他已经尽力了，所以她原谅了他。

paragraphs.en: As he said, he was a good man, even if he was a bad Wizard.
paragraphs.cn: 就像他说的那样，他是个好人，即使他是个坏巫师。

paragraphs.en: The first day’s journey was through the green fields and bright flowers that stretched about the Emerald City on every side.
paragraphs.cn: 第一天的路程，他们穿过了翡翠城四周绿绿的田野和开满鲜花的草地。

paragraphs.en: They slept that night on the grass, with nothing but the stars over them; and they rested very well indeed.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上他们睡在草地上，头顶上只有星星；他们睡得很好。

paragraphs.en: In the morning they traveled on until they came to a thick wood.
paragraphs.cn: 早上他们继续赶路，直到来到一片茂密的树林。

paragraphs.en: There was no way of going around it, for it seemed to extend to the right and left as far as they could see; and, besides, they did not dare change the direction of their journey for fear of getting lost.
paragraphs.cn: 他们没法绕过去，因为树林好像一直向左右延伸，看不到尽头；而且，他们也不敢改变方向，怕迷路。

paragraphs.en: So they looked for the place where it would be easiest to get into the forest.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他们找了一个最容易走进森林的地方。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow, who was in the lead, finally discovered a big tree with such wide-spreading branches that there was room for the party to pass underneath.
paragraphs.cn: 走在前面的稻草人，终于发现了一棵大树，它的树枝伸得很开，大家可以从下面过去。

paragraphs.en: So he walked forward to the tree, but just as he came under the first branches they bent down and twined around him, and the next minute he was raised from the ground and flung headlong among his fellow travelers.
paragraphs.cn: 他走过去，刚到第一根树枝下面，树枝就弯下来缠住了他。接着，他被从地上提起来，头朝下地扔到了同伴们中间。

paragraphs.en: This did not hurt the Scarecrow, but it surprised him, and he looked rather dizzy when Dorothy picked him up.
paragraphs.cn: 这没有伤到稻草人，但让他很吃惊。当多萝西把他捡起来时，他看起来有点头晕。

paragraphs.en: “Here is another space between the trees,” called the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “这里树中间还有个空隙！”狮子喊道。

paragraphs.en: “Let me try it first,” said the Scarecrow, “for it doesn’t hurt me to get thrown about.”
paragraphs.cn: “让我先试试吧，”稻草人说，“因为我被扔来扔去也不会疼。”

paragraphs.en: He walked up to another tree, as he spoke, but its branches immediately seized him and tossed him back again.
paragraphs.cn: 他一边说，一边走到另一棵树旁，可树枝立刻抓住他，又把他扔了回来。

paragraphs.en: “This is strange,” exclaimed Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “这真奇怪！”多萝西大声说。

paragraphs.en: “What shall we do?”
paragraphs.cn: “我们该怎么办呢？”

paragraphs.en: “The trees seem to have made up their minds to fight us, and stop our journey,” remarked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “这些树好像决定要和我们打架，不让我们走了，”狮子说。

paragraphs.en: “I believe I will try it myself,” said the Woodman, and shouldering his axe, he marched up to the first tree that had handled the Scarecrow so roughly.
paragraphs.cn: “我想我自己来试试。” 铁皮人说，他扛起斧头，走到第一棵树前，这棵树刚才对 稻草人 太不客气了。

paragraphs.en: When a big branch bent down to seize him the Woodman chopped at it so fiercely that he cut it in two.
paragraphs.cn: 当一根大树枝弯下来抓他时，铁皮人使劲一砍，就把树枝砍成了两半。

paragraphs.en: At once the tree began shaking all its branches as if in pain, and the Tin Woodman passed safely under it.
paragraphs.cn: 树立刻痛苦地摇晃着所有的树枝，铁皮人安全地从树下走过去了。

paragraphs.en: “Come on!” he shouted to the others. “Be quick!”
paragraphs.cn: “快走！”他大声对其他人喊道，“快点！”

paragraphs.en: They all ran forward and passed under the tree without injury, except Toto, who was caught by a small branch and shaken until he howled.
paragraphs.cn: 他们都跑过去，安全地从树下过去了，除了 托托。他被一根小树枝缠住，一直摇晃他，直到他大叫起来。

paragraphs.en: But the Woodman promptly chopped off the branch and set the little dog free.
paragraphs.cn: 但 铁皮人 立刻砍断了树枝，让小狗自由了。

paragraphs.en: The other trees of the forest did nothing to keep them back, so they made up their minds that only the first row of trees could bend down their branches, and that probably these were the policemen of the forest, and given this wonderful power in order to keep strangers out of it.
paragraphs.cn: 森林里其他的树没有拦住他们。大家就想，可能只有第一排的树才会弯下树枝吧。它们也许是森林里的警察，有了这种厉害的能力，就能不让陌生人进来。

paragraphs.en: The four travelers walked with ease through the trees until they came to the farther edge of the wood.
paragraphs.cn: 四个旅行者轻松地穿过树林，一直走到森林的另一边。

paragraphs.en: Then, to their surprise, they found before them a high wall which seemed to be made of white china.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，让他们很惊讶的是，他们面前有一堵高高的墙，看起来像是用白色的瓷做的。

paragraphs.en: It was smooth, like the surface of a dish, and higher than their heads.
paragraphs.cn: 它很光滑，就像盘子的表面一样，比他们的头还要高。

paragraphs.en: “What shall we do now?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我们现在该怎么办呢？” 多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: “I will make a ladder,” said the Tin Woodman, “for we certainly must climb over the wall.”
paragraphs.cn: “我来做一个梯子。” 铁皮人说，“我们肯定要爬过这堵墙。”

paragraphs.en: While the Woodman was making a ladder from wood which he found in the forest Dorothy lay down and slept, for she was tired by the long walk.
paragraphs.cn: 当 铁皮人 用他在森林里找到的木头做梯子时，多萝西 躺下来睡着了，因为走了很长的路，她累了。

paragraphs.en: The Lion also curled himself up to sleep and Toto lay beside him.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子 也蜷缩起来睡觉，托托 躺在他旁边。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow watched the Woodman while he worked, and said to him:
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 看着 铁皮人 工作，然后对他说：

paragraphs.en: “I cannot think why this wall is here, nor what it is made of.”
paragraphs.cn: “我搞不懂这堵墙为什么会在这里，也不知道它是用什么做的。”

paragraphs.en: “Rest your brains and do not worry about the wall,” replied the Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “别费脑筋了，也别担心这堵墙。” 铁皮人 回答说。

paragraphs.en: “When we have climbed over it, we shall know what is on the other side.”
paragraphs.cn: “等我们爬过去，就知道墙后面是什么了。”

paragraphs.en: After a time the ladder was finished.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，梯子做好了。

paragraphs.en: It looked clumsy, but the Tin Woodman was sure it was strong and would answer their purpose.
paragraphs.cn: 它看起来有点笨重，但 铁皮人 确定它很结实，能帮上他们的忙。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow waked Dorothy and the Lion and Toto, and told them that the ladder was ready.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 叫醒了 多萝西 和 狮子 和 托托，告诉他们梯子已经准备好了。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow climbed up the ladder first, but he was so awkward that Dorothy had to follow close behind and keep him from falling off.
paragraphs.cn: 稻草人 第一个爬上梯子，但他太笨拙了，所以 多萝西 必须紧跟在他后面，不让他摔下来。

paragraphs.en: When he got his head over the top of the wall the Scarecrow said, “Oh, my!”
paragraphs.cn: 当他的头探过墙顶时，稻草人 说：“噢，天哪！”

paragraphs.en: “Go on,” exclaimed Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “快点！” 多萝西 大声说。

paragraphs.en: So the Scarecrow climbed farther up and sat down on the top of the wall, and Dorothy put her head over and cried, “Oh, my!” just as the Scarecrow had done.
paragraphs.cn: 于是 稻草人 又往上爬了一点，坐在了墙顶上，多萝西 也把头探过去，大叫一声：“噢，天哪！” 就像 稻草人 刚才那样。

paragraphs.en: Then Toto came up, and immediately began to bark, but Dorothy made him be still.
paragraphs.cn: 接着 托托 也爬上来了，立刻就开始叫，但 多萝西 让他安静下来。

paragraphs.en: The Lion climbed the ladder next, and the Tin Woodman came last; but both of them cried, “Oh, my!” as soon as they looked over the wall.
paragraphs.cn: 接着 狮子 爬上梯子，铁皮人 最后一个上来；可他们俩刚把头探过墙，就都大叫：“噢，天哪！”

paragraphs.en: When they were all sitting in a row on the top of the wall, they looked down and saw a strange sight.
paragraphs.cn: 当他们都一排排地坐在墙顶上时，他们往下看，看到了一幅奇怪的景象。

paragraphs.en: Before them was a great stretch of country having a floor as smooth and shining and white as the bottom of a big platter.
paragraphs.cn: 在他们面前是一大片地方，地面又光滑又亮，白得像一个大盘子的底面。

paragraphs.en: Scattered around were many houses made entirely of china and painted in the brightest colors.
paragraphs.cn: 四周散落着许多房子，它们完全是用瓷做的，漆成了最鲜艳的颜色。

paragraphs.en: These houses were quite small, the biggest of them reaching only as high as Dorothy’s waist.
paragraphs.cn: 这些房子都很小，最大的也只到多萝西的腰那么高。

paragraphs.en: There were also pretty little barns, with china fences around them; and many cows and sheep and horses and pigs and chickens, all made of china, were standing about in groups.
paragraphs.cn: 还有很多漂亮的小谷仓，周围有瓷器做的围栏；许多瓷器做的小牛、小羊、小马、小猪和小鸡，都成群地站在那里。

paragraphs.en: But the strangest of all were the people who lived in this queer country.
paragraphs.cn: 但最奇怪的是，住在这个奇怪国家里的人们。

paragraphs.en: There were milkmaids and shepherdesses, with brightly colored bodices and golden spots all over their gowns; and princesses with most gorgeous frocks of silver and gold and purple; and shepherds dressed in knee breeches with pink and yellow and blue stripes down them, and golden buckles on their shoes; and princes with jeweled crowns upon their heads, wearing ermine robes and satin doublets; and funny clowns in ruffled gowns, with round red spots upon their cheeks and tall, pointed caps.
paragraphs.cn: 有挤奶的婶婶和放羊的姐姐，她们穿的衣服很亮，裙子上还有金色的点点。有公主，穿着闪闪发光的银色、金色和紫色的裙子。牧羊人穿着有粉色、黄色、蓝色条纹的裤子，鞋子上有金色的扣子。王子头上戴着漂亮的宝石王冠，穿着软软的皮草衣服。还有好玩的小丑，穿着皱巴巴的衣服，脸上画着红点，戴着高高的尖帽子。

paragraphs.en: And, strangest of all, these people were all made of china, even to their clothes, and were so small that the tallest of them was no higher than Dorothy’s knee.
paragraphs.cn: 而最奇怪的是，这些人全都是瓷器做的，连衣服也是！他们太小了，最高的人也只到多萝西的膝盖。

paragraphs.en: No one did so much as look at the travelers at first, except one little purple china dog with an extra-large head, which came to the wall and barked at them in a tiny voice, afterwards running away again.
paragraphs.cn: 一开始，没有人理会这些旅行者。只有一只紫色的小瓷狗，它有一个大大的头，走到墙边，冲他们轻轻地叫了几声，然后又跑开了。

paragraphs.en: “How shall we get down?” asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我们怎么下去呢？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: They found the ladder so heavy they could not pull it up, so the Scarecrow fell off the wall and the others jumped down upon him so that the hard floor would not hurt their feet.
paragraphs.cn: 他们发现梯子太重了，拉不上去。所以稻草人从墙上跳了下来，其他人也跳到他身上，这样硬硬的地板就不会伤到他们的脚了。

paragraphs.en: Of course they took pains not to light on his head and get the pins in their feet.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，他们很小心，没有跳到他的头上，也没有让钉子扎到脚。

paragraphs.en: When all were safely down they picked up the Scarecrow, whose body was quite flattened out, and patted his straw into shape again.
paragraphs.cn: 当他们都安全下来后，他们抱起稻草人，他的身体都扁扁的了，然后拍了拍，让他的稻草又变回原来的样子。

paragraphs.en: “We must cross this strange place in order to get to the other side,” said Dorothy, “for it would be unwise for us to go any other way except due South.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们必须穿过这个奇怪的地方才能到对面，”多萝西说，“因为如果我们不一直往南走，那就不太好。”

paragraphs.en: They began walking through the country of the china people, and the first thing they came to was a china milkmaid milking a china cow.
paragraphs.cn: 他们开始走过这个瓷器人的国家。他们遇到的第一个景象是一个瓷器挤奶姑娘正在挤一头瓷器奶牛的奶。

paragraphs.en: As they drew near, the cow suddenly gave a kick and kicked over the stool, the pail, and even the milkmaid herself, and all fell on the china ground with a great clatter.
paragraphs.cn: 当他们走近时，那头奶牛突然踢了一下，踢翻了凳子、桶，甚至连挤奶姑娘也踢倒了！所有东西都“哗啦”一声掉在了瓷器做的地上。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was shocked to see that the cow had broken her leg off, and that the pail was lying in several small pieces, while the poor milkmaid had a nick in her left elbow.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西很惊讶地看到，奶牛的一条腿断了，桶也碎成了好几块。可怜的挤奶姑娘左手肘也裂了一个小口子。

paragraphs.en: “There!” cried the milkmaid angrily.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！”挤奶姑娘生气地叫道。

paragraphs.en: “See what you have done!
paragraphs.cn: “看看你们做了什么好事！”

paragraphs.en: My cow has broken her leg, and I must take her to the mender’s shop and have it glued on again.
paragraphs.cn: 我的奶牛腿断了，我得带她去修理店，把腿再粘好。

paragraphs.en: What do you mean by coming here and frightening my cow?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们来这里吓我的奶牛，是什么意思呀？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m very sorry,” returned Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “对不起，”多萝西回答道。

paragraphs.en: “Please forgive us.”
paragraphs.cn: “请原谅我们。”

paragraphs.en: But the pretty milkmaid was much too vexed to make any answer.
paragraphs.cn: 但漂亮的挤奶姑娘太生气了，生气得都没法回答。

paragraphs.en: She picked up the leg sulkily and led her cow away, the poor animal limping on three legs.
paragraphs.cn: 她不高兴地捡起那条断腿，然后牵着奶牛走了，那可怜的奶牛只能用三条腿走路，一瘸一拐的。

paragraphs.en: As she left them the milkmaid cast many reproachful glances over her shoulder at the clumsy strangers, holding her nicked elbow close to her side.
paragraphs.cn: 她走的时候，挤奶姑娘回头瞪了好几眼这些笨手笨脚的陌生人，她还紧紧地捂着自己裂口的胳膊肘。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was quite grieved at this mishap.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西看到这场意外，心里很难过。

paragraphs.en: “We must be very careful here,” said the kind-hearted Woodman, “or we may hurt these pretty little people so they will never get over it.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们在这里可要非常小心啊，”善良的铁皮人说，“不然我们可能会弄伤这些漂亮的小人儿，他们就再也好不了了。”

paragraphs.en: A little farther on Dorothy met a most beautifully dressed young Princess, who stopped short as she saw the strangers and started to run away.
paragraphs.cn: 再往前走一点，多萝西遇到了一位穿着非常漂亮的年轻公主。公主一看到陌生人就停住了，然后想跑开。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy wanted to see more of the Princess, so she ran after her.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西想多看看这位公主，所以她就追了上去。

paragraphs.en: But the china girl cried out:
paragraphs.cn: 但那个瓷器小女孩大声喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Don’t chase me!
paragraphs.cn: “别追我！

paragraphs.en: Don’t chase me!”
paragraphs.cn: 别追我！”

paragraphs.en: She had such a frightened little voice that Dorothy stopped and said, “Why not?”
paragraphs.cn: 她的声音吓得有些发抖，多萝西停下来问：“为什么不跑呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Because,” answered the Princess, also stopping, a safe distance away, “if I run I may fall down and break myself.”
paragraphs.cn: “因为呀，”公主也停了下来，站得远远的，说，“如果我跑，可能会摔倒，把自己摔碎的。”

paragraphs.en: “But could you not be mended?” asked the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “可是，你不能修好吗？”小女孩问。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, yes; but one is never so pretty after being mended, you know,” replied the Princess.
paragraphs.cn: “噢，可以呀；但修好以后就没那么漂亮了，你知道的。”公主回答。

paragraphs.en: “I suppose not,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “我想也是吧。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “Now there is Mr. Joker, one of our clowns,” continued the china lady, “who is always trying to stand upon his head.
paragraphs.cn: “看，那位小丑先生，”瓷器女士继续说，“他是我们这里的小丑，老是喜欢倒立。

paragraphs.en: He has broken himself so often that he is mended in a hundred places, and doesn’t look at all pretty.
paragraphs.cn: 他摔碎过好多次了，修了有一百个地方，一点也不漂亮了。

paragraphs.en: Here he comes now, so you can see for yourself.”
paragraphs.cn: 他现在过来了，你可以自己看看。”

paragraphs.en: Indeed, a jolly little clown came walking toward them, and Dorothy could see that in spite of his pretty clothes of red and yellow and green he was completely covered with cracks, running every which way and showing plainly that he had been mended in many places.
paragraphs.cn: 果然，一个开心的小丑向他们走来。多萝西看到，尽管他穿着红黄绿相间的漂亮衣服，但全身都是裂缝，裂缝到处都是，很明显他被修补过很多次。

paragraphs.en: The Clown put his hands in his pockets, and after puffing out his cheeks and nodding his head at them saucily, he said:
paragraphs.cn: 小丑把手插进口袋里，鼓起脸颊，顽皮地对他们点点头，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “My lady fair, Why do you stare At poor old Mr. Joker?
paragraphs.cn: “美丽的女士，你为什么盯着可怜的小丑先生看？

paragraphs.en: You’re quite as stiff And prim as if You’d eaten up a poker!”
paragraphs.cn: 你是不是吃了个火钳，怎么呆呆的，这么严肃！”

paragraphs.en: “Be quiet, sir!” said the Princess. “Can’t you see these are strangers, and should be treated with respect?”
paragraphs.cn: “安静点，先生！”公主说，“难道你没看到这些是陌生人吗？我们应该尊重他们。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s respect, I expect,” declared the Clown, and immediately stood upon his head.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我想这就是尊重吧，”小丑说，然后立刻倒立了起来。

paragraphs.en: “Don’t mind Mr. Joker,” said the Princess to Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “别理小丑先生。”公主对多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “He is considerably cracked in his head, and that makes him foolish.”
paragraphs.cn: “他脑袋里裂缝太多了，所以有点傻。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I don’t mind him a bit,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “噢，我一点也不介意他。”多萝西说。

paragraphs.en: “But you are so beautiful,” she continued, “that I am sure I could love you dearly.
paragraphs.cn: “但是你太漂亮了，”她继续说，“我肯定会非常非常喜欢你的。

paragraphs.en: Won’t you let me carry you back to Kansas, and stand you on Aunt Em’s mantel?
paragraphs.cn: 你愿不愿意让我把你带回堪萨斯，然后把你放在艾姆婶婶的壁炉架上？

paragraphs.en: I could carry you in my basket.”
paragraphs.cn: 我可以用我的篮子把你装走。”

paragraphs.en: “That would make me very unhappy,” answered the china Princess.
paragraphs.cn: “那会让我很不开心。”瓷器公主回答。

paragraphs.en: “You see, here in our country we live contentedly, and can talk and move around as we please.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，在我们这个国家，我们过得很开心，可以随便说话和走动。

paragraphs.en: But whenever any of us are taken away our joints at once stiffen, and we can only stand straight and look pretty.
paragraphs.cn: 但只要我们中的任何一个被带走，我们的关节就会立刻变硬，只能直直地站着，看起来漂亮而已。

paragraphs.en: Of course that is all that is expected of us when we are on mantels and cabinets and drawing-room tables, but our lives are much pleasanter here in our own country.”
paragraphs.cn: 当然啦，当我们被放在壁炉架、柜子和客厅桌上时，大家也只希望我们这样。但在这里，我们自己的国家，生活要快乐得多。”

paragraphs.en: “I would not make you unhappy for all the world!” exclaimed Dorothy. “So I’ll just say good-bye.”
paragraphs.cn: “我才不愿意让你不开心呢！”多萝西大声说，“那我只好说再见了。”

paragraphs.en: “Good-bye,” replied the Princess.
paragraphs.cn: “再见。”公主回答。

paragraphs.en: They walked carefully through the china country.
paragraphs.cn: 他们小心翼翼地穿过瓷器国家。

paragraphs.en: The little animals and all the people scampered out of their way, fearing the strangers would break them, and after an hour or so the travelers reached the other side of the country and came to another china wall.
paragraphs.cn: 小动物们和所有的人都跑开了，生怕陌生人会把他们弄碎。过了一个多小时，旅行者们到达了这个国家的另一边，看到了一堵新的瓷器墙。

paragraphs.en: It was not so high as the first, however, and by standing upon the Lion’s back they all managed to scramble to the top.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，这堵墙没有第一堵那么高。他们站在狮子的背上，都爬到了墙顶。

paragraphs.en: Then the Lion gathered his legs under him and jumped on the wall; but just as he jumped, he upset a china church with his tail and smashed it all to pieces.
paragraphs.cn: 然后狮子把腿收起来，跳到墙上；但他刚跳上去，就用尾巴撞倒了一座瓷器教堂，把它全都摔碎了。

paragraphs.en: “That was too bad,” said Dorothy, “but really I think we were lucky in not doing these little people more harm than breaking a cow’s leg and a church.
paragraphs.cn: “真不好呀，” 多萝西 说，“不过我们很幸运，没给这些小人儿带来更多麻烦，只弄断了一头牛的腿和一座教堂。”

paragraphs.en: They are all so brittle!”
paragraphs.cn: 他们都好脆呀！”

paragraphs.en: “They are, indeed,” said the Scarecrow, “and I am thankful I am made of straw and cannot be easily damaged.
paragraphs.cn: “他们确实是，” 稻草人 说，“我很开心我是稻草做的，不容易坏掉。

paragraphs.en: There are worse things in the world than being a Scarecrow.”
paragraphs.cn: 世界上还有比当个 稻草人 更糟糕的事呢。”

chapters.title_en: The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts

paragraphs.en: After climbing down from the china wall the travelers found themselves in a disagreeable country, full of bogs and marshes and covered with tall, rank grass.
paragraphs.cn: 从瓷墙上爬下来后，他们来到一个不舒服的地方，那里有好多泥沼和湿地，长满了高高的野草。

paragraphs.en: It was difficult to walk without falling into muddy holes, for the grass was so thick that it hid them from sight.
paragraphs.cn: 走路很不容易，不小心就会掉进泥坑里，因为草太厚了，把坑都藏起来了。

paragraphs.en: However, by carefully picking their way, they got safely along until they reached solid ground.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他们小心地选路走，终于安全地来到了一块结实的地面。

paragraphs.en: But here the country seemed wilder than ever, and after a long and tiresome walk through the underbrush they entered another forest, where the trees were bigger and older than any they had ever seen.
paragraphs.cn: 但这里比以前更荒凉了，走了很久很久，穿过矮树丛，他们又进了一片森林，那里的树比他们见过的所有树都大，都老。

paragraphs.en: “This forest is perfectly delightful,” declared the Lion, looking around him with joy.
paragraphs.cn: “这片森林真是太棒了！” 狮子 开心地看着四周说。

paragraphs.en: “Never have I seen a more beautiful place.”
paragraphs.cn: “我从没见过这么美的地方。”

paragraphs.en: “It seems gloomy,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “这里看起来有点暗，” 稻草人 说。

paragraphs.en: “Not a bit of it,” answered the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “一点也不啊！” 狮子 回答说。

paragraphs.en: “I should like to live here all my life.
paragraphs.cn: “我真想一辈子住在这里呢。

paragraphs.en: See how soft the dried leaves are under your feet and how rich and green the moss is that clings to these old trees.
paragraphs.cn: 看，你脚下的干树叶多软啊，这些老树上的苔藓多绿多好看啊。

paragraphs.en: Surely no wild beast could wish a pleasanter home.”
paragraphs.cn: 肯定没有野兽会不喜欢这里，不想住在这里吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Perhaps there are wild beasts in the forest now,” said Dorothy.
paragraphs.cn: “也许森林里现在有野兽呢，” 多萝西 说。

paragraphs.en: “I suppose there are,” returned the Lion, “but I do not see any of them about.”
paragraphs.cn: “我想是有的，” 狮子 回答，“但我没看到它们呀。”

paragraphs.en: They walked through the forest until it became too dark to go any farther.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一直走啊走，穿过森林，直到天黑得不能再走了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy and Toto and the Lion lay down to sleep, while the Woodman and the Scarecrow kept watch over them as usual.
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西、托托 和 狮子 躺下睡觉，而 铁皮人 和 稻草人 像以前一样，帮他们看守着。

paragraphs.en: When morning came, they started again.
paragraphs.cn: 天亮了，他们又出发了。

paragraphs.en: Before they had gone far they heard a low rumble, as of the growling of many wild animals.
paragraphs.cn: 他们没走多远，就听到一阵低沉的轰隆声，好像是好多野兽在吼叫。

paragraphs.en: Toto whimpered a little, but none of the others was frightened, and they kept along the well-trodden path until they came to an opening in the wood, in which were gathered hundreds of beasts of every variety.
paragraphs.cn: 托托 小声哼哼了几下，但其他人都没有害怕。他们沿着小路一直走，来到一片空地，那里聚了几百只各种各样的野兽。

paragraphs.en: There were tigers and elephants and bears and wolves and foxes and all the others in the natural history, and for a moment Dorothy was afraid.
paragraphs.cn: 那里有老虎、大象、熊、狼、狐狸，还有好多好多动物。那一刻，多萝西 害怕了。

paragraphs.en: But the Lion explained that the animals were holding a meeting, and he judged by their snarling and growling that they were in great trouble.
paragraphs.cn: 但 狮子 告诉大家，动物们正在开会。他从它们的吼叫声听出来，它们遇到了大麻烦。

paragraphs.en: As he spoke several of the beasts caught sight of him, and at once the great assemblage hushed as if by magic.
paragraphs.cn: 他说话的时候，有几只野兽看到了他，一下子，所有的动物都像变魔术一样，安静下来了。

paragraphs.en: The biggest of the tigers came up to the Lion and bowed, saying:
paragraphs.cn: 最大的一只老虎走到 狮子 面前，弯了弯腰，说：

paragraphs.en: “Welcome, O King of Beasts!
paragraphs.cn: “欢迎您，动物之王！

paragraphs.en: You have come in good time to fight our enemy and bring peace to all the animals of the forest once more.”
paragraphs.cn: 您来得真及时，快来帮我们打败敌人，让森林里的动物们重新过上平静的日子吧。”

paragraphs.en: “What is your trouble?” asked the Lion quietly.
paragraphs.cn: “你们有什么麻烦呀？” 狮子 轻轻地问。

paragraphs.en: “We are all threatened,” answered the tiger, “by a fierce enemy which has lately come into this forest.
paragraphs.cn: “我们都遇到了危险，”老虎回答，“一个很凶的敌人最近来到了这片森林，威胁着我们所有人。

paragraphs.en: It is a most tremendous monster, like a great spider, with a body as big as an elephant and legs as long as a tree trunk.
paragraphs.cn: 它是个巨大的怪物，像个大蜘蛛。它的身体像大象一样大，腿像树干一样长。

paragraphs.en: It has eight of these long legs, and as the monster crawls through the forest he seizes an animal with a leg and drags it to his mouth, where he eats it as a spider does a fly.
paragraphs.cn: 它有八条长长的腿。怪物在森林里爬的时候，会用一条腿抓住动物，拖到嘴边，像蜘蛛吃苍蝇一样把它们吃掉。

paragraphs.en: Not one of us is safe while this fierce creature is alive, and we had called a meeting to decide how to take care of ourselves when you came among us.”
paragraphs.cn: 只要这个凶猛的怪物还活着，我们谁都不安全。你来的时候，我们正在开会，讨论怎么保护自己呢。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion thought for a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子想了想。

paragraphs.en: “Are there any other lions in this forest?” he asked.
paragraphs.cn: “这片森林里还有别的狮子吗？”他问。

paragraphs.en: “No; there were some, but the monster has eaten them all.
paragraphs.cn: “没有；以前是有些，但都被怪物吃光了。

paragraphs.en: And, besides, they were none of them nearly so large and brave as you.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，它们都没你这么大，也没你这么勇敢。”

paragraphs.en: “If I put an end to your enemy, will you bow down to me and obey me as King of the Forest?” inquired the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “如果我帮你们除掉这个敌人，你们会向我低头，听我的话，把我当成森林之王吗？”狮子问。

paragraphs.en: “We will do that gladly,” returned the tiger; and all the other beasts roared with a mighty roar: “We will!”
paragraphs.cn: “我们很乐意这么做！”老虎回答。所有其他动物都大声吼道：“我们愿意！”

paragraphs.en: “Where is this great spider of yours now?” asked the Lion.
paragraphs.cn: “你们说的这个大蜘蛛现在在哪里？”狮子问。

paragraphs.en: “Yonder, among the oak trees,” said the tiger, pointing with his forefoot.
paragraphs.cn: “就在那边，橡树林里。”老虎用前爪指着说。

paragraphs.en: “Take good care of these friends of mine,” said the Lion, “and I will go at once to fight the monster.”
paragraphs.cn: “你们好好照顾我的这些朋友，”狮子说，“我这就去跟怪物打架。”

paragraphs.en: He bade his comrades good-bye and marched proudly away to do battle with the enemy.
paragraphs.cn: 他跟伙伴们告别，骄傲地走开了，要去跟敌人打架。

paragraphs.en: The great spider was lying asleep when the Lion found him, and it looked so ugly that its foe turned up his nose in disgust.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子找到大蜘蛛的时候，它正在睡觉。大蜘蛛长得太丑了，敌人看了都厌恶地皱起了鼻子。

paragraphs.en: Its legs were quite as long as the tiger had said, and its body covered with coarse black hair.
paragraphs.cn: 它的腿真的像老虎说的那样长，身体上长满了粗粗的黑毛。

paragraphs.en: It had a great mouth, with a row of sharp teeth a foot long; but its head was joined to the pudgy body by a neck as slender as a wasp’s waist.
paragraphs.cn: 它有个大大的嘴巴，里面有一排一尺长的尖牙。但它的头和胖胖的身体之间，脖子细得像黄蜂的腰。

paragraphs.en: This gave the Lion a hint of the best way to attack the creature, and as he knew it was easier to fight it asleep than awake, he gave a great spring and landed directly upon the monster’s back.
paragraphs.cn: 这让狮子知道了攻击它的最好办法。他知道趁它睡觉的时候打更容易，于是猛地一跳，直接跳到怪物的背上。

paragraphs.en: Then, with one blow of his heavy paw, all armed with sharp claws, he knocked the spider’s head from its body.
paragraphs.cn: 他用带着锋利指甲的沉重爪子一拍，就把蜘蛛的头从身体上打掉了。

paragraphs.en: Jumping down, he watched it until the long legs stopped wiggling, when he knew it was quite dead.
paragraphs.cn: 他跳下来，看着它，直到它的长腿不再动了，这才知道它真的死了。

paragraphs.en: The Lion went back to the opening where the beasts of the forest were waiting for him and said proudly:
paragraphs.cn: 狮子回到了空地上，森林里的动物们正在那里等他，他骄傲地说：

paragraphs.en: “You need fear your enemy no longer.”
paragraphs.cn: “你们再也不用害怕敌人了。”

paragraphs.en: Then the beasts bowed down to the Lion as their King, and he promised to come back and rule over them as soon as Dorothy was safely on her way to Kansas.
paragraphs.cn: 动物们向狮子低头，把他当成了它们的国王。他答应等多萝西安全地去往堪萨斯后，就回来统治它们。

paragraphs.en: The four travelers passed through the rest of the forest in safety, and when they came out from its gloom saw before them a steep hill, covered from top to bottom with great pieces of rock.
paragraphs.cn: 四个旅行者安全地走出了森林。当他们走出阴暗的森林时，看到前面有一座陡峭的山，山上从头到脚都是大块大块的石头。

paragraphs.en: “That will be a hard climb,” said the Scarecrow, “but we must get over the hill, nevertheless.”
paragraphs.cn: “那会很难爬，”稻草人说，“但我们还是得翻过这座山。”

paragraphs.en: So he led the way and the others followed.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他带头，其他人跟着。

paragraphs.en: They had nearly reached the first rock when they heard a rough voice cry out, “Keep back!”
paragraphs.cn: 他们快走到第一块大石头那里时，听到一个粗鲁的声音喊道：“别过来！”

paragraphs.en: “Who are you?” asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “你们是谁？”稻草人问。

paragraphs.en: Then a head showed itself over the rock and the same voice said, “This hill belongs to us, and we don’t allow anyone to cross it.”
paragraphs.cn: 然后，一个脑袋从石头后面露出来，那个声音又说：“这座山是我们的，我们不让任何人过。”

paragraphs.en: “But we must cross it,” said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.cn: “但我们必须过去。”稻草人说。

paragraphs.en: “We’re going to the country of the Quadlings.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们要去奎德林人的国家。”

paragraphs.en: “But you shall not!” replied the voice, and there stepped from behind the rock the strangest man the travelers had ever seen.
paragraphs.cn: “不行！”那个声音说，一个奇怪的男人从石头后面走了出来，旅行者们从没见过他这么奇怪的人。

paragraphs.en: He was quite short and stout and had a big head, which was flat at the top and supported by a thick neck full of wrinkles.
paragraphs.cn: 他很矮很胖，头大大的，头顶平平的，粗粗的脖子上有好多皱纹。

paragraphs.en: But he had no arms at all, and, seeing this, the Scarecrow did not fear that so helpless a creature could prevent them from climbing the hill.
paragraphs.cn: 可是他一点胳膊都没有！看到这，稻草人觉得这个没有胳膊的人帮不了什么忙，所以不怕他阻止自己爬山。

paragraphs.en: So he said, “I’m sorry not to do as you wish, but we must pass over your hill whether you like it or not,” and he walked boldly forward.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他说：“不好意思，我们不能听你的，不管你喜不喜欢，我们都得过这座山。”他大胆地往前走。

paragraphs.en: As quick as lightning the man’s head shot forward and his neck stretched out until the top of the head, where it was flat, struck the Scarecrow in the middle and sent him tumbling, over and over, down the hill.
paragraphs.cn: 像闪电一样快，那个人的头往前一冲，脖子伸得好长，他平平的头顶正好打在稻草人的身上，把稻草人撞得咕噜噜地滚下了山。

paragraphs.en: Almost as quickly as it came the head went back to the body, and the man laughed harshly as he said, “It isn’t as easy as you think!”
paragraphs.cn: 他的头几乎一下子就缩了回去，那个人大声地笑着说：“这可不像你想的那么容易！”

paragraphs.en: A chorus of boisterous laughter came from the other rocks, and Dorothy saw hundreds of the armless Hammer-Heads upon the hillside, one behind every rock.
paragraphs.cn: 其他石头后面传来了一阵大大的笑声，多萝西看到山坡上好多没有胳膊的锤头人，每块石头后面都藏着一个。

paragraphs.en: The Lion became quite angry at the laughter caused by the Scarecrow’s mishap, and giving a loud roar that echoed like thunder, he dashed up the hill.
paragraphs.cn: 狮子看到稻草人摔倒了，大家还在笑，他很生气。他大吼一声，声音像打雷一样响，然后冲上了山。

paragraphs.en: Again a head shot swiftly out, and the great Lion went rolling down the hill as if he had been struck by a cannon ball.
paragraphs.cn: 又一个头迅速地冲了出来，大大的狮子像被大炮弹打中一样，咕噜噜地滚下了山。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy ran down and helped the Scarecrow to his feet, and the Lion came up to her, feeling rather bruised and sore, and said, “It is useless to fight people with shooting heads; no one can withstand them.”
paragraphs.cn: 多萝西跑下去扶起稻草人，狮子走到她身边，感觉自己又青又痛，说：“和这些会伸头打人的家伙打架没用，谁也打不过他们。”

paragraphs.en: “What can we do, then?” she asked.
paragraphs.cn: “那我们该怎么办呢？”她问。

paragraphs.en: “Call the Winged Monkeys,” suggested the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.cn: “叫飞猴来。”铁皮人说。

paragraphs.en: “You have still the right to command them once more.”
paragraphs.cn: “你还可以再命令他们一次。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well,” she answered, and putting on the Golden Cap she uttered the magic words.
paragraphs.cn: “好的。”她回答，然后戴上金冠，念出了神奇的咒语。

paragraphs.en: The Monkeys were as prompt as ever, and in a few moments the entire band stood before her.
paragraphs.cn: 猴子们像以前一样，很快就来了，不一会儿，所有的猴子都站在了她面前。

paragraphs.en: “What are your commands?” inquired the King of the Monkeys, bowing low.
paragraphs.cn: “您有什么吩咐？”猴王弯下腰，恭敬地问。

paragraphs.en: “Carry us over the hill to the country of the Quadlings,” answered the girl.
paragraphs.cn: “带我们翻过这座山，去奎德林人的国家。”女孩回答说。

paragraphs.en: “It shall be done,” said the King, and at once the Winged Monkeys caught the four travelers and Toto up in their arms and flew away with them.
paragraphs.cn: “没问题。”猴王说。飞猴马上就把四个旅行者和托托抱起来，带着他们飞走了。

paragraphs.en: As they passed over the hill the Hammer-Heads yelled with vexation, and shot their heads high in the air, but they could not reach the Winged Monkeys, which carried Dorothy and her comrades safely over the hill and set them down in the beautiful country of the Quadlings.
paragraphs.cn: 当他们飞过山的时候，锤头人气得大叫，把头高高地伸向空中，可是他们还是够不着飞猴。飞猴安全地带着多萝西和她的朋友们飞过了山，把他们轻轻地放在了美丽的奎德林人国家。

paragraphs.en: “This is the last time you can summon us,” said the leader to Dorothy; “so good-bye and good luck to you.”
paragraphs.cn: “这是你最后一次叫我们了。”领队对多萝西说，“再见啦，祝你好运！”

paragraphs.en: “Good-bye, and thank you very much,” returned the girl; and the Monkeys rose into the air and were out of sight in a twinkling.
